parts: Give me some ideas for interesting interactive and visual things ChatGPT can do.

# GPT-6 with Intelligent UI

ChatGPT can now create interactive experiences directly in a conversation, including adjustable diagrams, step-by-step explorations, and visual tools that respond to your choices.

Here are four examples to try.

<grid columns="lg">
  <grid-item>
    <box radius="2xl" clip>
      <AsyncImage query="professional editorial food photography lemon spinach pasta in handmade ivory ceramic bowl fresh lemon zest parmesan natural warm window light" alt="Lemon-and-spinach pasta in a ceramic serving dish" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%" fit="cover" radius="none" frame={false}/>
    </box>
    <title>Easy pasta recipe</title>
    <text size="sm" color="secondary">Make lemon-and-spinach pasta with a checklist and quantities that scale for 2 or 4.</text>
    <spacer/>
    <button block onClick={() => GenUI.issueNewTurn("Show me how to make quick lemon-and-spinach pasta for dinner. Let me check off ingredients and switch between cooking for two or four.")}>Try it</button>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box radius="2xl" clip>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" width="100%">
        <defs>
          <radialGradient id="starbirth">
            <stop offset="0" stopColor="#E2E6FF"/>
            <stop offset=".26" stopColor="#A0A6D9"/>
            <stop offset=".65" stopColor="#7B4BB1" stopOpacity=".45"/>
            <stop offset="1" stopColor="#593BB6" stopOpacity="0"/>
          </radialGradient>
          <radialGradient id="starbright">
            <stop offset="0" stopColor="#FFFBE4"/>
            <stop offset=".55" stopColor="#FFE9A3"/>
            <stop offset="1" stopColor="#EEA344"/>
          </radialGradient>
          <radialGradient id="stargiant">
            <stop offset="0" stopColor="#FFE19B"/>
            <stop offset=".65" stopColor="#F18E48"/>
            <stop offset="1" stopColor="#BA412D"/>
          </radialGradient>
          <radialGradient id="stardwarf">
            <stop offset="0" stopColor="#FFFFFF"/>
            <stop offset=".6" stopColor="#C6E9FF"/>
            <stop offset="1" stopColor="#729FD5"/>
          </radialGradient>
        </defs>
        <rect width="320" height="180" fill="#101828"/>
        {#each [[17,23,1],[52,36,.7],[85,17,.8],[138,29,1],[171,14,.6],[248,27,1],[292,31,.7],[24,108,.7],[70,118,.6],[143,105,.6],[261,128,.7],[305,117,.7],[161,56,.8],[232,98,.5]] as s,i}
          <circle key={i} cx={s[0]} cy={s[1]} r={s[2]} fill="#CBD5E1" opacity=".65"/>
        {/each}
        <path d="M70 83H93 M148 83H164 M235 83H265" stroke="#64748B" strokeWidth="1" strokeDasharray="2 4"/>
        <circle cx="43" cy="82" r="31" fill="url(#starbirth)"/>
        <circle cx="43" cy="82" r="5" fill="#E2DAFF"/>
        <circle cx="122" cy="82" r="21" fill="#EBA83A" opacity=".12"/>
        <circle cx="122" cy="82" r="16" fill="url(#starbright)"/>
        <circle cx="201" cy="82" r="32" fill="#E27341" opacity=".12"/>
        <circle cx="201" cy="82" r="27" fill="url(#stargiant)"/>
        <circle cx="283" cy="82" r="15" fill="#A2CFFA" opacity=".12"/>
        <circle cx="283" cy="82" r="9" fill="url(#stardwarf)"/>
        <g fill="#DCE4F1" fontSize="10" textAnchor="middle">
          <text x="43" y="143">Birth</text>
          <text x="122" y="143">Stable</text>
          <text x="201" y="143">Red giant</text>
          <text x="283" y="143">Remnant</text>
        </g>
        <text x="16" y="20" fill="#8192B0" fontSize="8" letterSpacing="1.5">STELLAR EVOLUTION</text>
      </svg>
    </box>
    <title>The life of a star</title>
    <text size="sm" color="secondary">Step through a star’s life with simple diagrams and clear explanations.</text>
    <spacer/>
    <button block onClick={() => GenUI.issueNewTurn("Explain to me the lifecycle of a main sequence star. Give me options to step through the key stages and clear explanations on each step.")}>Try it</button>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box radius="2xl" clip>
      <svg viewBox="0 0 320 180" width="100%">
        <rect width="320" height="180" fill="#256B45"/>
        <path d="M0 45H320 M0 90H320 M0 135H320" stroke="#398259" strokeWidth="45" opacity=".34"/>
        <g fill="none" stroke="#E2F0DB" strokeWidth="1.4" opacity=".85">
          <rect x="9" y="12" width="302" height="156" rx="1"/>
          <path d="M30 12V168 M311 48H261V132H311 M311 64H289V116H311"/>
          <path d="M261 71A19 19 0 0 0 261 109"/>
          <path d="M30 56A34 34 0 0 1 30 124"/>
        </g>
        <rect x="311" y="72" width="7" height="36" fill="none" stroke="#FFFFFF" strokeWidth="2.5"/>
        <line x1="228" y1="12" x2="228" y2="168" stroke="#FFE9A4" strokeWidth="1.8" strokeDasharray="5 4"/>
        <g fontSize="9" fill="#E7F4E9">
          <text x="14" y="27">PASS</text>
          <text x="235" y="23" fill="#FFE9A4">Offside line</text>
        </g>
        <path d="M100 118Q151 77 216 61" fill="none" stroke="#FFFFFF" strokeDasharray="4 4" strokeWidth="1.5" opacity=".9"/>
        <path d="M211 59L217 60L214 66" fill="none" stroke="white" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
        <g>
          <circle cx="97" cy="121" r="10" fill="#D5EBFF" opacity=".2"/>
          <circle cx="97" cy="121" r="7" fill="#2678D4" stroke="#D8EDFF" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
          <circle cx="216" cy="60" r="11" fill="#D5EBFF" opacity=".2"/>
          <circle cx="216" cy="60" r="7" fill="#2678D4" stroke="#D8EDFF" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
          <circle cx="228" cy="112" r="8" fill="#E96755" stroke="#FFE5DE" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
          <circle cx="296" cy="89" r="8" fill="#F2B84A" stroke="#FFF0C9" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
          <circle cx="109" cy="128" r="4" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
          <path d="M107 127L110 125L112 129L109 131Z" fill="#263647"/>
        </g>
        <g fill="#F0F7F0" fontSize="9">
          <text x="183" y="43">Receiver</text>
          <text x="202" y="134">Defender</text>
          <text x="270" y="111">GK</text>
        </g>
      </svg>
    </box>
    <title>Offside explained</title>
    <text size="sm" color="secondary">Move a receiver at the moment of a pass to see what makes a position onside or offside.</text>
    <spacer/>
    <button block onClick={() => GenUI.issueNewTurn("Help me understand the offside rule. Let me drag the player receiving the pass to see when they’re onside or offside.")}>Try it</button>
  </grid-item>
  <grid-item>
    <box radius="2xl" clip>
      <AsyncImage query="historic beautiful library interior grand symmetrical reading room ornate carved wooden bookshelves long tables warm brass lamps dramatic vanishing point architectural editorial photography" alt="The interior of a historic library" aspectRatio="16:9" width="100%" fit="cover" radius="none" frame={false}/>
    </box>
    <title>Beautiful library exploration</title>
    <text size="sm" color="secondary">Explore six beautiful libraries, one photograph and two surprising facts at a time.</text>
    <spacer/>
    <button block onClick={() => GenUI.issueNewTurn("Explain and help me learn about six of the most beautiful famous libraries in the world. Let me explore each library step by step, with a real photograph and two surprising facts for each.")}>Try it</button>
  </grid-item>
</grid>

    """Intersection volume of equal 3-balls, vectorized."""
    x = np.asarray(rho, dtype=float)

    """Half-length on which rho(s)<2R; the endpoint contributes zero."""
    if D >= 2.0 * radius:

    if q == 0.0:
        return T
    root = ((4.0 * radius * radius - D * D) / (q * q)) ** 0.25
    return min(T, root)

---
name: pdfs
description: Reliable, workflow-driven PDF processing: render → verify → operate → re-render/verify, covering reading, inspection, extraction, editing, forms, OCR, redaction, conversion, and diffing. Prefer authoring in DOCX or PPTX (then converting to PDF) for text-heavy docs or slide-like layouts; use ReportLab here for programmatic PDF generation.
---

# PDF Skill (Read • Inspect • Extract • Edit • Render • Forms • OCR • Redact • Convert • Diff)

This skill is designed for **reliable, workflow-driven** PDF work: **render -> verify -> operate -> re-render verify**.

## Before you touch PDFs: should this be DOCX/PPTX instead?

Even if the user asks for a PDF deliverable, the best workflow is often:

- **Text-heavy, business-doc layout (headings, TOC, long tables, rich lists)** -> use the **DOCX skill** to author, then convert to PDF with `lo_convert_to_pdf.py`.
- **Slide-like visual layout (charts, callouts, fixed positioning, figure captions)** -> use the **Slides skill** (PPTX) to author, then export to PDF.
- **Programmatic generation** -> ReportLab (this skill) is fine.

If you find yourself hand-tuning line breaks or typography in ReportLab, you probably picked the wrong authoring format.

---

## Core loop (always)

1) Render to images

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/render_pdf.py input.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_renders/in --dpi 200
```

2) Inspect PNGs (tables/figures/layout are authoritative)

3) Perform the edit/extract/create

4) Re-render and compare

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/compare_renders.py before.pdf after.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_diff --dpi 200
```

---

## Task index (progressive)

Start with the smallest task that answers the user:

### Read / review
- `tasks/read_review.md`

### Extract (text/layout/tables/images/attachments/forms)
- `tasks/extract.md`
- `tasks/coords.md` (coordinate sanity)

### Edit (merge/split/rotate/crop/watermark/paginate/encrypt/repair)
- `tasks/edit.md`
- `tasks/compare.md` (visual regression)

### Forms
- Fillable forms: `tasks/forms_annotations.md`
- Debugging/introspection: `tasks/forms_debugging.md`
- Non-fillable / stamping workflow: `tasks/forms_nonfillable.md`

### OCR
- `tasks/ocr.md`

### Preflight / normalize
- `tasks/preflight.md`

### Redaction
- `tasks/redact.md`

### Renderer parity
- `tasks/parity.md`

### Batch processing
- `tasks/batch.md`

### Create / convert
- `tasks/create.md`
- `tasks/convert.md`
- `tasks/js_tools.md` (pdf-lib, pdfjs)


---

## Package map (where things live)

This pack includes a `manifest.txt` that is a **pure list of relative file paths** used by download tooling.

Quick map:

- **tasks/** (what to do)
  - `read_review.md` - render-first reading/review
  - `extract.md` - extract text/layout/tables/images/attachments/forms
  - `coords.md` - coordinate system cheatsheet (PDF pt vs image px)
  - `edit.md` - merge/split/select/rotate/crop/watermark/paginate/encrypt/repair
  - `compare.md` - visual diff workflow
  - `forms_annotations.md` - fillable forms + appearance pitfalls + correctness checklist
  - `forms_debugging.md` - widget-level introspection + acceptable values
  - `forms_nonfillable.md` - stamp-by-boxes workflow for non-fillable forms
  - `ocr.md` - OCR scanned PDFs to searchable
  - `preflight.md` - quick triage + normalization guidance
  - `redact.md` - true redaction workflows
  - `parity.md` - render parity across engines
  - `batch.md` - batch helpers for corpora
  - `create.md` - choose reportlab/latex/html/docx/pptx pipeline
  - `convert.md` - docx/pptx/html/markdown/latex to PDF conversion
  - `js_tools.md` - pdf-lib/pdfjs helper CLIs

- **scripts/** (run these)
  - `render_pdf.py` - render to PNGs (pdfium or poppler)
  - `compare_renders.py` - render-and-diff two PDFs (pixel diff)
  - `pdf_inspect.py` - metadata/structure overview
  - `pdf_extract.py` - text/words/chars/tables/images/attachments/annots/forms
  - `pdf_edit.py` - editing toolkit (merge/split/select/rotate/crop/watermark/paginate/encrypt/repair/optimize)
  - `pdf_preflight.py` - preflight/triage warnings
  - `pdf_redact.py` - true redaction (remove underlying content)
  - `renderer_parity.py` - diff pdftoppm vs pdfium renders
  - `batch_pdf.py` - batch runner for common ops
  - `box_picker_html.py` - generate interactive HTML to pick rectangles -> JSON in PDF coords
  - `place_text_by_boxes.py` - stamp text/checkmarks into rectangles (non-fillable forms)
  - `ocr_pdf.py` - OCR wrapper
  - `html_to_pdf.py`, `md_to_pdf.py`, `latex_to_pdf.py`, `lo_convert_to_pdf.py` - conversion helpers

- **js/** (Node helpers)
  - `install_deps.sh` - installs pdf-lib + pdfjs-dist
  - `fill_form.mjs` - fill + optional flatten (supports flags and positional args)
  - `extract_form_fields.mjs` - list AcroForm fields
  - `extract_text_pdfjs.mjs` - extract text via pdfjs-dist

- **examples/**
  - `smoke_test.md` - runnable smoke flows

- **troubleshooting/**
  - `common.md` - common pitfalls and fixes

---

## Final deliverable expectations

- No clipped text, overlaps, black squares, or broken glyphs in rendered PNGs.
- Verify in at least **one** renderer (`pdfium` or `pdftoppm`). For tricky forms, verify in **two**.
- Remove intermediate artifacts from the deliverable folder (keep only final PDF(s)).
- Avoid Unicode dashes that some renderers mishandle; prefer ASCII `-`.

The material you've uploaded suggests something much more interesting than a collection of physics illustrations: **an interactive SAT/H(s)H geometry laboratory.**

We can make the mathematics directly manipulable, showing how four-dimensional structures produce observable intersections, how helices and worldtubes relate, and how changing geometric parameters affects calculated quantities.

There are also important historical layers in these documents. The early SAT formulations, contemporary H(s)H worldtube constructions, and experimental mathematical fixtures should remain distinguishable. That lets us illustrate the development of the framework without accidentally presenting conjectural mechanisms as established results.

Let's start with two working exhibits.

{@module
const filamentPoint = (w,u,a,k) => ({x:u*w+a*Math.cos(k*w),y:a*Math.sin(k*w)});
const filamentTrace = (u,a,k,mode) => {
  const out=[];
  for(let i=0;i<=240;i++){
    const w=-4.4+8.8*i/240;
    const p=filamentPoint(w,u,a,k);
    const x=160+43*p.x;
    const y=mode==="block"?120-23*w:119-43*p.y;
    out.push((i===0?"M":"L")+x.toFixed(3)+" "+y.toFixed(3));
  }
  return out.join(" ");
};
const lensVol = (d,R=1.2) => d>=2*R?0:Math.PI*(4*R+d)*(2*R-d)**2/12;
const contactCalc=(D,q)=>{
  const R=1.2,T=1,N=256;
  if(D>=2*R)return {E:0,F:0,h:0};
  const h=q===0?T:Math.min(T,Math.pow((4*R*R-D*D)/(q*q),.25));
  let es=0,fs=0;
  const step=h/N;
  for(let i=0;i<=N;i++){
    const s=i*step;
    const rho=Math.sqrt(D*D+q*q*s**4);
    const w=(i===0||i===N)?1:(i%2===0?2:4);
    const E=lensVol(rho,R);
    const F=rho<2*R?(Math.PI/4)*(4*R*R-rho*rho)*D/rho:0;
    es+=w*E;fs+=w*F;
  }
  return {E:2*step*es/3,F:2*step*fs/3,h};
};
const overlapProfile = (D,q) => {
  const v0=lensVol(D);
  let path="M 24 236";
  for(let i=0;i<=160;i++){
    const s=-1+2*i/160;
    const d=Math.sqrt(D*D+q*q*s**4);
    const f=v0>0?lensVol(d)/v0:0;
    path+=" L "+(24+272*i/160).toFixed(2)+" "+(236-42*f).toFixed(2);
  }
  return path+" L 296 236 Z";
};
}

Moving the control changes the intersection, not the block geometry itself. The finite-core toggle adds a schematic envelope, not an assumed fundamental filament thickness.

# PDF Skill (Read • Inspect • Extract • Edit • Render • Forms • OCR • Redact • Convert • Diff)

This skill is designed for **reliable, workflow-driven** PDF work: **render -> verify -> operate -> re-render verify**.

## Before you touch PDFs: should this be DOCX/PPTX instead?

Even if the user asks for a PDF deliverable, the best workflow is often:

- **Text-heavy, business-doc layout (headings, TOC, long tables, rich lists)** -> use the **DOCX skill** to author, then convert to PDF with `lo_convert_to_pdf.py`.
- **Slide-like visual layout (charts, callouts, fixed positioning, figure captions)** -> use the **Slides skill** (PPTX) to author, then export to PDF.
- **Programmatic generation** -> ReportLab (this skill) is fine.

If you find yourself hand-tuning line breaks or typography in ReportLab, you probably picked the wrong authoring format.

---

## Core loop (always)

1) Render to images

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/render_pdf.py input.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_renders/in --dpi 200
```

2) Inspect PNGs (tables/figures/layout are authoritative)

3) Perform the edit/extract/create

4) Re-render and compare

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/compare_renders.py before.pdf after.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_diff --dpi 200
```

---

## Task index (progressive)

Start with the smallest task that answers the user:

### Read / review
- `tasks/read_review.md`

### Extract (text/layout/tables/images/attachments/forms)
- `tasks/extract.md`
- `tasks/coords.md` (coordinate sanity)

### Edit (merge/split/rotate/crop/watermark/paginate/encrypt/repair)
- `tasks/edit.md`
- `tasks/compare.md` (visual regression)

### Forms
- Fillable forms: `tasks/forms_annotations.md`
- Debugging/introspection: `tasks/forms_debugging.md`
- Non-fillable / stamping workflow: `tasks/forms_nonfillable.md`

### OCR
- `tasks/ocr.md`

### Preflight / normalize
- `tasks/preflight.md`

### Redaction
- `tasks/redact.md`

### Renderer parity
- `tasks/parity.md`

### Batch processing
- `tasks/batch.md`

### Create / convert
- `tasks/create.md`
- `tasks/convert.md`
- `tasks/js_tools.md` (pdf-lib, pdfjs)


---

## Package map (where things live)

This pack includes a `manifest.txt` that is a **pure list of relative file paths** used by download tooling.

Quick map:

- **tasks/** (what to do)
  - `read_review.md` - render-first reading/review
  - `extract.md` - extract text/layout/tables/images/attachments/forms
  - `coords.md` - coordinate system cheatsheet (PDF pt vs image px)
  - `edit.md` - merge/split/select/rotate/crop/watermark/paginate/encrypt/repair
  - `compare.md` - visual diff workflow
  - `forms_annotations.md` - fillable forms + appearance pitfalls + correctness checklist
  - `forms_debugging.md` - widget-level introspection + acceptable values
  - `forms_nonfillable.md` - stamp-by-boxes workflow for non-fillable forms
  - `ocr.md` - OCR scanned PDFs to searchable

I’m combining bounded spherical motion with a meaningful 4D projection: independent plane rotations preserve norm, while stereographic scaling maps the path into 3D. The interface will support playback, scrubbing, camera rotation, tracing, and adjustable parameters.

# 🌀 Whirligig: Full Interactive Demo

Here's the complete working prototype, including the rotating geometry, drawing interface, and mathematical controls.

**[▶ Open the Full Whirligig Demo](sandbox:/mnt/data/whirligig_lab.html)**

- **3D Sphere / Torus:** Explore the original mechanical Fourier-mapping concept.
- **4D Universal Indicatrix:** Experiment with independent rotations in four dimensions.
- **Manipulate the geometry:** Adjust rotation rates, phase, amplitude, coupling, and scale.
- **Rotate the camera:** Drag to examine the geometry from different angles.
- **Control time:** Play, pause, or manually scrub through a rotation cycle.
- **Explore presets:** Load different mathematical configurations.
- **Export SVG:** Save the resulting geometric traces as vector drawings.

The demonstration runs locally in your browser without additional software or external libraries.

### WB — Established Working Bedrock

Premises sufficiently established within the current project state that ordinary sandbox work may use them without reopening them every time. This status means *operatively usable*, not mathematically proven or physically validated.

Current result, construction, interpretation, mapping, or hypothesis important enough to carry forward but still defeasible. **Tentative findings must not silently become downstream bedrock merely through repetition.**

### OC — Open / Contested

Live ambiguity, unresolved alternatives, or a proposition currently under challenge. Downstream work must preserve the uncertainty.

Previously important premise or formulation no longer controlling current theory work. Preserve it with provenance and point to what superseded it.

## Search / retrieval

- **Mersearch / Mercer_Searcher** — Primary corpus-wide body-search route. Use for terms, concepts, names, precursors, terminology drift, and deliberately divergent searches. Search variants and neighboring concepts, not just exact modern vocabulary.

- **SAT/H(s)H repos and GitHub search/history** — Search current files, historical files, commits, diffs, issues, handoffs, Labs, Commons, worker outputs, source indexes, and deleted/superseded states when recoverable. Commit history is often essential for chronology.

- **NLM / numbered archive folders** — Deep source-recovery layer. Folder numbers are wayfinding, not authority or chronology. Follow indexes back to originals where possible and flag gaps.
- **Nathan Words / Nathan-source excavation** — Use for Nathan’s actual language, conceptual ancestry, reversals, terminology, methodological statements, and voice. A Nathan-source item is evidence of what was said in that context, not automatic current-theory authority.
- **Braintrust Memorial Commons / Field Notes / Labs / Q&A / handoffs / check-ins** — Useful for hypotheses, failed approaches, recommendations, unresolved questions, cross-instance observations, and pointers into deeper sources. Treat as working records, not established theory.
- **Revival materials / historical-instance records** — Use to recover earlier instances, methods, forgotten results, first-blush reactions, and historical terminology. Search aliases: e.g. Alberr / Albert / Einstein and other known identity variants.
- **Public-site / Glass Sausage Factory feeds and artifacts** — Useful for locating presentation-ready material, public chronology, papers, conversations, quotes/news, and publication state. Public presentation does not by itself establish theory status.

## Search behavior

Search conceptually and historically, not only lexically. Try modern term → older synonyms → descriptive phrases → opposite framing → nearby dates → likely conversations → original artifact.

When useful, deliberately search somewhere unlikely: old SAT, philosophy/methodology, abandoned branches, unrelated-looking conversations, historical instances, or material opposite your normal specialty. Unexpected ancestry is often valuable.

Prefer the original source over an index, summary, recollection, or later retelling. Preserve exact path/date/author/instance/status when something matters.

When uncertain: **preserve the boundary, record the pointer, and route the question rather than crossing it.**

Bring back the useful thing itself, plus:

**where it came from → when → who/what produced it → exact status → why it matters → what it does not establish → best next pointer.**

**Status:** CURRENT backend presentation contract  
**Date:** 2026-09-30  
**Scope:** public reader/library navigation and rendering only. This file does not define theory status.

## Core rule

The public site must never make repository serialization or authoring markup the default reading experience.

Repository objects fall into three presentation classes:

1. **READER DOCUMENT** — a human-readable primary/source document. It must be routed through a presentation derivative before ordinary display.
2. **MACHINE / CONTROL** — JSON feeds, manifests, live-influx packets, scripts, workflow/control documents, build suggestions, indexes intended primarily for machines/operators. These are backend inputs and are not ordinary Reading Library documents.
3. **RAW SOURCE** — exact original bytes/text retained for provenance. Raw view is secondary and explicitly requested; it is never the default presentation.

## Hard exclusions from generic browse-as-document

The generic reader must not offer these as ordinary reader documents:

- `PUBLIC_SITE/live_influx/**`
- `PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/**`
- `PUBLIC_SITE/build_suggestions/**`
- `PUBLIC_SITE/*_FEED.json`, `CURRENT_WORK.json`, `ASSET_MANIFEST.json`
- workflow/control files whose purpose is operating the site rather than explaining SAT/H(s)H
- executable/source-code files unless the visitor explicitly chooses a source/code view

The 2026-09-28 CALIPER JSON packet is the motivating regression. It points to a presented method document; the packet itself is not the document.

## Presentation derivative

For reader documents, prefer this chain:

`source -> audience-calibrated preface -> RevTeX source -> compiled PDF -> site PDF/document viewer`

The ordinary visitor sees the compiled presentation. The source/original remains available through a clearly secondary **SOURCE / RAW** affordance.

Presentation must preserve source identity, date, status, and provenance while allowing formatting repair. Formatting repair may normalize broken Markdown/LaTeX/math serialization but must not silently alter scientific content.

### PDF acceptance

A presentation derivative is eligible only when:

- section hierarchy is rendered, not exposed as markup;
- inline/display mathematics is typeset;
- tables, figures, boxes, references, URLs, and equations respect page boundaries;
- long equations and URLs wrap or break safely;
- no text or box crosses printable/viewer bounds;
- narrow-screen viewer reflow/zoom remains usable;
- a short plain-English preface identifies what the document is, intended audience, historical/current status, and where it sits in SAT/H(s)H;
- technical readers receive direct links/pointers to the highest-value equations, calculations, findings, assumptions, tests, and source record where applicable.

## Reader routing

A generic repository path is not sufficient evidence that an object belongs in the Reading Library.

If a backend packet/feed nominates a source:
1. resolve its intended human-facing source;
2. find/build the presentation derivative;
3. route the public card/link to that derivative;
4. retain packet/feed/raw source only as provenance/backend controls.

If no presentation derivative exists, show a concise **presentation pending** state or omit it from ordinary browse. Do not dump markup as fallback.

## Live-update behavior

Backend feeds may refresh automatically, but live updating must not bypass the presentation gate. New source material can become discoverable as **pending presentation** without becoming a raw public reading page.

Use explicit state:
- PRESENTED
- PRESENTATION PENDING
- CACHED / snapshot timestamp
- OFFLINE
- SOURCE ONLY

Never leave indefinite `Loading…` as the public state.

## Lane separation

This contract is Sites presentation infrastructure only. Do not inject Sites policy, licensing mechanics, staging workflow prose, or internal coordination language into theory documents.

Theory sources remain theory sources. Presentation metadata belongs here.

2. Reviewed-paper presentation has an already-documented shared defect: Markdown and TeX manuscript sources have been exposed as raw/unformatted markup through the `sandbox_manuscript` route.
3. The archive/repository universe is heterogeneous enough that extension-based or generic repository browsing cannot safely define a public Reading Library.
4. Newly uploaded images are mixed provenance: exact/script-drawn figures, solver-run plots, provenance scans, metrics screenshots, generated illustrations, duplicates and unclassified images. Direct auto-gallery admission is unsafe.

## Backend correction

Use `PUBLIC_SITE/READER_ROUTING_REGISTRY.md` as the default-deny route contract together with `PRESENTATION_GATE.md`.

Public document route:

No derivative:

## Navigability

Public browse/search should organize *presented objects*, not repository serialization. Repository location remains provenance metadata.

Recommended primary facets:
- Start Here / orientation
- Current H(s)H
- Historical SAT
- Papers
- Methods / calculations
- Geometry / solvers
- Visual atlas
- Podcast / talks
- Archive / provenance
- Glossary

A technical reader can drill to source provenance from any presented object without making source markup the public reading experience.

## Live-update contract

Discovery may be live. Presentation is versioned/gated.

Each public object should expose:
- presentation state;
- source repo/path + source identity/hash;
- derivative identity/hash/build timestamp;
- theory/history/status label;
- last successful refresh.

Do not leave indefinite Loading states. Use LIVE, CACHED, PRESENTATION PENDING, OFFLINE, or SOURCE ONLY.

**Status:** ACTIVE public-site presentation guidance  
**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive  
**Authority:** presentation/editorial infrastructure only; theory status remains controlled by BEDROCK and source-specific surfaces.

## Editorial posture

The site should be **curious, exact, confident about what exists, and restrained about what it means**.

Avoid a default posture of apology, self-deprecation, or defensive throat-clearing. SAT/H(s)H can be presented as an unusual open research program worth examining without either underselling it or implying validation that has not occurred.

The preferred rhythm is:

> **interesting object → what it says/does → why it matters here → source/status**

not:

> **warning → disclaimer → warning → interesting object**

Caveats remain important, but they should normally appear as concise metadata, status chips, provenance notes, or a compact research-status panel rather than dominating the emotional voice of the page.

### Voice

Prefer:

- `active research program`
- `current construction`
- `historical formulation`
- `open question`
- `comparison target`
- `structural resonance`
- `direct constraint`
- `source recovered`
- `under active mathematical review`
- `relationship not established`

Use sparingly or avoid as default framing:

- `just a pet theory`
- `not a victory`
- `mere resemblance`
- repeated `this does not prove...` constructions
- red-alert styling for ordinary uncertainty
- language that sounds embarrassed by speculative or exploratory work merely because it is exploratory

When a stronger caution is actually needed, state it plainly and locally.

## Research-status copy

A compact standing status block may say:

> **Research status** — SAT/H(s)H is an active research program with a public development record. The archive includes foundational premises, historical formulations, current reconstruction, mathematical and computational work, failed branches, and results at different stages of review. Source and status travel with the material.

This replaces long defensive caveat blocks as the normal front-door treatment.

## In the News

### Editorial purpose

`In the News` is a rotating window onto external scientific results that are interesting to place beside SAT/H(s)H work.

The section is **not** restricted to results already expected by the project. It may include:

- measurements that directly constrain a live SAT/H(s)H idea;
- results that resemble or illuminate a structural motif being explored;
- findings that make an old SAT/H(s)H conversation newly interesting to revisit;
- apparently contradictory results that sharpen a test;
- genuinely eyebrow-raising observations with no established relationship yet, when the juxtaposition itself is intellectually useful.

The site should not flatten these categories into `evidence for SAT`.

### Preferred heading language

Good options include:

- **In the News — New results at the edges of the map**
- **In the News — Results, constraints, and curious touchpoints**
- **In the News — What caught our attention**

Avoid the older defensive heading `Signals worth testing—not victories to announce.`

### Card anatomy

Each news card should expose:

[L2]   "content": "# 🔎 MERSEARCH — START HERE FOR EVERY ARCHIVE RESEARCH WORKER

**Effective 2026-10-09. Direct user instruction:** SAT/H(s)H LLM workers **should be using Mersearch now** for archive archaeology, source recovery, prior calculations, theory history, provenance, and source-first mathematical work. It is an active shared tool, not a future idea. **Search before claiming a construction is absent, novel, unrecoverable or superseded.**

**Additional controlling Nathan Direct, 2026-10-09:** Read [internal-first SAT, FIE/RMS, and restricted-source rules](NATHAN_DIRECT_2026-10-09_INTERNAL_FIRST_PROVENANCE_AND_SOURCE_BOUNDARY.md). Before consulting outside prior art, find/cite and examine SAT/H(s)H precedent and develop its internal implications first. *No Hopf/spherical carrier is imported.* **Hypothesis H proper and directly Schreiber-authored content stay off-limits** even if mirrored. Other formerly quarantined comparisons need *per-item* clearance. The searcher's automatic `PRIOR_ART`/`QUARANTINE` exclusions remain intentionally unchanged: do **not** bypass with a blanket index or publish them. The nlab Mersearch port is stand-alone and is not an interoperability bridge.


## The 15-second rule

**Default: search ALL THREE permitted repositories together.**

1. `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` (original SAT / GLASS)
2. `Satobloc/HsH` (H(s)H, full conversations and current work)
3. `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES` (private/internal reference resources and toolkit; **not** a public search corpus or theory authority)

Treat `PRIOR_ART` and `QUARANTINE` as excluded. Do not silently limit a historical search to one archive. If one source is unavailable, **state which repository was missing** and report that results are **partial**. Repository names alone do not establish access rights; follow actual permissions and source classification.

### Choose the search interface you actually have

| You can… | Use | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run Python against checked-out archives | Pinned `mersearch-stable-1.0`, invoked over all three roots | Available now; stable Boolean/NEAR/math notation, not chronology inference |
| Use the HsH GitHub connector but cannot run Python | `.github/workflows/mersearch-request-bridge.yml` via `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json` on `main` | **Three-root bridge activated 2026-10-09**; inspect the published manifest before asserting coverage |
| Work on the chronology/multi-archive development branch | `mersearch-chronology-20261007`: run `python tools/search_archive_content.py --capabilities`, `--help`, `--examples`, `--coverage` | Candidate 1.2, tested on synthetic fixtures; **not** the pinned stable release |
| Only have GitHub code search | Query each of the three repositories independently and disclose caps/limitations | Fallback, **not** a verified Mersearch run |

**Do not confuse the human Pages interface with research search.** The public web page is a curated conversation-*title/path* catalog until a separately reviewed public full-text index goes live. It does not expose the whole research corpus.

## GitHub connector route: read before writing

1. Read `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json`. This is a **shared single-slot bridge**, and another worker may have a pending request. **Do not overwrite** a pending request (currently a Ravel contact/backreaction query as of this note). If occupied, use your own local Mersearch checkout, inspect previously published runs, or coordinate a turn. Do not pretend a connector code search is a Mersearch result.
2. When the slot is free, write a fresh unique `request_id`, a query using the stable 1.0 language, requester and purpose. A change to this file on `main` starts the GitHub Actions workflow.
3. Retrieve the indexed result folder `indexes/mersearch_requests/<request_id>/`, including `SEARCH_RESULTS.json`, `SEARCH_RESULTS.md` and `RUN_MANIFEST.json`. The moving aliases `latest.*` are not sufficient provenance and may not be current.
   - **New as of 2026-10-11:** fresh successful bridge runs additionally write bounded `SEARCH_RECEIPT.md` and `SEARCH_RECEIPT.json` in the same request-specific folder. Their SHA-256 digests are recorded in `RUN_MANIFEST.json`. Read the compact receipt first when the full results are too large for connector text readers; the receipt is a *navigation sample* and does not replace the complete search output. Existing runs are not retroactively changed. Detailed `resources/` hit content is deliberately omitted from the public receipt.
4. Confirm the **actual** searched repositories, exact source SHAs, stable Mersearch implementation ref, exclusions and completion. Failed or incomplete runs are not results. Remember: scan exclusions and large files may limit completeness even if three repositories were checked out.

## Local pinned Mersearch usage

From a stable checkout with sibling archive directories visible (paths here are examples):

```bash
python tools/search_archive_content.py \
  /data/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 /data/HsH /data/HSH_RESOURCES \
  --expr '("refractive index" NEAR/12 "phase shift") OR "0.24"' \
  --sort date --out /tmp/mersearch-optical
```

More queries:

```text
("stringing along theory" OR "toy theory") AND (filament OR string)
("Chronophysical" OR "SAT Mark V") AND "phase shift"
math:"B=3/(4*pi)"
(name:*LAB* OR path:*PHASE*) AND (optical OR kink)
author:user AND (worldtube NEAR/12 holonomy)
```

Stable search supports Boolean `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, parentheses, quoted phrases, `NEAR/n`, `author:`, `role:`, `body:`, `math:`, `title:`, `date:`, `name:`, `path:`, `status:` and path/name globs. The mathematical mode normalizes notation but does **not** prove algebraic equivalence. Search several alternate mathematical forms; don't pretend automatic CAS exists.

**LLMs must discover available capabilities.** On the development branch, start with `--capabilities`. On stable 1.0, read `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_RELEASES.md` and `--help`; do not assume later flags exist. Never guess a filter name.

## Required researcher reading and provenance cycle (October 9)

Each substantive theory-source pass should consult [FIE](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf) and relevant [RMS primary sources](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/RMS%20THE%20FRAMEWORK.txt) periodically, plus randomly or systematically sampled **older SAT files**. Search HsH *nested development folders, loose exports, LIVE CONVOS, root files and miscellaneous CONVOS locations*, not only the conventional `SAT_CONVOS_*` folders. Note exactly which documents were *read*, *searched*, *metadata-inventoried* or *unavailable*. Log new source-located equations and share concise cross-worker insights through Common Room. Early terminology and apparently failed constructions must be reconstructed before replacement mechanisms are invented.

For any proposed external crosswalk, maintain this sequence: **SAT source search → exact SAT citations → internal reconstruction/test → nonrestricted prior-art source review → comparator citation only**. The new amendment does not authorize access to the two remaining forbidden classes, indiscriminate private source indexing, or changing public search allowlists.

## Historical provenance

- Direct message timestamps from structured exports are hard evidence for those messages. Folder/archive dates and dates **mentioned** in text are not interchangeable.
- Early use of version names (SAT Mark IV.2, Mark V, SAT X/XY/Z/O, Chronophysical, Stringing Along Theory, toy theory) may date a passage only **tentatively**; retrospective use, renamed concepts and compilations can invalidate simple inferences.

- For the `0.24 rad` lineage, prioritize early **laboratory optical phase-shift** calculations and related **refractive-index** discussion before imposing later projection-constant interpretations.
- Include exact source path, line/message locator, original date if known, query, searched repositories, engine/ref, and limitations with every finding.

## Immediate operating rule

If an agent's task involves SAT/H(s)H history, equations, geometry, or the status of a claimed earlier result, **invoke a permitted search route first and inspect original matched context before inventing a replacement**. Do not delay serious calculation once useful sources are found.

[L2]   "content": "# BEDROCK — SAT / H(s)H Theory Control Surface

**Status:** ACTIVE — central living theory-premise register  
**Authority:** Nathan Direct controls this register.  
**Scope:** SAT → H(s)H theory work.  
**Rule:** **Read this before substantive theory work. Return here when theory work changes what may safely be assumed.**

> This document is a control surface for theory work, not a claim that the research program is physically correct. It records what the project currently permits workers to treat as premises, what remains tentative, and what has been overridden, contested, or superseded.

## 0. Central routing rule

All substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work should use this document as its central premise-state reference.

The working flow is:

**Foundational sources / historical SAT → BEDROCK → sandbox theory work → tentative finding → testing / comparison / Nathan review → BEDROCK**

Do not reconstruct the project's bedrock from the newest paper, the newest conversation, a synthesis, memory, outside mathematics, or repeated AI agreement when this register or its cited primary sources answer the question.

This register does **not** replace primary sources. It points to them and records their current authority/status.

### Two central theory surfaces

- **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)** answers: **What may theory work presently assume, and with what authority/status?**
- **[STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md](STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md)** answers: **Where is the theory now, what is live, what is being translated/built, and what remains unclosed?**

`STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` is subordinate to BEDROCK and newer Nathan Direct. It is the living map, not an independent source of authority.

---

## 1. Authority and status strata

### ND — Nathan Direct / Override

Explicit current direction from Nathan. This is the highest local authority for what the project presently means, assumes, calls something, or treats as live.

A newer Nathan Direct statement may promote, modify, demote, or override an older entry. **Do not delete the older state.** Mark the relationship so the historical transition remains visible.

### FB — Foundational Bedrock

Premises inherited from material explicitly designated foundational by Nathan, especially **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended**. These may be reformulated or developed later, but workers should not silently discard or rewrite them.

### WB — Established Working Bedrock

Premises sufficiently established within the current project state that ordinary sandbox work may use them without reopening them every time. This status means *operatively usable*, not mathematically proven or physically validated.

### TF — Tentative Finding

Current result, construction, interpretation, mapping, or hypothesis important enough to carry forward but still defeasible. **Tentative findings must not silently become downstream bedrock merely through repetition.**

### OC — Open / Contested

Live ambiguity, unresolved alternatives, or a proposition currently under challenge. Downstream work must preserve the uncertainty.

### SS — Superseded / Historical

Previously important premise or formulation no longer controlling current theory work. Preserve it with provenance and point to what superseded it.

---

## 2. bedrock register

Each proposition should be small enough to cite and update independently.

### BR-000 — Fundamental Intuitions Extended is the foundational source

- **Status:** ND + FB
- **Scope:** FIE → SAT → H(s)H
- **Statement:** **The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended is the core foundational doctrine for SAT and almost literally the core foundational doctrine for H(s)H.** H(s)H may develop, formalize, revise, or reframe inherited structures, but foundational questions should consult FIE directly rather than reconstructing them from summaries, memory, analogy, or outside mathematics.
- **Primary source:** [The Fundamental Intuitions — Extended](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf)
- **Control references:** [HsH Issue #2 — HARD-CORE MUST-KNOW](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/2) · [HsH Issue #3 — orientation/resource-map task](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/issues/3)
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, reaffirmed 2026-09-16.

### BR-001 — FIE → SAT → H(s)H is an ancestry, not a replacement chain

- **Status:** ND + WB
- **Scope:** project-wide theory interpretation
- **Statement:** Read current H(s)H as developing from SAT, and SAT as developing from the foundational intuitions. Later terminology or formalism does not automatically erase the earlier conceptual dependency. Apparent conflicts should be investigated historically and explicitly rather than silently harmonized.
- **Source:** Nathan Direct orientation embodied in Issues #2/#3 and current workflow control.
- **Date/status note:** active 2026-09-16.

### BR-002 — BEDROCK is the center for theory work

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** all substantive SAT/H(s)H theory work
- **Statement:** Workers begin substantive theory work by checking this register and return findings here through the status process below. A recent derivation, synthesis, solver output, or sandbox document does not outrank the premise state recorded here merely by being newer or more polished.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-003 — New theory results enter as tentative by default

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions
- **Statement:** A result does not become bedrock because an AI derived it, multiple AIs agreed with it, it is coherent, it is current, or it is polished. New substantive results enter as **TF — Tentative Finding** unless Nathan directly assigns a stronger status or an explicit later promotion process does so.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-004 — Nathan Direct overrides preserve stratigraphy

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** theory-state transitions and provenance
- **Statement:** When Nathan modifies or overrides an existing premise, preserve the old entry/status and explicitly link the transition. Do not rewrite history to make the current formulation appear to have existed earlier.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16.

### BR-005 — θ₄ baseline is measured from the time normal

- **Status:** ND
- **Scope:** SAT θ₄ convention and SAT → H(s)H translation
- **Statement:** SAT θ₄ measures the filament–timesheet intersection angle from the **time normal**. Null/vacuum orientation is **θ₄ = 0**, with the filament tangent parallel to the time normal / timesheet propagation direction. For a particle at rest, θ₄ is equivalent to inverse helical pitch.
- **Source:** [`!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md`](!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md), 2026-09-16 θ₄ baseline entry, explicitly recorded there as Nathan-direct clarification.
- **Boundary:** The adjacent working hypothesis about the origin/inheritance of winding is **not** part of this entry and remains exploratory unless separately promoted.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-16; propagated to BEDROCK 2026-09-18.

---

## 3. Open / contested register

### OC-001 — Q versus inverse-Q / braid smoothing and scaling is unresolved

- **Status:** ND + OC
- **Scope:** SAT/H(s)H Q-rule, inverse-Q rule, braid smoothing, scaling, and scale-transition reconstruction
- **Statement:** **Neither the Q rule nor the inverse-Q rule is currently adequate. Both are insufficient.** Do not treat either formulation as the resolved/current rule. The reconstruction target is to recover why each was insufficient, what smoothing/scaling problem each attempted to solve, what alternatives or bridges were attempted, and what later work superseded or constrained them.
- **Source:** [`WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_DIRECT_WORKFLOW_STATE.md`](WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_DIRECT_WORKFLOW_STATE.md), Nathan-direct clarification dated 2026-09-19.
- **Boundary:** Proposed devices such as a “holonomy bridge” remain historical/exploratory unless separately established; NotebookLM material is wayfinding/reconstruction evidence subject to authorship/source-boundary checks, not automatic theory authority.
- **Next discriminator:** source-chronology reconstruction across Q, inverse-Q, braid-smoothing, scaling, scale-transition, and bridge attempts.
- **Date/status note:** Nathan Direct, 2026-09-19; propagated to BEDROCK 2026-09-19.

### OC-002 — Temporal support of electromagnetic/electrogravity interactions

- **Status:** ND + OC
- **Scope:** wavefront-local update, Kelvin vortices, timesheet solitons, responsive-medium interpretation
- **Statement:** The active time-wavefront thickness remains the preferred first-pass *region of update*. Whether electromagnetic effects also persist in portions of the 4D block ahead of or behind a passing sheet is **open**. A strictly wavefront-local account is Nathan's tentative preference, **not a settled law**. The historic t-boson/f-boson and timesheet-soliton vocabulary and a responsive medium are to be compared for which, if any, physical state persists.
- **Preserved distinctions:** Worldtube continuity and back-tug/transtemporal interbraid force remain inherited SAT modeling commitments. Electromagnetic memory is a separate unresolved constitutive question. Neither a static Coulomb law nor a toolkit's vortex analogy demonstrates complete Maxwell/QED dynamics.
- **Source:** Nathan Direct, 2026-10-09 current conversation; raw message anchor pending. [Mercer bounded source/geometry check](WORKSPACES/MERCER/2026-10-09_KERR_ER_SLAB_INHERITANCE_AND_ARCHIVE_PASS.md).
- **Next discriminator:** derive Coulomb stationary limit *and* finite-speed response to time-dependent charge currents in at least a wavefront-only and persistent-medium version, before tuning to CODATA.

---

## 4. Tentative findings intake

This section is the landing zone for important theory-bearing results that may matter downstream but have **not** been promoted to working/foundational bedrock.

Do not bulk-import every sandbox observation. Add a TF entry when carrying the result forward will materially reduce repeated reconstruction or prevent downstream workers from missing an important live possibility.

```text
### TF-### — Short proposition name

- Status: TF
- Scope:
- Statement:
- Source(s):
- Date first recorded:
- Checks actually performed:
- Dependencies / assumptions:
- Known breakers / counterevidence:
- Relationship to existing BR/TF/OC/SS entries:
- Next discriminator:
```

**No tentative findings are seeded here merely to populate the section.** Existing Ravel/Meridian/other sandbox work should be admitted individually in later bounded passes after its exact source and status are checked.

---

## 5. Nathan Direct override / amendment intake

### ND-2026-10-09-01 — SAT inheritance; H(s)H Kerr/ER tube core is the *working* hypothesis

- **Scope:** SAT-to-H(s)H construction and source/tool ingestion.
- **Controls:** SAT worldlines in Minkowski space with a linear or radial w, extended as H(s)H finite-core worldtubes. Do **not** import Hopf carriers, extra spherical ontology, vertices or outside constructions as prerequisites.
- **Working hypothesis, TENTATIVE:** H(s)H worldtubes as Kerr-like Einstein–Rosen structures; the Kerr ring as an intersection trace of a tube singular support; a conjectured geometric origin of exclusion; candidate closed-string-like intersections of shell substructure and topology-dependent modes. - **Inherited SAT mechanisms:** four-dimensional physical worldtube continuity, interbraid/back-tug/transtemporal interactions for gravitation and strong-like behavior within the model. Operational physical validity is separate.
- **Preserved OC:** electrogravity/Kelvin mechanism and whether EM influence exists outside the **finite-thickness active update wavefront**; no premature decision on persistent medium versus localized timesheet-soliton/t-/f-boson implementation. See OC-002.
- **Source and reconstruction priority:** read old SAT foundational and failed/superseded constructions; use real HsH conversations including loose and root exports, and the permitted reference toolkit as *external machinery*, never as imported ontology. Follow literal Nathan wording and preserve provenance.

Earlier blanket exclusion language below is retained as historical text where not yet reconciled.

### ND-2026-10-09-02 — Straight vacuum filament and partial prior-art access release

- **Authority:** Direct user cross-post, October 9, 2026, signed with signet represented **only** as `[OWL]`; raw conversation/message IDs pending archive.
- **Model clarification:** A SAT worldline does *not* wrap around a carrier. H(s)H extends it as a finite-core worldtube. Straight aligned tube is the conjectured ideal vacuum limit: 90° to timesheet / 0° from time normal and propagation; current BR-005 `θ₄=0` applies. ## 6. Promotion / demotion discipline

Allowed state movements include:

- `TF → WB` — a tentative finding becomes an ordinary working premise.
- `TF → OC` — evidence or interpretation becomes materially unsettled.
- `TF → SS` — abandoned or superseded.
- `WB → OC` — a working premise is reop

## HsH onboarding and website infrastructure review

I've accessed the live **Satobloc/HsH GitHub repository** and followed its front-door documentation into the onboarding, operations, and public-site infrastructure.

The important finding is that **you already have a substantial website backend and publication workflow**. My earlier answer treated the Whirligig as an isolated HTML file requiring manual handling. That overlooked the infrastructure you've developed.

### 1. Archive onboarding

I've retrieved and examined the principal governing documents:

- `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `BEDROCK.md`
- `ONBOARDING/ARCHIVE_TOOLS_ROAMING_CARD.md`
- The Mersearch worker instructions
- The October 15 house-write-first publication rules
- Cross-repository execution and shared-state write safety

The front door explicitly separates current theory authority, historical evidence, operational workflows, and publication infrastructure.

**An important operational correction:** The GitHub connector is a fallback write mechanism, not the default. Workers are instructed to discover and execute existing house workflows before declaring a publication failure.

### 2. Glass Sausage Factory backend

I've inspected the `PUBLIC_SITE/` directory and read the principal website architecture and presentation contracts.

The existing system includes:

| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| `PUBLIC_SITE/README.md` | Site architecture and content management |
| `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` | Development continuity and publication history |
| `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` | Visual design, typography, interaction guidance |
| `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` | Registered visual assets and provenance |
| `CURRENT_WORK.json` | Current research presentation |
| `GALLERY_FEED.json` | Visual Atlas content |
| `AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY.md` | Automatic repository-to-website discovery |
| `PRESENTATION_GATE.md` | Controls how source material becomes public content |
| `READER_ROUTING_REGISTRY.md` | Routes content into appropriate reader experiences |
| `DOC_DUMP_SITE_INTEGRATION.md` | Backend-to-Sites integration contracts |

The automatic discovery system scans the HsH and historical SAT repositories, publishes discovery data, and allows the website to refresh its content without rebuilding the entire site.

That is considerably more capable than the workflow I previously described.

### 3. Publication architecture

The documentation establishes a distinction between two surfaces.

**Repository backend:** Holds durable content, assets, metadata, publication records, and generated feeds.

**ChatGPT Sites frontend:** Consumes that material and presents the visitor experience.

The site development log explicitly warns that changing repository content does not establish that the live Sites frontend has changed.

That distinction matters for Whirligig. We can publish its source and register it as an interactive instrument through the existing backend, but we still need to establish the frontend's executable-content integration.

### 4. Whirligig integration

The repository already includes a `tools/whirligig_rq/` directory, which deserves examination before introducing another Whirligig implementation.

The appropriate integration would preserve the existing project structure and establish a dedicated visitor-facing instrument, potentially under a route such as `/laboratory/whirligig/`.

It should also register the instrument in the site's visual and discovery systems, preserve its mathematical provenance, and distinguish its historical mechanical-mapping mode from its four-dimensional Indicatrix mode.

### 5. What remains unverified

I have **not** completed an exhaustive reading of every nested website/backend file. I have inspected the main documentation and directory structure, but several components still require examination, including the full Whirligig tooling, the website runtime scripts, and the actual frontend implementation.

I also attempted to access the published Glass Sausage Factory website. The browsing interface could not retrieve it, so I cannot claim to have visually inspected the live frontend.

**Current status:** Principal onboarding and website architecture reviewed; full backend/frontend audit incomplete; Whirligig not yet published.

The key correction is clear, however: **we should integrate the Whirligig through the infrastructure you already built, rather than inventing a competing publication system.**

[L2]   "content": "# Whirligig R/Q Engine: rolling sphere, gimbals, two equations, Curvy_Lisa

**Version:** experimental v0.1, 11 October 2026  
**Status:** SANDBOXED engineering reconstruction. Mathematical/procedural tool, not a proof of a physical isomorphism.

This is a working, configurable **two-equation** mechanism drawn from the historical R/Q / Great Annulum / W_obble / W_iggle / Curvy_Lisa description, together with the archived continuous Navier–Stokes Whirligig Python predecessor. It generates equation curves on a sphere, carries them inside a rolling ball constrained by a torus, uses two genuine orthogonal gimbal hinges to select curve endpoints, constructs the R–Q crossbar and a rotation-minimizing plane perpendicular to it, then intersects a rotating pen ray with the **actual torus quartic** to generate Curvy_Lisa.

**Source provenance:**
- [*FINDING THE DONUT*, pp. 23–27](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/FINDING%20THE%20DONUT%20(nolat).txt), March 2026.
- [*THE_WHIRLIGIG*](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/HsH-SAT%20Roundup%203/THE_WHIRLIGIG.txt).
- [Existing continuous NS Whirligig source](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/continuous_ns_whirligig_solver%20%281%29.py), independently specifying the sphere's moving contact frame, Bishop connector, torus-wall ray casting, and a Navier–Stokes test setup.
- [*WHIRLIGIG -- REDEFINING SUCCESS*](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/WHIRLIGIG%20--%20REDEFINING%20SUCCESS.txt): a **constructive existence** goal for a back hallway, not a demand for one unique universal derivative.
- Original source distinguishes 3D mechanical toy geometry from actual four-dimensional systems. This code does too.

## Run

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python whirligig.py --input example_equations.json --out output --search
python plot_mechanics.py --input example_equations.json --out mechanics_snapshot.png --gif rolling_whirligig.gif
python validate_mapping.py --input example_equations.json --out mapping_validation.json
python -m pytest -q
```

`--input` is optional: a two-harmonic-pair demonstration is built in.

## Input equation adapters

Two independent specs are supplied as `R` and `Q` in a JSON file. Every adapter records its representation choice, physical units remain those of the caller, and original numerical coordinates are preserved apart from the sphere carrier. **No universal faithful parameterization exists for arbitrary symbolic equations without specifying a solution branch, observables, and a parameter interval.** Accordingly the tool supports:

| Kind | Example | What is done | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `0.5*cos(2*t)+0.1*sin(5*t)` | Scalar function encoded reversibly in sphere latitude; azimuth is `t` | Functions must be finite on the interval. Periodicity tested, not fabricated |
| `parametric` | `{"components":["cos(t)","sin(t)"]}` | 2D trajectory via reversible stereographic embedding; 3D trajectory radialized with magnitude preserved separately | 3D radial projection loses magnitude in its sphere output |
| `implicit` | `x*x/2.25+y*y-1=0` written as `x*x/2.25+y*y-1` | Extract largest closed real zero contour and stereographically lift | Grid approximate; must set bounding box and a suitable branch |
| `ode` | `{"rhs":["y","-x"],"initial":[1,0]}` | Numerically integrates a 1–3 dimensional ODE and embeds the path | May not close; only specified initial-value solution is represented |
| `sampled` | `{"path":"path.csv"}` | Arclength-resamples a closed 2D/3D numeric curve | Intended for PDE/GR/field equations solved upstream; refuses open CSV curves |

Expression parsing is AST-restricted: arithmetic and common NumPy scalar mathematical functions only. No `eval()`, attribute access, user code import, or arbitrary shell expression execution.

For a PDE, differential geometry equation, non-Euclidean metric, or symbolic Schwarzschild geodesic, **first choose a solution and chart** and pass the resulting parametric/CSV path. This prevents smuggling an arbitrary metric into a falsely universal polar-projection routine. Keep the full source equation and domain as metadata outside the low-dimensional carrier.

## Exact selected-contact rolling law

Let the torus have major radius `R` and tube/minor radius `a`. Let the sphere have radius `b<a` and travel on a center circle of radius

\[
\rho=R+a-b,\qquad C(\psi)=\rho(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0).
\]

The selected contact on the outer equator is

\[
P(\psi)=(R+a)(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0)=C+b\mathbf e_r.
\]

For rolling without slip at this **isolated chosen point**, the laboratory angular velocity obeys

\[
\boldsymbol\omega=-\frac{\rho}{b}\dot\psi\mathbf e_z,
\quad \dot C+\boldsymbol\omega\times(b\mathbf e_r)=0.
\]

Define the Great-Annulum body contact angle

\[
\gamma(\psi)=\frac{R+a}{b}\psi.
\]

Let `W(ψ)` be the orthonormal world frame `(e_r,e_phi,e_z)` and `B(γ)` the body-frame triad `(r_annulus,t_annulus,n_annulus)`. The **actual orientation** is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=W(\psi)B(\gamma)^T\in SO(3).
\]

`P=C+Q b r_annulus` is tested point by point. A whole-revolution orientation closes when the contact gearing `g=(R+a)/b` is integral. The historical *even multiple* condition is satisfied by choosing `g=6` by default:

- `R=1.6`, `a=0.55`, `b=(R+a)/6=0.358333...`, `rho=1.791666...`.
- A five-point fourth-order finite-difference check of the no-slip velocity converges to zero under grid refinement, while the underlying analytic identity is exact.
- With `b=a` (the originally described limiting sphere size), ball and torus tube share a nonisolated meridional contact set. The program **can render that mode** when `allow_degenerate_contact=true`, but explicitly does **not certify unique-contact rolling**; imposing no slip at every contact point would be overconstrained.

## Gimbal, connector and pen

The input R endpoint is acted on by an internal `Ry(pitch)` hinge; the Q endpoint by an independent `Rx(roll)` hinge. Their axes are perpendicular **by exact construction**. Hinge angles use integer-period rotations with optional sinusoidal modulations. The sphere's physical `SO(3)` rotation is separate from these **internal coordinate controls**. The two endpoints are transported into the lab frame with the exact `Q(ψ)` orientation above.

`W_obble=(R_world+Q_world)/2` is the connector midpoint, and `W_iggle` is the plane perpendicular to the connector. A minimal-rotation Bishop frame supplies its two orthonormal axes. The pen rotates in that plane. Its **first forward** intersection with the torus is found by solving the torus implicit quartic and selecting its smallest positive real root, not by approximating a torus-looking curve.

Optional `align_source_anchors` rotates one source curve **by a single rigid SO(3) alignment**, mapping an off-phase point and tangent on Q to a point and tangent on R. This is a transparent representation intervention, **not an isomorphism proof**, and it is logged with the alignment matrix and both residuals.

An optional Bishop-holonomy correction adjusts the pen's phase around the full circuit. The correction is recorded, and may be disabled: the program does not silently assert that an uncompensated trace must close.

## Results and automatic smoothness search

The `--search` scan varies **four even annulum gear ratios**, pen rotation rates, and independently chosen gimbal rotations. It preserves **all sixty** ranked candidates in `ranked_candidates.json`, including failures; it also saves the selected best candidate's full reproducible arrays, metrics and precision geometry figures. The ranking favors:

- valid mechanical contact, SO(3) orientation and torus quartic intersections;
- nondegenerate sphere/tube clearance;
- both input-equation closures and full orientation closure;
- C¹ seam closure, low curvature variation, low curvature percentile, low high-frequency Fourier tail.

These smoothness thresholds are **engineering filters**, not physical selection laws. C² seam mismatch is reported separately, and smooth candidates must not be mistaken for solutions to the source equations on the other side of their chosen projections. Explicit held-out source-equation residual tests are required before a proposed back hallway is accepted.

For the supplied synthetic two-harmonic pair with independently aligned anchors:

| Diagnostic | Observed |
|---|---:|
| selected contact velocity (analytic) | `0.0` |
| selected contact velocity, 128 samples | `2.14823e-4` |
| selected contact velocity, 256 samples | `1.34990e-5` |
| selected contact velocity, 512 samples | `8.44822e-7` |
| ball-frame closure | `1.73e-15` |
| torus implicit residual | `8.53e-14` |
| Curvy_Lisa positional seam | `8.55e-16` |
| C¹ seam (tangent difference) | `0.00117` |
| R anchor point and tangent gaps | `2.89e-17`, `1.42e-16` |
| response to +1% R amplitude | `0.00287` RMS output shift |
| response to +1% Q amplitude | `0.00903` RMS output shift |

The tests include intentionally nonperiodic inputs and nonintegral rolling gear, both of which must fail the relevant closure checks. Thirteen automated tests passed in the first checked build.

## Files

- `whirligig.py`: generalized two-equation 3D mechanical engine, parsers, closure checks, finite-clearance rolling, search.
- `ui4d.py`: separate, exact six-plane `SO(4)` Universal Indicatrix representation using `y(s)=r(s)R(s)x0`; **not yet coupled to 3D rigid-ball mechanics**.
- `plot_mechanics.py`: precision-drawn sphere/gimbal/annulum/connector/pen figures and optional GIF.
- `validate_mapping.py`: finite-difference grid convergence and independent source-equation perturbations.
- `test_whirligig.py`: 11 regression/negative tests.
- `example_equations.json`: two independent scalar formula inputs with optional anchor alignment.
- `example_ode_vs_implicit.json`: harmonic oscillator versus an ellipse equation.
- `example_historical_limit.json`: equal-radius historical rendering with explicit degeneracy diagnostic.
- `demo/`, `aligned_demo/`: retained 60-run candidate sweeps and selected-best numerical arrays and plots.

## Remaining work

1. **Historic Great Annulum:** source says a self-intersecting annulum with antipodal self-tangent, but does not give its analytic curve. This release makes an explicit great-circle choice. Recover and test the intended self-intersecting annulum before calling this exact historical reconstruction.
2. **4D rolling/gimbal lift:** the sphere/torus apparatus implements the explicitly described **3D toy version**. The separate `ui4d.py` provides its honest SO(4) representation layer, not a fabricated four-dimensional contact geometry.
3. **Joint dynamical derivations:** embedding an equation into a polar curve is not equivalent to deriving an invariant relation from two different equations. Implement input-specific residual or observable maps and compare against held-out predictions in both sectors.
4. **Continuous optimization:** current candidate search is discrete, not a variational or interval-arithmetic global search. Upgrade with constrained smooth optimization, holonomy loops, singularity branch resolution, and complexity/energy budgets.
5. **Metrology and units:** use dimensionless toy geometry until source physical scales and constraints are specified. Do not import GR coefficients into an assumed definition of the engine.

**Research handling:** mathematical apparatus should be assessed independently of speculative framing; no physical claim is inferred from geometric representability alone. Attribution: SAT/H(s)H user and archive research, with original sources linked above; free reuse with citation to source where appropriate.

[L2]   "content": "# Executed results, 11 October 2026

## Source-pair and historical apparatus
Test R = 0.55 cos(2t)+0.15 sin(3t), Q = 0.6 sin(3t)+0.1 cos(5t). Independent source anchors optionally aligned by one constant SO(3) rotation and tangent-frame alignment. Physical sphere minor b=(1.6+0.55)/6, inside a=0.55 torus tube. Selected-contact gear six follows the original even-multiple circuit requirement.

## Sweep
Sixty combinations of the even annulum gear `4,6,8,10`, pen angular harmonic `0..4`, and gimbal turns `(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)`. Full unfiltered, reproducible results are in `aligned_demo/ranked_candidates.json`. The experimental C¹ and curvature filters accept 24 out of 60; 15 near-degenerate gear-four cases are deliberately penalized. The selected best of the aligned case is gear six, pen turn four, gimbal turn `(0,1)`; `aligned_demo/best_run/` contains its actual geometry arrays, curves and diagnostic plots. The unaligned case has 17 smooth outputs out of 60.

## Two-input mechanism verification
The separately configured demonstration passes:

- Both scalar latitude encodings invert numerically, with source residuals of order 1e-15.
- The optional source-anchor rotation aligns an off-phase R/Q pair in position and tangent direction to within 3e-17 and 1.5e-16, respectively.
- Exact analytic rolling contact velocity residual is zero.
- Numeric fourth-order finite differences of contact velocity go from 2.14823e-4 at 128 steps to 1.34990e-5 at 256, and 8.44822e-7 at 512. Approximately sixteenfold convergence after each doubling, indicating the intended fourth-order scaling.
- SO(3) orientation and torus-wall residuals remain around 1e-14 or smaller. Whole-turn ball frame closure around 1.7e-15.
- Curvy_Lisa seam position mismatch around 1e-15, C¹ normalized tangent mismatch about 0.00117 for the configured aligned pair.
- Disabling Bishop-frame holonomy compensation gives a large position mismatch (~1.09); enabling the explicit compensation closes the traced output. This is a **documented control adjustment**, not a claim of spontaneous pen closure.
- A +1% change to R produces Curvy_Lisa RMS change 0.002867; a +1% change to Q produces RMS change 0.009027. The output thus depends on **both source equations**, rather than only on the rolling frame.
- A separate oscillator ODE versus implicit ellipse-contour pair also runs and closes, confirming more than one input type.
- The strict `b=a` original limiting geometry renders and closes its selected pen trace when geared integrally but **does not qualify as unique-contact no-slip**.

## Failures that remain useful
The default pen-turn-three pair closes but fails the heuristic smoothness selection: its curvature roughness is 148.3, compared with ~8.5 for the smoother unaligned selected candidate. An explicitly nonperiodic input `R(t)=t` fails source closure, and a nonintegral roll gear fails ball-orientation closure. These negative controls are required and retained.

## Scope
**This is a tested 3D Whirligig engineering reconstruction, not the complete mathematical 4D original.** Original GrAnn is not analytically specified as a self-intersecting annulum; this release uses a sphere great circle and logs that choice. Full R/Q 4D UI coupling, canonical equation-to-polar-curve equivalence for arbitrary PDEs, derived dynamical back hallways, and externally grounded physical tests remain to be implemented.

**Nothing here establishes GR–QM identity or an isomorphism by itself.** Closure and smoothness are candidate filters. A full isomorphism requires specified source/target domains, preserved operators/invariants, and inverse/held-out reconstructions, one sector at a time.

[L2]   "content": "# Automatic website discovery

The Glass Sausage Factory consumes `PUBLIC_SITE/generated/discovery.json` and its
copied gallery thumbnails. `tools/site_discovery.py` scans both public repositories
on every source push and hourly at :17 UTC. The historical SAT archive is read-only.
The website reads this data without requiring a Sites redeployment; open pages
refresh every five minutes. Workers need not create intake packets.

- SHA changes record additions and revisions. Deleted paths drop from the next
  complete scan; failed repository scans retain last-good records and report stale.
- A rolling 48-item docket refreshes the home page and public notebook. The larger
  catalog remains searchable by title, path, format and bounded text excerpts.
  This is discovery search, **not** a replacement for Mersearch full-text research.
- Source dates inferred from filenames are labelled date hints. Detection times
  are not authorship dates. Inclusion does not change manuscript authority/status.
- Images throughout SAT_VISUALS qualify for generic DAI artwork when the
  EXIF-oriented dimensions are at least 128px and width/height is 0.90–1.10.
  Eligible images are copied as 480px thumbnails; nonsquare files remain excluded
  from generic rotation. Technical figures are not overwritten.
- PRIVATE resources, PRIOR_ART, QUARANTINE and the removed Science Made Stupid
  conversation are excluded. Source identity and hashes remain visible.
- The collector retries network failures, validates source blob hashes, walks
  truncated GitHub trees, and publishes JSON atomically. Errors appear in the feed.

Run: `python tools/site_discovery.py --out PUBLIC_SITE/generated`
Search: `python tools/site_discovery.py --search 'worldtube transport'`
Dependencies: Python 3.12 and Pillow. GITHUB_TOKEN is optional for API quota;
credentials are never emitted in data. The workflow uses its repository token.

Writer verification: the initial scan and generated JSON are validated locally;
inspect the named GitHub Actions run for unattended writer completion. GitHub may
delay scheduled runs. A browser refresh is not the unattended writer.

Because I implemented the Whirligig incorrectly.

You're seeing two genuine defects, not a problem with the camera angle.

### 1. The sphere is not inside the torus

In the browser demo, I drew a unit sphere centered at the origin and a torus with a major radius of approximately 1.43, also centered at the origin.

That produces a sphere surrounded by a ring. It does **not** produce the rolling ball inside the toroidal tube described in your Whirligig design.

### 2. The torus isn't coupled to anything

You're correct. In the code, the torus is decorative.

The point's position is generated independently:

\[
\theta=A\sin(\omega_A\lambda+\delta)
\]

\[
\phi=\omega_B\lambda+\kappa\sin(\omega_A\lambda+\delta)
\]

Neither equation references the torus geometry. There is no rolling-contact constraint, no moving ball center, and no no-slip condition.

Worse, I already found that your HsH repository contains a substantially more complete implementation in `tools/whirligig_rq/`.

### What the instrument should do

<box gap={2}>
  <svg viewBox="0 0 340 180" width="100%" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
    <ellipse cx="170" cy="95" rx="142" ry="65" fill="none" stroke="#9a7750" strokeWidth="24" opacity=".28"/>
    <ellipse cx="170" cy="95" rx="142" ry="65" fill="none" stroke="#b98755" strokeWidth="2"/>
    <ellipse cx="170" cy="95" rx="104" ry="37" fill="none" stroke="#b98755" strokeWidth="1" strokeDasharray="4 4" opacity=".6"/>
    <circle cx="170" cy="26" r="27" fill="#6f9f9b" fillOpacity=".22" stroke="#6f9f9b" strokeWidth="2"/>
    <circle cx="170" cy="26" r="3" fill="#e0c18a"/>
    <path d="M170 26 L170 0" stroke="#e0c18a" strokeWidth="1.5"/>
    <path d="M202 27 Q237 35 259 56" fill="none" stroke="#6f9f9b" strokeWidth="1.5" strokeDasharray="4 3"/>
    <text x="210" y="21" fontSize="10" fill="currentColor">Rolling sphere</text>
    <text x="170" y="173" fontSize="11" fill="currentColor" textAnchor="middle">Toroidal guide</text>
  </svg>
  <caption>Conceptual arrangement, not a precision mechanical drawing.</caption>
</box>

The ball's center must travel along a circular path inside the toroidal tube, while its orientation changes according to the rolling constraint.

Your existing research implementation specifies:

\[
\rho=R+a-b
\]

where \(R\) is the torus major radius, \(a\) its tube radius, and \(b\) the sphere radius.

It also gives the selected-contact, no-slip condition:

\[
\dot{\mathbf C}+
\boldsymbol{\omega}\times(b\mathbf e_r)=0
\]

The internal gimbals, R–Q connector, and pen then need to operate within that moving geometry.

**The fundamental mistake was building a rotating-point visualizer and labeling it Whirligig.** Although its rotations are mathematically defined, it doesn't implement the apparatus you specified.

The correct repair is to make the existing HsH Whirligig R/Q engine the mechanical reference and rebuild the browser visualization around its actual geometry, rather than cosmetically moving the sphere inside the torus.
