[L2]   "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Sandboxed GrAnn minimum-return SO(3) lock.

A functional 3-axis rotational locking candidate, NOT the historical
self-intersecting GrAnn, NOT the full R/Q elbow mechanism, and NOT a globally
no-slip sphere/tube contact for the b=a limiting case.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from fractions import Fraction
from math import gcd, lcm, pi, sqrt
import json
import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation


def exact_ratio(value):
    return value if isinstance(value, Fraction) else Fraction(str(value))


def common_return(rates):
    """Minimal positive INTEGRAL number of base torus circuits for all phases.

    A physical joint configuration requires additional SO(3), contact, branch,
    input-tangent and elbow closure checks. An arithmetic LCM is not enough.
    """
    phases = {k: exact_ratio(v) for k, v in rates.items()}
    if not phases:
        raise ValueError("At least one phase rate is required")
    duration = lcm(*(f.denominator for f in phases.values()))
    counts = {k: int(v * duration) for k, v in phases.items()}
    nonzero = [abs(n) for n in counts.values() if n]
    return {
        "base_torus_circuits": duration,
        "turns_at_return": counts,
        "lcm_of_completed_winding_counts": lcm(*nonzero) if nonzero else 0,
    }


def minimum_grann_turns(major, radius, source_periods=(1, 1),
                        require_even=True):
    """Smallest admissible integer material turns > geometric rolling ratio.

    The strict inequality ensures nonzero x/y spin, while evenness and the
    caller's source orders are optional/divisibility constraints. These orders
    must come from validated source-curve phase/symmetry closure, not labels.
    """
    M, b = exact_ratio(major), exact_ratio(radius)
    if M <= b or b <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Need torus major radius > ball/tube radius > 0")
    orders = [int(x) for x in source_periods]
    if any(x <= 0 for x in orders):
        raise ValueError("Source periods must be positive integers")
    multiple = lcm(*(orders + ([2] if require_even else [1])))
    gear = (M + b) / b
    turns = multiple * (gear.numerator // (gear.denominator * multiple) + 1)
    return turns, float(gear)


def simulate(major=1.65, radius=.55, source_periods=(1, 1),
             require_even=True, samples=2401):
    n, gear = minimum_grann_turns(major, radius, source_periods, require_even)
    R, b = float(major), float(radius)
    sigma = sqrt(n*n - gear*gear)
    psi = np.linspace(0., 2*pi, samples)
    er = np.column_stack((np.cos(psi), np.sin(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    et = np.column_stack((-np.sin(psi), np.cos(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    Q = (Rotation.from_rotvec(np.column_stack((np.zeros_like(psi),
                                              np.zeros_like(psi), psi)))
         * Rotation.from_rotvec(np.outer(psi,
                                        np.array([sigma, 0., -gear])))).as_matrix()
    C = R * er
    contact_body = np.einsum("nji,nj->ni", Q, er)
    wall_pivot = C + b*np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Q, contact_body)
    wall_target = (R+b)*er
    omega = np.column_stack((sigma*er[:,0], sigma*er[:,1],
                             np.full(len(psi), -R/b)))
    slip = R*et + np.cross(omega, b*er)
    spin_angle = n * psi
    theta_turns = spin_angle[-1]/(2*pi)
    dQ = np.gradient(Q, psi, axis=0, edge_order=2)
    Omega = dQ @ np.swapaxes(Q, 1, 2)
    omega_fd = np.column_stack((Omega[:,2,1],Omega[:,0,2],
                                Omega[:,1,0]))
    fd_slip = R*et + np.cross(omega_fd, b*er)
    track_distance = float(np.sum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(contact_body, axis=0), axis=1)))
    result = {
        "major_radius": R,
        "ball_and_tube_radius": b,
        "geometric_contact_ratio": gear,
        "minimal_grann_turns": n,
        "source_phase_orders": list(source_periods),
        "even_winding": (n % 2 == 0),
        "radial_spin_rate": sigma,
        "angular_velocity_component_ranges": {
            axis: [float(omega[:,i].min()),float(omega[:,i].max())]
            for i,axis in enumerate(("x","y","z"))
        },
        "material_turn_count": float(theta_turns),
        "material_track_length_total": track_distance,
        "predicted_material_track_length_total": 2*pi*gear,
        "one_contact_track_cycle_length": 2*pi*gear/n,
        "max_pivot_wall_error": float(np.linalg.norm(wall_pivot-wall_target,axis=1).max()),
        "max_analytic_point_slip": float(np.linalg.norm(slip,axis=1).max()),
        "max_fd_point_slip_interior": float(np.linalg.norm(fd_slip[5:-5],axis=1).max()),
        "SO3_seam_error": float(np.linalg.norm(Q[0]-Q[-1])),
        "SO3_orthogonality_error": float(np.abs(np.swapaxes(Q,1,2)@Q-np.eye(3)).max()),
    }
    return result


def check(report):
    assert report["max_pivot_wall_error"] < 1e-10, "Wall pivot mismatch"
    assert report["max_analytic_point_slip"] < 1e-10, "Selected-point rolling fails"
    assert report["SO3_seam_error"] < 1e-10, "Orientation failed to close"
    assert report["SO3_orthogonality_error"] < 1e-10, "Frame ceased to be SO(3)"
    assert report["radial_spin_rate"] > 0, "All-axis motion missing"
    for component in ("x","y","z"):
        a,b=report["angular_velocity_component_ranges"][component]
        assert b-a > 1e-6 or (component=="z" and abs(a)>1e-6)
    assert report["material_turn_count"] == report["minimal_grann_turns"]


def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--major",type=float,default=1.65)
    p.add_argument("--radius",type=float,default=.55)
    p.add_argument("--r-order",type=int,default=1)
    p.add_argument("--q-order",type=int,default=1)
    p.add_argument("--samples",type=int,default=2401)
    p.add_argument("--check",action="store_true")
    args=p.parse_args()
    out=simulate(args.major,args.radius,(args.r_order,args.q_order),
                 samples=args.samples)
    if args.check:
        check(out)
    print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))


if __name__=="__main__":
    main()

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md","content":"# GrAnn / R–Q Whirligig: inner-wall rolling and minimum shared rotational lock

**Date:** 2026-10-21  
**Status:** SANDBOXED browser engineering reconstruction, repository-published, real-browser/Sites deployment not independently verified.  
**Source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in `Satobloc/HsH`.  
**User correction:** GrAnn is fundamentally rotational locking through **all three spatial axes**, with the **minimum shared return** determining the number of rotations of the single perpendicular gimbal elbow. The sphere rolls on the **inner radial surface of the torus**, not the outer one. The previously visible outward-contact spin looked backward because it was actually the wrong contact branch.

## Selected contact and direction

Let torus major radius be `R`, tube radius and sphere radius both `b=a`, orbital position `C(ψ)=R(cosψ,sinψ,0)=R e_r`, and orbit tangent `e_φ`. The two torus radial equator points are:

```text
Donomphulon = P_inner = (R-b)e_r
P_ivot      = P_outer = (R+b)e_r
r_inner     = P_inner-C = -b e_r
C'          = R e_φ
```

Nominated inner-wall no-slip requires `C' + ω × (-b e_r) = 0` per unit `ψ`, hence the **z component** of angular velocity is `ω_z=+R/b`, in the SAME physical sign as torus progression. For the old **outer** contact `r=+b e_r`, the required sign was `ω_z=-R/b`. Reversing playback alone is not an acceptable fix: switch the selected wall, contact offset, and the resulting orientation/velocity constraint together.

The earlier browser version accidentally labeled its single inner contact as both P_ivot and Donomphulon. This is corrected: P_ivot remains the **outer** circumferential point per the historical source, while Donomphulon is the **inner** selected rolling point; the diameter `2b` separates them. The material GrAnn track passes through both contact and antipode.

## Minimum even three-axis rotational lock

Write `r=R/b`, `δ=r−1`. In this deliberately defined SO(3) locking ansatz, take

```text
n = smallest positive EVEN integer strictly larger than |δ|
σ = sqrt(n²−δ²)                              (nonzero transverse spin)
u = (σ,0,δ)/n                               (unit body axis)
Q(ψ) = Rot_z(ψ) Rot_u(n ψ)
```

Then the world angular velocity per `ψ` is

```text
ω = σ cosψ e_x + σ sinψ e_y + r e_z.
```

The sphere therefore rotates through **x and y over the orbit** as well as the **positive z rolling direction**, without violating the nominated inner-wall slip constraint. Because `n` is an integer and the orbital angle makes a full turn, the complete orientation `Q(2π)=Q(0)`; the **smallest even** `n>|δ|` makes the x/y component strictly nonzero. This is a minimality statement only **within this specified constant-oblique-axis ansatz**, not proof of a globally unique minimal mechanism.

The sphere's body material contact is

```text
g_body(ψ)=Q(ψ)⁻¹(−e_r(ψ))
```

and the torus wall determines `C = P_inner - b Q g_body`. The resulting body track is a generally non-great circular GrAnn contact locus. Its historical self-intersection `GrAnn_Omph`, special antipodal self-tangency `GrAnn_t_ipode` and original R-anchor crossover **have not been reconstructed**. This lock is functional, not a claim to have recovered the exact source-described shape.

## Crossbar and elbow timing

R and Q remain independent E/W **sphere curves**. A common meridional sweep intersects both curves separately, yielding two moving body points `R(ψ)` and `Q(ψ)`. Their freely varying connector has midpoint W_obble; its one and only projecting gimbal elbow is constrained exactly perpendicular to the connector.

The current browser maps each selected input to one closed 2π sphere curve, so one full normalized sweep lap returns both source curves to their represented starting parameters. Let `m` be the selectable **integer** number of complete sweeps per torus orbit. Define

```text
elbow_turns = lcm(n,m)
theta_elbow(ψ) = elbow_turns * ψ
```

This replaces the former separate arbitrary elbow-turn slider and the ad hoc `curvature_gain*(curvature_R−curvature_Q)` phase. The single gimbal elbow intersects the actual torus wall to make Curvy Lisa. The R/Q representation may have shorter scalar periods but a complete spatial curve still carries its azimuth winding; use full curve/orientation closure, not merely scalar equality, to test return.

For `R=1.65,b=.55`: `r=3,δ=2,n=4,σ=sqrt(12)`; default m=1 gives elbow=4, while m=3 gives elbow=12. Other radii choose their own minimal-even n with a floating-point guard at integer boundaries. General source-specific fractional windings, quaternion signs, nonperiodic solutions, nontrivial holonomy and independently varying follower phases would require a more general common-return solver; these are not silently presumed solved.

The browser retains its original **14** equation adapters and adds **28** explicit scalar representatives. They are organized as:

**Status:** Nathan Direct functional correction (2026-10-18), with a separately derived/tested **candidate** realization of a contact-preserving SO(3) lock. Not implemented in the live Whirligig browser instrument.

## Instruction hierarchy

Nathan clarifies that GrAnn–R/Q is fundamentally **rotational locking**:

1. Sphere rotation must pass through **all three spatial axes**.
2. The apparatus must use the **minimum simultaneous number of rotations** that brings the relevant source curve(s) and all mechanical parts back to their complete configurations.
3. The gimbal elbow's rotation count is to be **driven from that common denominator/return**, not independently prescribed by a decorative turn-rate slider.
4. Torus wall contact, sliding R and Q followers, variable crossbar and the single perpendicular projecting elbow remain required.

This supersedes treating geodesic curvature as the *primary purpose* of GrAnn, and supersedes arbitrary elbow curvature-gain modulation as the final mechanism. The earlier Darboux curvature-to-spin paper is retained as a mathematically useful alternative or consequence, NOT the new GrAnn functional definition.

**Important distinction:** The historical GrAnn self-intersection and self-tangency remain source-described geometry, but this revised *functional target* does not justify inventing or imposing a particular figure-eight material curve if the phase lock can be achieved by simpler geometry.

## Common denominator / minimum return

Normalize one torus circuit to one unit of `u`. If independently required axis and curve phase rates are reduced rationals `w_i=p_i/q_i` turns per torus circuit, then the smallest **integral number of complete torus circuits** on which every phase individually returns is

```
D = lcm(q_x, q_y, q_z, q_R, q_Q, ...).
n_i = D * p_i/q_i       integer total turns in that return.
```

Example: x=1/2, y=1/3, z=1/4, R=1, Q=1/6 turns per base circuit. Then **D=12 torus circuits** and `(n_x,n_y,n_z,n_R,n_Q)=(6,4,3,12,2)`. Checking every positive integer duration confirms no smaller positive integer than 12 returns all phases.

**Arithmetic caveat:** `D` (the least common return duration) and `lcm(n_x,n_y,n_z,n_R,n_Q)` (a possible joint gear count for the elbow) are distinct objects and must be displayed separately. Exact closure of SO(3), the two moving input contacts and the elbow-to-wall trace must be verified independently; phase integrality alone is not a mechanical closure proof. We should specify whether elbow *total turns* are D or the LCM of integer windings by the actual gear-linkage definition, rather than quietly conflating the two. Nathan's common-denominator instruction fixes **no independent elbow oscillator** in either case.

Also preserve the historic even-GrAnn-circuits requirement as an independently reported parity constraint, unless superseded by a later explicit instruction.

## Exact contact-preserving all-three-axes candidate

The earlier browser has only one GrAnn rotation phase `g psi`; its elbow rate and curvature gain are separately chosen. We can instead construct a minimal multi-axis **rotational lock** without violating the selected outer-wall rolling constraint.

Use torus major radius `R0` and equal sphere/tube radius `b=a`. Let `psi` be torus orbital angle, `e_r=(cos psi,sin psi,0)`, and `g=(R0+b)/b`. Choose an integer `N>g` that satisfies the required even-parity and R/Q closure divisibility constraints, and choose the **smallest eligible** N. Set

```
sigma = sqrt(N^2-g^2) > 0
K = (sigma, 0, -g)   ;  |K|=N
Q(psi) = Rot_z(psi) * exp_SO3(psi [K]x)
```

where `[K]x` is the cross-product generator. This is a proposed **concrete** SO(3) realization, not source-given original apparatus hardware.

Differentiating the matrix product yields physical world angular velocity per unit orbital angle:

```
omega / psi_dot = sigma cos(psi) e_x + sigma sin(psi) e_y - (R0/b) e_z.
```

All three axes participate when `sigma>0`. The x/y components are the allowed rotation about the moving outer contact normal, while the z component satisfies the selected-contact no-slip requirement. With sphere center `C=R0 e_r` and contact offset `b e_r`:

```
dC/dpsi + (omega / psi_dot) cross (b e_r) = 0.
```

The body-frame material contact locus is `G_body(psi)=Q(psi)^T e_r(psi)`. In this candidate it is a closed *small circle* on the sphere traversed N times per torus circuit. It is GrAnn's rotating contact **track**, not an asserted reconstruction of its originally described Omph/t_ipode self-intersection. The actual arc length per individual material cycle is `L=2*pi*g/N`, so N material turns carry total contact arc length `2*pi*g`, matching the no-slip contact transport.

If the source-input phase orders are positive integers `d_R,d_Q,...`, a practical candidate is

```
k=lcm(2,d_R,d_Q,...).
N=k * (floor(g/k)+1)     // smallest multiple of k STRICTLY greater than g
```

provided the axis/curve orders have been measured or specified, not guessed. The elbow must be geared to the same master N-cycle phase and validated for complete configuration closure; no autonomous `pen_turns` or arbitrarily tuned curvature multiplier is the final mechanism.

## Executed mathematical check

A NumPy/SciPy `scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation` calculation with `R0=1.65`, `b=0.55`, `g=4`, `N=6` (minimal **even** N strictly greater than four) gave:

- `sigma=sqrt(20)=4.47213595499958`.
- physical world angular-velocity components x and y each cover roughly [-4.4721,+4.4721]; the z component is -3 per unit psi.
- torus outer-contact position residual max ~9.2e-16 model units;
- selected-point analytic slip residual max ~3.3e-16;
- full SO(3) orientation-seam Frobenius residual ~1.9e-15;
- GrAnn material track completes six turns; unit-sphere contact arc length traversed 2*pi*g~25.13274, one material circuit length ~4.18879.

The limiting `N=g=4` has `sigma=0` and does **NOT** engage all three axes. N=8 works but is not minimal, so would fail the *minimality* design requirement at this default radius. The selected-contact rolling demonstration is **not** a proof of global no-slip for the nonisolated equal-radius contact locus.

Those must be completed before marking the browser apparatus corrected.

## Implementation acceptance criteria

- GrAnn drives the sphere's complete SO(3) orientation, not a visual ring or independent oscillator; all three axes show nontrivial motion and pass a numerical angular-velocity check.
- The number N is computed from admissible periodicities and minimality, not picked for aesthetic output.
- R/Q contacts found by independent geometric intersections using the common transported frame; source loops return with consistent tangents and branches.
- One variable-length crossbar and one perpendicular elbow; the elbow turn count comes from the same lock with no free decorative oscillator.
- Torus outer-pivot contact, selected-point slip and actual wall intersections satisfy verified constraints.
- SO(3) frame, R and Q contact positions/tangents, elbow orientation, and Curvy Lisa trace all return together, or the candidate is rejected.
- Distinguish source-derived specifications, chosen kinematic interventions, and unproved equation-isomorphism/derivative claims.

## Design

Each input must provide an explicit dimensionless periodic *scalar representative* `f(λ)`, with λ ranging from zero to 2π and a periodic closed result. The instrument applies independent R and Q selection, R/Q **display** gain, and a Q sampling phase. The source's scalar value changes the spherical polar aperture through the existing bounded mapping, preserving opposite E/W hemispheres. It is **not** a universal invertible map from a field equation, metric, representation, wavefunction or solution space to a 3D curve.

Distinct input equations are mapped to the same sphere using an explicitly chosen adapter, not assumed to be isomorphic. Geometry coupling remains unchanged: independent source curves, simultaneous equal-fraction arc-length traversal, one variable-length crossbar, one perpendicular projecting elbow, minimum shared return clock, torus-wall Curvy Lisa output. The numerical comparison readout displays root-mean-square difference between the two **ungained scalar profile samples**, not an equation-isomorphism criterion or field-theory test.

## Catalog

| Code | Mathematical object | Specific selected closed representative | Epistemic scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harm_r` | synthetic harmonic R | cos(2λ)+(3/11)sin(3λ) | demonstration |
| `harm_q` | synthetic harmonic Q | sin(3λ)+(1/6)cos(5λ) | demonstration |
| `u1_phase` | U(1) relative phase | Re exp(i[λ+0.25 sin(2λ)]) | fixed-reference gauge phase; **not gauge invariant** |
| `su2_character` | SU(2) fundamental character | ½Tr diag(exp(iφ),exp(−iφ))=cos φ, φ=2λ+0.35sin λ | group path only; not an SU(2) Yang–Mills field |
| `su3_character` | SU(3) fundamental character | (1+2cos φ)/3, φ=2λ+0.25sin(3λ) | diagonal group path; not QCD dynamics or a Wilson loop |
| `gw_plus` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h₊/h₀=cos(2λ) | TT-gauge wave component, phase-normalized |
| `gw_cross` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h×/h₀=sin(2λ) | TT-gauge component, not gauge-independent complete spacetime |
| `schwarz_orbit` | Schwarzschild timelike circular geodesic | x/r₀=cos λ at equatorial r₀=8M | coordinate x projection, λ is **orbital phase**, not proper time |
| `schwarz_lapse` | Schwarzschild metric lapse | 10[√(1−2M/r(λ))−√(1−2/8)], r/M=8+1.5cos λ | prescribed radial scan, **not a geodesic** |
| `kerr_drag` | Kerr equatorial ZAMO frame dragging | ω(r)=2Ma/(r³+a²r+2Ma²); a/M=0.5; r/M=8+cos λ; f=ω(r)/ω(8M)−1 | prescribed radial scan, **not an orbit** |
| `qm_rabi` | two-level Schrödinger solution | H=(ℏΩ/2)σₓ, Pₑ=sin²(λ/2); 2Pₑ−1=−cos λ | ideal resonant system, λ=Ωt |
| `qm_spin` | spin-½ Larmor precession | H=(ℏω/2)σz; ⟨σₓ⟩=cos λ | ideal initial +x state, λ=ωt |
| `qm_coherent` | quantum harmonic oscillator coherent state | ⟨x⟩/A=cos(3λ) | selected expectation value, ωt=3λ |
| `qm_interference` | coherent two-energy-state superposition | interference factor cos(ΔEt/ℏ)=cos(3λ) | phase interference factor only, not the full probability density |

**Important gauge distinction:** the trace of a chosen group element is a class function under conjugation, but these chosen paths are *not* derived from a gauge connection integrated along physical closed spacetime loops. Do not present them as gauge-invariant Yang–Mills Wilson-loop measurements or solutions to the gauge field equations.

**Important GR distinction:** a selected metric is an exact gravitational solution in its stated idealized setting, but sampling one metric component along an arbitrarily imposed periodic radius does not automatically yield a geodesic or solve a new Einstein field equation. Only the stated Schwarzschild circular-orbit model uses a selected timelike geodesic.

**Important QM distinction:** phase, expectation value, and population probability are different objects. Each input explicitly states which is sampled. Do not equate scalar trace similarity with quantum-state equivalence.

- Two independent selectors: **Equation R / East** and **Equation Q / West**, each containing all 14 profiles.
- Ten named pair presets for same-sector and cross-sector exploration.
- Swap R ↔ Q without claiming invariance of the crossbar/elbow output under swap.
- Equations and clear provenance/scope text visible adjacent to each selector.
- Original demonstration remains the default and reproduces the former coefficients when display gains are 0.55 and 0.60.
- Q sampling phase applies to the chosen Q input before the sphere projection.
- Source groups and formula labels are authored static data. No `eval` of user-supplied mathematics or dynamic execution of arbitrary expressions.
- Exported SVG reflects the selected composite elbow-tip trace.

## Verification and remaining work

The HTML file was independently read back from GitHub after its committed write. A stubbed JavaScript DOM/canvas test executed all 14 profiles on the R selector and all 14 on Q, tested all ten pair presets, independent swap, opposite hemisphere membership, numerical connector–elbow perpendicularity, and numerical torus-wall intersection existence. Maximum orthogonality residual over tested R/preset configurations was below 4.1e−16; all 1,651 samples in each tested configuration had an elbow–torus intersection. The **Q selector** likewise produced zero missing hits or E/W violations in the same baseline mechanical configuration.

These are executed geometry smoke tests **not** browser/visual-acceptance tests, and are not formal verification of the chosen mathematical adapters. Full browser usability, semantic mathematical review, and deployed ChatGPT Sites publication remain unverified.

Next steps: add optional parameter controls with domain/unit checking for each representative; standardize a serialized source specification compatible with the Python engine; separately validate higher-dimensional and nonperiodic solution branches without forcing fake closure; and test whether the experimental composite curves preserve source invariants beyond similar appearance.

## 2026-10-21 UPDATE: 42-profile unfiltered comparison library (supersedes 14-only summary)

The current browser implements the 14 earlier demonstration, gauge, GR, and QM profiles **plus 28 new mathematical representatives**. The selector groups now include **Best-known series (11)** and **Often overlooked series (17)**, alongside the original sector groups. The groups are editorial and exhaustive within this defined library; “best-known” and “often overlooked” are not objective rank, rarity, or significance assessments.

**Best-known:** Newtonian oscillator, Kepler ellipse, Maxwell vacuum wave, Fourier heat mode, Laplace disk harmonic, Schrödinger infinite-well eigenfunction scan, wave-equation standing mode, special-relativistic Lorentz factor, Planck spectrum, Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution, Fermi–Dirac occupation.

**Often overlooked:** Jacobi theta₃, Legendre P₄, Chebyshev T₅, Bessel J₀ (numerical quadrature), Clausen Cl₂ (truncated Fourier series), Re Li₂ (truncated power series), 2D Dirac Berry-curvature scan, Mathieu equation coefficient (not a Mathieu solution), KdV sech² soliton (periodic spatial scan, not a periodic traveling solution), sine–Gordon kink scan, Burgers viscous-shock profile scan, Morse potential, Lennard–Jones 12–6 potential, Kitaev-chain Bogoliubov band, Pöschl–Teller well, Fresnel C (numerical quadrature), U(1) Wilson phase for a **specified** family of fluxes.

Each named profile displays its explicit formula, the sampled quantity, and what is NOT implied. A prescribed closed sampling path is *not* equivalent to claiming an inherently nonperiodic solution becomes periodic. The current UI has **no user-supplied arbitrary code evaluation**. The synthetic and physical examples are never declared automatically equivalent by curve appearance.

This avoids auto-selecting outputs for beauty, similarity, or expected theory claims. Manual R/Q selection and original named pairs are preserved.

# GrAnn R/Q: minimum-return three-axis rotational lock

**Status:** Nathan Direct functional correction (2026-10-18), with a separately derived/tested **candidate** realization of a contact-preserving SO(3) lock. Not implemented in the live Whirligig browser instrument.

## Instruction hierarchy

Nathan clarifies that GrAnn–R/Q is fundamentally **rotational locking**:

1. Sphere rotation must pass through **all three spatial axes**.
2. The apparatus must use the **minimum simultaneous number of rotations** that brings the relevant source curve(s) and all mechanical parts back to their complete configurations.
3. The gimbal elbow's rotation count is to be **driven from that common denominator/return**, not independently prescribed by a decorative turn-rate slider.
4. Torus wall contact, sliding R and Q followers, variable crossbar and the single perpendicular projecting elbow remain required.

This supersedes treating geodesic curvature as the *primary purpose* of GrAnn, and supersedes arbitrary elbow curvature-gain modulation as the final mechanism. The earlier Darboux curvature-to-spin paper is retained as a mathematically useful alternative or consequence, NOT the new GrAnn functional definition.

**Important distinction:** The historical GrAnn self-intersection and self-tangency remain source-described geometry, but this revised *functional target* does not justify inventing or imposing a particular figure-eight material curve if the phase lock can be achieved by simpler geometry.

## Common denominator / minimum return

Normalize one torus circuit to one unit of `u`. If independently required axis and curve phase rates are reduced rationals `w_i=p_i/q_i` turns per torus circuit, then the smallest **integral number of complete torus circuits** on which every phase individually returns is

```
D = lcm(q_x, q_y, q_z, q_R, q_Q, ...).
n_i = D * p_i/q_i       integer total turns in that return.
```

Example: x=1/2, y=1/3, z=1/4, R=1, Q=1/6 turns per base circuit. Then **D=12 torus circuits** and `(n_x,n_y,n_z,n_R,n_Q)=(6,4,3,12,2)`. Checking every positive integer duration confirms no smaller positive integer than 12 returns all phases.

**Arithmetic caveat:** `D` (the least common return duration) and `lcm(n_x,n_y,n_z,n_R,n_Q)` (a possible joint gear count for the elbow) are distinct objects and must be displayed separately. Exact closure of SO(3), the two moving input contacts and the elbow-to-wall trace must be verified independently; phase integrality alone is not a mechanical closure proof. We should specify whether elbow *total turns* are D or the LCM of integer windings by the actual gear-linkage definition, rather than quietly conflating the two. Nathan's common-denominator instruction fixes **no independent elbow oscillator** in either case.

Also preserve the historic even-GrAnn-circuits requirement as an independently reported parity constraint, unless superseded by a later explicit instruction.

## Exact contact-preserving all-three-axes candidate

The earlier browser has only one GrAnn rotation phase `g psi`; its elbow rate and curvature gain are separately chosen. We can instead construct a minimal multi-axis **rotational lock** without violating the selected outer-wall rolling constraint.

Use torus major radius `R0` and equal sphere/tube radius `b=a`. Let `psi` be torus orbital angle, `e_r=(cos psi,sin psi,0)`, and `g=(R0+b)/b`. Choose an integer `N>g` that satisfies the required even-parity and R/Q closure divisibility constraints, and choose the **smallest eligible** N. Set

```
sigma = sqrt(N^2-g^2) > 0
K = (sigma, 0, -g)   ;  |K|=N
Q(psi) = Rot_z(psi) * exp_SO3(psi [K]x)
```

where `[K]x` is the cross-product generator. This is a proposed **concrete** SO(3) realization, not source-given original apparatus hardware.

Differentiating the matrix product yields physical world angular velocity per unit orbital angle:

```
omega / psi_dot = sigma cos(psi) e_x + sigma sin(psi) e_y - (R0/b) e_z.
```

All three axes participate when `sigma>0`. The x/y components are the allowed rotation about the moving outer contact normal, while the z component satisfies the selected-contact no-slip requirement. With sphere center `C=R0 e_r` and contact offset `b e_r`:

```
dC/dpsi + (omega / psi_dot) cross (b e_r) = 0.
```

The body-frame material contact locus is `G_body(psi)=Q(psi)^T e_r(psi)`. In this candidate it is a closed *small circle* on the sphere traversed N times per torus circuit. It is GrAnn's rotating contact **track**, not an asserted reconstruction of its originally described Omph/t_ipode self-intersection. The actual arc length per individual material cycle is `L=2*pi*g/N`, so N material turns carry total contact arc length `2*pi*g`, matching the no-slip contact transport.

If the source-input phase orders are positive integers `d_R,d_Q,...`, a practical candidate is

```
k=lcm(2,d_R,d_Q,...).
N=k * (floor(g/k)+1)     // smallest multiple of k STRICTLY greater than g
```

provided the axis/curve orders have been measured or specified, not guessed. The elbow must be geared to the same master N-cycle phase and validated for complete configuration closure; no autonomous `pen_turns` or arbitrarily tuned curvature multiplier is the final mechanism.

## Executed mathematical check

A NumPy/SciPy `scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation` calculation with `R0=1.65`, `b=0.55`, `g=4`, `N=6` (minimal **even** N strictly greater than four) gave:

- `sigma=sqrt(20)=4.47213595499958`.
- physical world angular-velocity components x and y each cover roughly [-4.4721,+4.4721]; the z component is -3 per unit psi.
- torus outer-contact position residual max ~9.2e-16 model units;
- selected-point analytic slip residual max ~3.3e-16;
- full SO(3) orientation-seam Frobenius residual ~1.9e-15;
- GrAnn material track completes six turns; unit-sphere contact arc length traversed 2*pi*g~25.13274, one material circuit length ~4.18879.

The limiting `N=g=4` has `sigma=0` and does **NOT** engage all three axes. N=8 works but is not minimal, so would fail the *minimality* design requirement at this default radius. The selected-contact rolling demonstration is **not** a proof of global no-slip for the nonisolated equal-radius contact locus.

**Not done:** Integrating the Q matrix and N into both R/Q sliding-intersection branch solvers, removing the old independent elbow-rate law, deriving the real gear linkage and deciding whether elbow's total-turn count is D or `lcm(n_i)`, and testing full R/Q/crossbar/elbow/torus-wall closure. Those must be completed before marking the browser apparatus corrected.

## Implementation acceptance criteria

- GrAnn drives the sphere's complete SO(3) orientation, not a visual ring or independent oscillator; all three axes show nontrivial motion and pass a numerical angular-velocity check.
- The number N is computed from admissible periodicities and minimality, not picked for aesthetic output.
- R/Q contacts found by independent geometric intersections using the common transported frame; source loops return with consistent tangents and branches.
- One variable-length crossbar and one perpendicular elbow; the elbow turn count comes from the same lock with no free decorative oscillator.
- Torus outer-pivot contact, selected-point slip and actual wall intersections satisfy verified constraints.
- SO(3) frame, R and Q contact positions/tangents, elbow orientation, and Curvy Lisa trace all return together, or the candidate is rejected.
- Distinguish source-derived specifications, chosen kinematic interventions, and unproved equation-isomorphism/derivative claims.

# GrAnn → Torus Wall | Selected-contact mechanical reconstruction

**Status:** SANDBOXED mechanical carrier implemented; FULL HISTORICAL GRANN NOT RECONSTRUCTED  
**Date:** 2026-10-18  
**Browser source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`  
**Reconstruction commits:** `215f83ff9775021cd321fdcd73d5dbf7cb925f70` (constraint), `8c0aa800e7b6697e5144fdeacf70ac87ec8af36d` (drawing)  
**Reference engine:** `tools/whirligig_rq/whirligig.py`, particularly `frame_and_roll`.

## Nathan Direct source constraints

The original 3D toy is transcribed in [FINDING THE DONUT, pp. 25–27](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/FINDING%20THE%20DONUT%20(nolat).txt).

The construction specifies: GrAnn self-intersection `GrAnn_Omph` at the R-side point `i_r`; the antipodal `GrAnn_t_ipode` self-tangent; `P_ivot` simultaneously on GrAnn and `TorOuRad`; `Donomphulon` moving along `TorInCirc`; `BigRad` through the Donut center, Donomphulon and P_ivot; sphere rolling with **even multiple of GrAnn circuits per outer-torus circuit**; and Curvy Lisa written by the single constrained perpendicular elbow on the torus. The original text calls this the **3D toy version**.

**Source limitation:** The historical excerpt specifies the two special self-intersection/tangency constraints but does not provide a unique analytic parameterization of a self-intersecting Great Annulum. A great circle is therefore a partial carrier model, not the full named GrAnn. Do not invent that missing topology or claim `GrAnn_Omph=i_r` is satisfied.

## Implemented contact-driven kinematics

Let `R` be the torus major radius; `a=b` the torus tube radius and sphere radius. Let `ψ` denote the torus-centerline orbital angle. The chosen GrAnn contact-phase speed is

```text
gear = (R+a)/b    (historical even winding requires gear=2n, n positive integer)
γ(ψ) = gear · ψ
r_GrAnn_body(ψ) = (sin γ, 0, cos γ)
W(ψ) = (e_r, e_phi, e_z)
B(γ) = (r_GrAnn, t_GrAnn, n_GrAnn)
Q(ψ) = W(ψ) · B(γ)^T
P_ivot(ψ) = (R+a) e_r(ψ)             // constrained outer wall
C(ψ) = P_ivot(ψ) − b Q(ψ)r_GrAnn(ψ) // center DERIVED from wall contact
GrAnn_carrier(λ;ψ) = C(ψ)+b Q(ψ)(sin λ,0,cos λ)
Donomphulon(ψ) = (R−a) e_r(ψ)       // inner torus circumference
GrAnn_antipode = C(ψ) − b Q(ψ)r_GrAnn(ψ)
BigRad: origin ↔ P_ivot, containing Donomphulon.
```

The browser derives C from the outer-wall pivot and GrAnn body contact rather than positioning C independently and merely drawing a ring afterward. This is an explicit selected-contact kinematic constraint, although **for this particular orientation it algebraically reproduces the earlier center path**. It does *not yet* add the full source-described force/kinematic influence of an intersecting GrAnn on the R follower and composite elbow. Do not represent that incomplete part as solved.

At `a=b`, the opposite point of the selected great-circle carrier is at the inner torus circumference. That is a consequence of this degenerate equal-radius contact construction, not a proof of no-slip across the entire contact circle.

Selected-contact rolling condition per unit `ψ`:
```text
dC/dψ + ω × (b e_r) = 0;   ω=(0,0,−R/b).
```
The simultaneous GrAnn/contact conditions depend on `ψ`; the independent R/Q sweep-plane contact selection and single perpendicular elbow remain unchanged from the prior browser instrument.

## Browser diagnostics

The revised UI includes a panel named **GrAnn torus-wall coupling**, plus a 4:1 historical even-winding reference button. The sphere body-frame view shows the magenta great-circle carrier with its gold moving selected contact and blue antipode. The world/toroidal view shows the carrier, gold `P_ivot`, blue `Donomphulon`, and `BigRad`. The panel numerically reports:
- `P_ivot` deviation from outer torus implicit surface and the contact constraint;
- antipode-to-Donomphulon coincidence and inner torus wall residual;
- BigRad collinearity;

import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation
from math import gcd, lcm, floor, pi, sqrt
def inner_audit(R=1.65,b=.55,sweep=1,nsteps=3001):
    delta=R/b-1
    n=2*(floor((abs(delta)+1e-10)/2)+1)
    sig=sqrt(n*n-delta*delta)
    psi=np.linspace(0,2*pi,nsteps)
    er=np.column_stack((np.cos(psi),np.sin(psi),np.zeros_like(psi)))
    et=np.column_stack((-np.sin(psi),np.cos(psi),np.zeros_like(psi)))
    orient=(Rotation.from_rotvec(psi[:,None]*np.array([0,0,1]))
            *Rotation.from_rotvec(psi[:,None]*np.array([sig,0,delta]))).as_matrix()
    gb=np.einsum('nji,nj->ni',orient,-er)
    c=R*er
    inner=c+b*np.einsum('nij,nj->ni',orient,gb)
    outer=c-b*np.einsum('nij,nj->ni',orient,gb)
    w=sig*er+(R/b)*np.array([0,0,1])
    slip=R*et+np.cross(w,-b*er)
    deriv=np.gradient(orient,psi,axis=0,edge_order=2)
    O=deriv@np.transpose(orient,(0,2,1))
    wf=np.column_stack((O[:,2,1],O[:,0,2],O[:,1,0]))
    slipfd=R*et+np.cross(wf,-b*er)
    return dict(major=R,b=b,min_turns=n,elbow=lcm(n,sweep),sigma=sig,
                inner_error=np.linalg.norm(inner-(R-b)*er,axis=1).max(),
                outer_error=np.linalg.norm(outer-(R+b)*er,axis=1).max(),
                selected_slip=np.linalg.norm(slip,axis=1).max(),
                fd_slip=np.linalg.norm(slipfd[5:-5],axis=1).max(),
                frame_seam=np.linalg.norm(orient[0]-orient[-1]),
                net_z_sign=np.min(w[:,2]),max_x=np.max(np.abs(w[:,0])),max_y=np.max(np.abs(w[:,1])))
[inner_audit(),inner_audit(sweep=3),inner_audit(R=1.6,b=.55),inner_audit(R=1.65,b=.55,nsteps=6001)]

"""Sandboxed GrAnn minimum-return SO(3) lock.

INNER-torus-contact 3-axis rotational locking candidate, NOT the historical
self-intersecting GrAnn, NOT the full R/Q elbow mechanism, and NOT a globally
no-slip sphere/tube contact for the b=a limiting case.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from fractions import Fraction
from math import gcd, lcm, pi, sqrt
import json
import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.transform import Rotation


def exact_ratio(value):
    return value if isinstance(value, Fraction) else Fraction(str(value))


def common_return(rates):
    """Minimal positive INTEGRAL number of base torus circuits for all phases.

    A physical joint configuration requires additional SO(3), contact, branch,
    input-tangent and elbow closure checks. An arithmetic LCM is not enough.
    """
    phases = {k: exact_ratio(v) for k, v in rates.items()}
    if not phases:
        raise ValueError("At least one phase rate is required")
    duration = lcm(*(f.denominator for f in phases.values()))
    counts = {k: int(v * duration) for k, v in phases.items()}
    nonzero = [abs(n) for n in counts.values() if n]
    return {
        "base_torus_circuits": duration,
        "turns_at_return": counts,
        "lcm_of_completed_winding_counts": lcm(*nonzero) if nonzero else 0,
    }


def minimum_grann_turns(major, radius, source_periods=(1, 1),
                        require_even=True):
    """Smallest admissible even material turns > inner-contact spin offset.

    Strict inequality preserves nonzero x/y spin. R/Q sweep periods lock the
    elbow through LCM, rather than forcing the material rotor count.
    """
    M, b = exact_ratio(major), exact_ratio(radius)
    if M <= b or b <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Need torus major radius > ball/tube radius > 0")
    orders = [int(x) for x in source_periods]
    if any(x <= 0 for x in orders):
        raise ValueError("Source periods must be positive integers")
    delta = M / b - 1
    multiple = 2 if require_even else 1
    turns = multiple * (delta.numerator // (delta.denominator * multiple) + 1)
    return turns, float(delta)


def simulate(major=1.65, radius=.55, source_periods=(1, 1),
             require_even=True, samples=2401):
    n, delta = minimum_grann_turns(major, radius, source_periods, require_even)
    R, b = float(major), float(radius)
    sigma = sqrt(n*n - delta*delta)
    psi = np.linspace(0., 2*pi, samples)
    er = np.column_stack((np.cos(psi), np.sin(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    et = np.column_stack((-np.sin(psi), np.cos(psi), np.zeros_like(psi)))
    Q = (Rotation.from_rotvec(np.column_stack((np.zeros_like(psi),
                                              np.zeros_like(psi), psi)))
         * Rotation.from_rotvec(np.outer(psi,
                                        np.array([sigma, 0., delta])))).as_matrix()
    C = R * er
    contact_body = np.einsum("nji,nj->ni", Q, -er)
    wall_pivot = C + b*np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Q, contact_body)
    wall_target = (R-b)*er
    outer_pivot = (R+b)*er
    ball_antipode = C - b*np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Q, contact_body)
    omega = np.column_stack((sigma*er[:,0], sigma*er[:,1],
                             np.full(len(psi), R/b)))
    slip = R*et + np.cross(omega, -b*er)
    spin_angle = n * psi
    theta_turns = spin_angle[-1]/(2*pi)
    dQ = np.gradient(Q, psi, axis=0, edge_order=2)
    Omega = dQ @ np.swapaxes(Q, 1, 2)
    omega_fd = np.column_stack((Omega[:,2,1],Omega[:,0,2],
                                Omega[:,1,0]))
    fd_slip = R*et + np.cross(omega_fd, -b*er)
    track_distance = float(np.sum(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(contact_body, axis=0), axis=1)))
    elbow_turns = lcm(n, *[int(x) for x in source_periods])
    result = {
        "major_radius": R,
        "ball_and_tube_radius": b,
        "inner_wall_roll_ratio": R/b,
        "co_rotating_spin_offset": delta,
        "selected_rolling_wall": "INNER",
        "minimal_grann_turns": n,
        "source_phase_orders": list(source_periods),
        "lcm_locked_elbow_turns": int(elbow_turns),
        "even_winding": (n % 2 == 0),
        "radial_spin_rate": sigma,
        "angular_velocity_component_ranges": {
            axis: [float(omega[:,i].min()),float(omega[:,i].max())]
            for i,axis in enumerate(("x","y","z"))
        },
        "material_turn_count": float(theta_turns),
        "material_track_length_total": track_distance,
        "predicted_material_track_length_total": 2*pi*abs(delta),
        "one_contact_track_cycle_length": 2*pi*abs(delta)/n,
        "max_inner_contact_error": float(np.linalg.norm(wall_pivot-wall_target,axis=1).max()),
        "max_outer_pivot_error": float(np.linalg.norm(ball_antipode-outer_pivot,axis=1).max()),
        "min_omega_z": float(omega[:,2].min()),
        "max_analytic_point_slip": float(np.linalg.norm(slip,axis=1).max()),
        "max_fd_point_slip_interior": float(np.linalg.norm(fd_slip[5:-5],axis=1).max()),
        "SO3_seam_error": float(np.linalg.norm(Q[0]-Q[-1])),
        "SO3_orthogonality_error": float(np.abs(np.swapaxes(Q,1,2)@Q-np.eye(3)).max()),
    }
    return result


def check(report):
    assert report["max_inner_contact_error"] < 1e-10, "Inner wall mismatch"
    assert report["max_outer_pivot_error"] < 1e-10, "Outer antipode mismatch"
    assert report["min_omega_z"] > 0, "Sphere must roll with positive z spin at inner contact"
    assert report["max_analytic_point_slip"] < 1e-10, "Selected-point rolling fails"
    assert report["SO3_seam_error"] < 1e-10, "Orientation failed to close"
    assert report["SO3_orthogonality_error"] < 1e-10, "Frame ceased to be SO(3)"
    assert report["radial_spin_rate"] > 0, "All-axis motion missing"
    for component in ("x","y","z"):
        a,b=report["angular_velocity_component_ranges"][component]
        assert b-a > 1e-6 or (component=="z" and abs(a)>1e-6)
    assert abs(report["material_turn_count"] - report["minimal_grann_turns"]) < 1e-8
    assert report["lcm_locked_elbow_turns"] % report["minimal_grann_turns"] == 0


def main():
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--major",type=float,default=1.65)
    p.add_argument("--radius",type=float,default=.55)
    p.add_argument("--r-order",type=int,default=1)
    p.add_argument("--q-order",type=int,default=1)
    p.add_argument("--samples",type=int,default=2401)
    p.add_argument("--check",action="store_true")
    args=p.parse_args()
    out=simulate(args.major,args.radius,(args.r_order,args.q_order),
                 samples=args.samples)
    if args.check:
        check(out)
    print(json.dumps(out,indent=2))


if __name__=="__main__":
    main()

[L2]   "content": "# GrAnn / R–Q Whirligig: inner-wall rolling and minimum shared rotational lock

**Date:** 2026-10-21  
**Status:** SANDBOXED browser engineering reconstruction, repository-published, real-browser/Sites deployment not independently verified.  
**Source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in `Satobloc/HsH`.  
**User correction:** GrAnn is fundamentally rotational locking through **all three spatial axes**, with the **minimum shared return** determining the number of rotations of the single perpendicular gimbal elbow. The sphere rolls on the **inner radial surface of the torus**, not the outer one. The previously visible outward-contact spin looked backward because it was actually the wrong contact branch.

## Selected contact and direction

Let torus major radius be `R`, tube radius and sphere radius both `b=a`, orbital position `C(ψ)=R(cosψ,sinψ,0)=R e_r`, and orbit tangent `e_φ`. The two torus radial equator points are:

```text
Donomphulon = P_inner = (R-b)e_r
P_ivot      = P_outer = (R+b)e_r
r_inner     = P_inner-C = -b e_r
C'          = R e_φ
```

Nominated inner-wall no-slip requires `C' + ω × (-b e_r) = 0` per unit `ψ`, hence the **z component** of angular velocity is `ω_z=+R/b`, in the SAME physical sign as torus progression. For the old **outer** contact `r=+b e_r`, the required sign was `ω_z=-R/b`. Reversing playback alone is not an acceptable fix: switch the selected wall, contact offset, and the resulting orientation/velocity constraint together.

The earlier browser version accidentally labeled its single inner contact as both P_ivot and Donomphulon. This is corrected: P_ivot remains the **outer** circumferential point per the historical source, while Donomphulon is the **inner** selected rolling point; the diameter `2b` separates them. The material GrAnn track passes through both contact and antipode.

## Minimum even three-axis rotational lock

Write `r=R/b`, `δ=r−1`. In this deliberately defined SO(3) locking ansatz, take

```text
n = smallest positive EVEN integer strictly larger than |δ|
σ = sqrt(n²−δ²)                              (nonzero transverse spin)
u = (σ,0,δ)/n                               (unit body axis)
Q(ψ) = Rot_z(ψ) Rot_u(n ψ)
```

Then the world angular velocity per `ψ` is

```text
ω = σ cosψ e_x + σ sinψ e_y + r e_z.
```

The sphere therefore rotates through **x and y over the orbit** as well as the **positive z rolling direction**, without violating the nominated inner-wall slip constraint. Because `n` is an integer and the orbital angle makes a full turn, the complete orientation `Q(2π)=Q(0)`; the **smallest even** `n>|δ|` makes the x/y component strictly nonzero. This is a minimality statement only **within this specified constant-oblique-axis ansatz**, not proof of a globally unique minimal mechanism.

The sphere's body material contact is

```text
g_body(ψ)=Q(ψ)⁻¹(−e_r(ψ))
```

and the torus wall determines `C = P_inner - b Q g_body`. The resulting body track is a generally non-great circular GrAnn contact locus. Its historical self-intersection `GrAnn_Omph`, special antipodal self-tangency `GrAnn_t_ipode` and original R-anchor crossover **have not been reconstructed**. This lock is functional, not a claim to have recovered the exact source-described shape.

## Crossbar and elbow timing

R and Q remain independent E/W **sphere curves**. A common meridional sweep intersects both curves separately, yielding two moving body points `R(ψ)` and `Q(ψ)`. Their freely varying connector has midpoint W_obble; its one and only projecting gimbal elbow is constrained exactly perpendicular to the connector.

The current browser maps each selected input to one closed 2π sphere curve, so one full normalized sweep lap returns both source curves to their represented starting parameters. Let `m` be the selectable **integer** number of complete sweeps per torus orbit. Define

```text
elbow_turns = lcm(n,m)
theta_elbow(ψ) = elbow_turns * ψ
```

This replaces the former separate arbitrary elbow-turn slider and the ad hoc `curvature_gain*(curvature_R−curvature_Q)` phase. The single gimbal elbow intersects the actual torus wall to make Curvy Lisa. The R/Q representation may have shorter scalar periods but a complete spatial curve still carries its azimuth winding; use full curve/orientation closure, not merely scalar equality, to test return.

For `R=1.65,b=.55`: `r=3,δ=2,n=4,σ=sqrt(12)`; default m=1 gives elbow=4, while m=3 gives elbow=12. Other radii choose their own minimal-even n with a floating-point guard at integer boundaries. General source-specific fractional windings, quaternion signs, nonperiodic solutions, nontrivial holonomy and independently varying follower phases would require a more general common-return solver; these are not silently presumed solved.

## Unfiltered comparator series

The browser retains its original **14** equation adapters and adds **28** explicit scalar representatives. They are organized as:
- **11 best-known examples:** harmonic oscillator, Kepler ellipse, Maxwell plane wave, Fourier heat equation, Laplace harmonic, Schrödinger box eigenfunction, standing wave, Lorentz gamma scan, Planck spectrum, Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution, Fermi–Dirac occupation.
- **17 often overlooked examples:** Jacobi theta, Legendre, Chebyshev, Bessel J0 (40-point quadrature), Clausen Cl2 (truncated), Re Li2 (truncated), Berry curvature in a two-band Dirac model, Mathieu coefficient, KdV one-soliton profile, sine–Gordon kink, viscous Burgers shock, Morse and Lennard–Jones potentials, Kitaev chain spectrum, Pöschl–Teller potential, Fresnel C (Simpson quadrature), U(1) Wilson phase.

These category labels are **editorial** and not an objective ranking of physical importance or novelty. Every profile remains selectable independently as R or Q, with a displayed formula, chosen representative and limitations. A deterministic no-ranking pair iterator traverses every unordered pair in the selected series: 55 best-known pairs, 136 overlooked pairs, or **861 combinations across all 42**. No automated beauty/tuning selection is applied to Curvy Lisa. Some source mathematical objects are nonperiodic; **the prescribed sample parameter is periodic**, not the original soliton, kink or trajectory.

## Executed test record

All executed checks use the browser's JavaScript with a **stub DOM/canvas**, not a real graphical browser.
- Default `R=1.65,b=.55,m=1`: `n=4,` `elbow_turns=4`, nonzero `σ=3.4641`, inner contact slip residual under `3.9e−16`, full SO(3) orientation return residual under `5.3e−15`, 1,401/1,401 first-forward elbow/torus ray intersections.
- `m=3` changes the locked elbow turns automatically to 12, with no independent elbow motor field.
- All 42 profiles generated finite, matching samples at 0 and 2π. The unfiltered series controls advanced through the ordered pairs.
- Full regression with all 42 profiles in the R selector and all 42 in the Q selector: **84 configurations, 117,684 evaluated apparatus samples**, zero missing torus wall hits or E/W violations, max bar/elbow unit-dot residual `4.45e−16`, max selected inner-contact slip residual `3.85e−16`.
- The P_ivot (outer) / Donomphulon (inner) radial distance was tested as `2b=1.1` in the default reference.

**Not verified:** actual published Sites page, real browser rendering/performance, dynamic no-slip at all points in the degenerate `a=b` full contact set, complete historical GrAnn topology, general equivalence of arbitrary physics equations, or a proof that Curvy Lisa equals a derivative.

## Supersession

This replaces the earlier default **outer-wall** rolling sign, its great-circle-only GrAnn geometry, the formerly user-adjustable elbow turns/curvature-gain, and the old shortcut that identified the radius gear `(R+b)/b` as the complete GrAnn/R/Q common return. Those prior research files remain in the archive as historical records, not the current design.

Live deployment requires the site builder to replace the existing `/laboratory/whirligig/` implementation from the current HsH source and verify the new inner contact, three-axis motion, unique outer and inner markers, automatic elbow count, and entire comparator series.

**Status:** SANDBOXED / OPERATIONAL BROWSER INPUT LIBRARY (not a mathematical equivalence claim)  
**Date:** 2026-10-17  
**Browser implementation:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`  
**Implementation commit:** `0cf005a95051ce046be71a04f01c60a3a166ad1e`  
**Source engine reference:** `tools/whirligig_rq/README.md`, `whirligig.py`

## Design

Each input must provide an explicit dimensionless periodic *scalar representative* `f(λ)`, with λ ranging from zero to 2π and a periodic closed result. The instrument applies independent R and Q selection, R/Q **display** gain, and a Q sampling phase. The source's scalar value changes the spherical polar aperture through the existing bounded mapping, preserving opposite E/W hemispheres. It is **not** a universal invertible map from a field equation, metric, representation, wavefunction or solution space to a 3D curve.

Distinct input equations are mapped to the same sphere using an explicitly chosen adapter, not assumed to be isomorphic. Geometry coupling remains unchanged: independent source curves, simultaneous equal-fraction arc-length traversal, one variable-length crossbar, one perpendicular projecting elbow, minimum shared return clock, torus-wall Curvy Lisa output. The numerical comparison readout displays root-mean-square difference between the two **ungained scalar profile samples**, not an equation-isomorphism criterion or field-theory test.

## Catalog

| Code | Mathematical object | Specific selected closed representative | Epistemic scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harm_r` | synthetic harmonic R | cos(2λ)+(3/11)sin(3λ) | demonstration |
| `harm_q` | synthetic harmonic Q | sin(3λ)+(1/6)cos(5λ) | demonstration |
| `u1_phase` | U(1) relative phase | Re exp(i[λ+0.25 sin(2λ)]) | fixed-reference gauge phase; **not gauge invariant** |
| `su2_character` | SU(2) fundamental character | ½Tr diag(exp(iφ),exp(−iφ))=cos φ, φ=2λ+0.35sin λ | group path only; not an SU(2) Yang–Mills field |
| `su3_character` | SU(3) fundamental character | (1+2cos φ)/3, φ=2λ+0.25sin(3λ) | diagonal group path; not QCD dynamics or a Wilson loop |
| `gw_plus` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h₊/h₀=cos(2λ) | TT-gauge wave component, phase-normalized |
| `gw_cross` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h×/h₀=sin(2λ) | TT-gauge component, not gauge-independent complete spacetime |
| `schwarz_orbit` | Schwarzschild timelike circular geodesic | x/r₀=cos λ at equatorial r₀=8M | coordinate x projection, λ is **orbital phase**, not proper time |
| `schwarz_lapse` | Schwarzschild metric lapse | 10[√(1−2M/r(λ))−√(1−2/8)], r/M=8+1.5cos λ | prescribed radial scan, **not a geodesic** |
| `kerr_drag` | Kerr equatorial ZAMO frame dragging | ω(r)=2Ma/(r³+a²r+2Ma²); a/M=0.5; r/M=8+cos λ; f=ω(r)/ω(8M)−1 | prescribed radial scan, **not an orbit** |
| `qm_rabi` | two-level Schrödinger solution | H=(ℏΩ/2)σₓ, Pₑ=sin²(λ/2); 2Pₑ−1=−cos λ | ideal resonant system, λ=Ωt |
| `qm_spin` | spin-½ Larmor precession | H=(ℏω/2)σz; ⟨σₓ⟩=cos λ | ideal initial +x state, λ=ωt |
| `qm_coherent` | quantum harmonic oscillator coherent state | ⟨x⟩/A=cos(3λ) | selected expectation value, ωt=3λ |
| `qm_interference` | coherent two-energy-state superposition | interference factor cos(ΔEt/ℏ)=cos(3λ) | phase interference factor only, not the full probability density |

**Important gauge distinction:** the trace of a chosen group element is a class function under conjugation, but these chosen paths are *not* derived from a gauge connection integrated along physical closed spacetime loops. Do not present them as gauge-invariant Yang–Mills Wilson-loop measurements or solutions to the gauge field equations.

**Important GR distinction:** a selected metric is an exact gravitational solution in its stated idealized setting, but sampling one metric component along an arbitrarily imposed periodic radius does not automatically yield a geodesic or solve a new Einstein field equation. ```bash

Two independent specs are supplied as `R` and `Q` in a JSON file. Every adapter records its representation choice, physical units remain those of the caller, and original numerical coordinates are preserved apart from the sphere carrier. **No universal faithful parameterization exists for arbitrary symbolic equations without specifying a solution branch, observables, and a parameter interval.** Accordingly the tool supports:

| Kind | Example | What is done | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `0.5*cos(2*t)+0.1*sin(5*t)` | Scalar function encoded reversibly in sphere latitude; azimuth is `t` | Functions must be finite on the interval. Periodicity tested, not fabricated |

## Exact selected-contact rolling law

Let the torus have major radius `R` and tube/minor radius `a`. Let the sphere have radius `b<a` and travel on a center circle of radius

\[
\rho=R+a-b,\qquad C(\psi)=\rho(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0).
\]

The selected contact on the outer equator is

\[
P(\psi)=(R+a)(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0)=C+b\mathbf e_r.
\]

For rolling without slip at this **isolated chosen point**, the laboratory angular velocity obeys

\[
\boldsymbol\omega=-\frac{\rho}{b}\dot\psi\mathbf e_z,
\quad \dot C+\boldsymbol\omega\times(b\mathbf e_r)=0.
\]

Define the Great-Annulum body contact angle

\[
\gamma(\psi)=\frac{R+a}{b}\psi.
\]

Let `W(ψ)` be the orthonormal world frame `(e_r,e_phi,e_z)` and `B(γ)` the body-frame triad `(r_annulus,t_annulus,n_annulus)`. The **actual orientation** is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=W(\psi)B(\gamma)^T\in SO(3).
\]

`P=C+Q b r_annulus` is tested point by point. A whole-revolution orientation closes when the contact gearing `g=(R+a)/b` is integral. The historical *even multiple* condition is satisfied by choosing `g=6` by default:

- `R=1.6`, `a=0.55`, `b=(R+a)/6=0.358333...`, `rho=1.791666...`.
- A five-point fourth-order finite-difference check of the no-slip velocity converges to zero under grid refinement, while the underlying analytic identity is exact.
- With `b=a` (the originally described limiting sphere size), ball and torus tube share a nonisolated meridional contact set. The program **can render that mode** when `allow_degenerate_contact=true`, but explicitly does **not certify unique-contact rolling**; imposing no slip at every contact point would be overconstrained.

The input R endpoint is acted on by an internal `Ry(pitch)` hinge; the Q endpoint by an independent `Rx(roll)` hinge. Their axes are perpendicular **by exact construction**. Hinge angles use integer-period rotations with optional sinusoidal modulations. The sphere's physical `SO(3)` rotation is separate from these **internal coordinate controls**. The two endpoints are transported into the lab frame with the exact `Q(ψ)` orientation above.

`W_obble=(R_world+Q_world)/2` is the connector midpoint, and `W_iggle` is the plane perpendicular to the connector. A minimal-rotation Bishop frame supplies its two orthonormal axes. The pen rotates in that plane. Its **first forward** intersection with the torus is found by solving the torus implicit quartic and selecting its smallest positive real root, not by approximating a torus-looking curve.

Optional `align_source_anchors` rotates one source curve **by a single rigid SO(3) alignment**, mapping an off-phase point and tangent on Q to a point and tangent on R. This is a transparent representation intervention, **not an isomorphism proof**, and it is logged with the alignment matrix and both residuals.

An optional Bishop-holonomy correction adjusts the pen's phase around the full circuit. The correction is recorded, and may be disabled: the program does not silently assert that an uncompensated trace must close.

The `--search` scan varies **four even annulum gear ratios**, pen rotation rates, and independently chosen gimbal rotations. It preserves **all sixty** ranked candidates in `ranked_candidates.json`, including failures; it also saves the selected best candidate's full reproducible arrays, metrics and precision geometry figures. {"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/update_file","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","path":"tools/whirligig_rq/README.md","sha":"1d4b7161fb7ab6a0a2b6d3c935ad9a8a1431220b","content":"# Whirligig R/Q Engine: rolling sphere, gimbals, two equations, Curvy_Lisa

> **2026-10-21 mechanism distinction:** The current **browser Whirligig** (see `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`) uses the **INNER torus radial surface** as the selected rolling contact, positive same-direction spin, a minimum even **three-axis GrAnn** SO(3) rotational lock, and `LCM(GrAnn turns, R/Q sweep turns)` to drive the unique gimbal elbow. See [the current technical contract](GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md). The standalone [grann_rotational_lock.py](grann_rotational_lock.py) has been updated to that branch. **The older full R/Q solver `whirligig.py` described below still uses the separate OUTER-wall selected-contact branch and its own original gimbal/pen implementation. Its results are not proof that the new browser coupling is implemented there.** Do not silently mix the branches or assume that a GitHub update deploys ChatGPT Sites.

**Version:** experimental v0.1, 11 October 2026  
**Status:** SANDBOXED engineering reconstruction. Mathematical/procedural tool, not a proof of a physical isomorphism.

This is a working, configurable **two-equation** mechanism drawn from the historical R/Q / Great Annulum / W_obble / W_iggle / Curvy_Lisa description, together with the archived continuous Navier–Stokes Whirligig Python predecessor. It generates equation curves on a sphere, carries them inside a rolling ball constrained by a torus, uses two genuine orthogonal gimbal hinges to select curve endpoints, constructs the R–Q crossbar and a rotation-minimizing plane perpendicular to it, then intersects a rotating pen ray with the **actual torus quartic** to generate Curvy_Lisa.

**Source provenance:**
- [*FINDING THE DONUT*, pp. 23–27](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/_AUTO_EXTRACTED_TEXT/FINDING%20THE%20DONUT%20(nolat).txt), March 2026.
- [*THE_WHIRLIGIG*](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/HsH-SAT%20Roundup%203/THE_WHIRLIGIG.txt).
- [Existing continuous NS Whirligig source](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/continuous_ns_whirligig_solver%20%281%29.py), independently specifying the sphere's moving contact frame, Bishop connector, torus-wall ray casting, and a Navier–Stokes test setup.
- [*WHIRLIGIG -- REDEFINING SUCCESS*](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/WHIRLIGIG%20--%20REDEFINING%20SUCCESS.txt): a **constructive existence** goal for a back hallway, not a demand for one unique universal derivative.
- Original source distinguishes 3D mechanical toy geometry from actual four-dimensional systems. This code does too.

## Run

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python whirligig.py --input example_equations.json --out output --search
python plot_mechanics.py --input example_equations.json --out mechanics_snapshot.png --gif rolling_whirligig.gif
python validate_mapping.py --input example_equations.json --out mapping_validation.json
python -m pytest -q
```

`--input` is optional: a two-harmonic-pair demonstration is built in.

## Input equation adapters

Two independent specs are supplied as `R` and `Q` in a JSON file. Every adapter records its representation choice, physical units remain those of the caller, and original numerical coordinates are preserved apart from the sphere carrier. **No universal faithful parameterization exists for arbitrary symbolic equations without specifying a solution branch, observables, and a parameter interval.** Accordingly the tool supports:

| Kind | Example | What is done | Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| `expression` | `0.5*cos(2*t)+0.1*sin(5*t)` | Scalar function encoded reversibly in sphere latitude; azimuth is `t` | Functions must be finite on the interval. Periodicity tested, not fabricated |
| `parametric` | `{"components":["cos(t)","sin(t)"]}` | 2D trajectory via reversible stereographic embedding; 3D trajectory radialized with magnitude preserved separately | 3D radial projection loses magnitude in its sphere output |
| `implicit` | `x*x/2.25+y*y-1=0` written as `x*x/2.25+y*y-1` | Extract largest closed real zero contour and stereographically lift | Grid approximate; must set bounding box and a suitable branch |
| `ode` | `{"rhs":["y","-x"],"initial":[1,0]}` | Numerically integrates a 1–3 dimensional ODE and embeds the path | May not close; only specified initial-value solution is represented |
| `sampled` | `{"path":"path.csv"}` | Arclength-resamples a closed 2D/3D numeric curve | Intended for PDE/GR/field equations solved upstream; refuses open CSV curves |

Expression parsing is AST-restricted: arithmetic and common NumPy scalar mathematical functions only. No `eval()`, attribute access, user code import, or arbitrary shell expression execution.

For a PDE, differential geometry equation, non-Euclidean metric, or symbolic Schwarzschild geodesic, **first choose a solution and chart** and pass the resulting parametric/CSV path. This prevents smuggling an arbitrary metric into a falsely universal polar-projection routine. Keep the full source equation and domain as metadata outside the low-dimensional carrier.

## Exact selected-contact rolling law

Let the torus have major radius `R` and tube/minor radius `a`. Let the sphere have radius `b<a` and travel on a center circle of radius

\[
\rho=R+a-b,\qquad C(\psi)=\rho(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0).
\]

The selected contact on the outer equator is

\[
P(\psi)=(R+a)(\cos\psi,\sin\psi,0)=C+b\mathbf e_r.
\]

For rolling without slip at this **isolated chosen point**, the laboratory angular velocity obeys

\[
\boldsymbol\omega=-\frac{\rho}{b}\dot\psi\mathbf e_z,
\quad \dot C+\boldsymbol\omega\times(b\mathbf e_r)=0.
\]

Define the Great-Annulum body contact angle

\[
\gamma(\psi)=\frac{R+a}{b}\psi.
\]

Let `W(ψ)` be the orthonormal world frame `(e_r,e_phi,e_z)` and `B(γ)` the body-frame triad `(r_annulus,t_annulus,n_annulus)`. The **actual orientation** is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=W(\psi)B(\gamma)^T\in SO(3).
\]

`P=C+Q b r_annulus` is tested point by point. A whole-revolution orientation closes when the contact gearing `g=(R+a)/b` is integral. The historical *even multiple* condition is satisfied by choosing `g=6` by default:

- `R=1.6`, `a=0.55`, `b=(R+a)/6=0.358333...`, `rho=1.791666...`.
- A five-point fourth-order finite-difference check of the no-slip velocity converges to zero under grid refinement, while the underlying analytic identity is exact.
- With `b=a` (the originally described limiting sphere size), ball and torus tube share a nonisolated meridional contact set. The program **can render that mode** when `allow_degenerate_contact=true`, but explicitly does **not certify unique-contact rolling**; imposing no slip at every contact point would be overconstrained.

## Gimbal, connector and pen

The input R endpoint is acted on by an internal `Ry(pitch)` hinge; the Q endpoint by an independent `Rx(roll)` hinge. Their axes are perpendicular **by exact construction**. Hinge angles use integer-period rotations with optional sinusoidal modulations. The sphere's physical `SO(3)` rotation is separate from these **internal coordinate controls**. The two endpoints are transported into the lab frame with the exact `Q(ψ)` orientation above.

`W_obble=(R_world+Q_world)/2` is the connector midpoint, and `W_iggle` is the plane perpendicular to the connector. A minimal-rotation Bishop frame supplies its two orthonormal axes. The pen rotates in that plane. Its **first forward** intersection with the torus is found by solving the torus implicit quartic and selecting its smallest positive real root, not by approximating a torus-looking curve.

Optional `align_source_anchors` rotates one source curve **by a single rigid SO(3) alignment**, mapping an off-phase point and tangent on Q to a point and tangent on R. This is a transparent representation intervention, **not an isomorphism proof**, and it is logged with the alignment matrix and both residuals.

An optional Bishop-holonomy correction adjusts the pen's phase around the full circuit. The correction is recorded, and may be disabled: the program does not silently assert that an uncompensated trace must close.

## Results and automatic smoothness search

The `--search` scan varies **four even annulum gear ratios**, pen rotation rates, and independently chosen gimbal rotations. It preserves **all sixty** ranked candidates in `ranked_candidates.json`, including failures; it also saves the selected best candidate's full reproducible arrays, metrics and precision geometry figures. The ranking favors:

- valid mechanical contact, SO(3) orientation and torus quartic intersections;
- nondegenerate sphere/tube clearance;
- both input-equation closures and full orientation closure;
- C¹ seam closure, low curvature variation, low curvature percentile, low high-frequency Fourier tail.

These smoothness thresholds are **engineering filters**, not physical selection laws. C² seam mismatch is reported separately, and smooth candidates must not be mistaken for solutions to the source equations on the other side of their chosen projections. Explicit held-out source-equation residual tests are required before a proposed back hallway is accepted.

For the supplied synthetic two-harmonic pair with independently aligned anchors:

| Diagnostic | Observed |
|---|---:|
| selected contact velocity (analytic) | `0.0` |
| selected contact velocity, 128 samples | `2.14823e-4` |
| selected contact velocity, 256 samples | `1.34990e-5` |
| selected contact velocity, 512 samples | `8.44822e-7` |
| ball-frame closure | `1.73e-15` |
| torus implicit residual | `8.53e-14` |
| Curvy_Lisa positional seam | `8.55e-16` |
| C¹ seam (tangent difference) | `0.00117` |
| R anchor point and tangent gaps | `2.89e-17`, `1.42e-16` |
| response to +1% R amplitude | `0.00287` RMS output shift |
| response to +1% Q amplitude | `0.00903` RMS output shift |

The tests include intentionally nonperiodic inputs and nonintegral rolling gear, both of which must fail the relevant closure checks. Thirteen automated tests passed in the first checked build.

## Files

- `whirligig.py`: generalized two-equation 3D mechanical engine, parsers, closure checks, finite-clearance rolling, search.
- `ui4d.py`: separate, exact six-plane `SO(4)` Universal Indicatrix representation using `y(s)=r(s)R(s)x0`; **not yet coupled to 3D rigid-ball mechanics**.
- `plot_mechanics.py`: precision-drawn sphere/gimbal/annulum/connector/pen figures and optional GIF.
- `validate_mapping.py`: finite-difference grid convergence and independent source-equation perturbations.
- `test_whirligig.py`: 11 regression/negative tests.
- `example_equations.json`: two independent scalar formula inputs with optional anchor alignment.
- `example_ode_vs_implicit.json`: harmonic oscillator versus an ellipse equation.
- `example_historical_limit.json`: equal-radius historical rendering with explicit degeneracy diagnostic.
- `demo/`, `aligned_demo/`: retained 60-run candidate sweeps and selected-best numerical arrays and plots.

## Remaining work

1. **Historic Great Annulum:** source says a self-intersecting annulum with antipodal self-tangent, but does not give its analytic curve. This release makes an explicit great-circle choice. Recover and test the intended self-intersecting annulum before calling this exact historical reconstruction.
2. **4D rolling/gimbal lift:** the sphere/torus apparatus implements the explicitly described **3D toy version**. The separate `ui4d.py` provides its honest SO(4) representation layer, not a fabricated four-dimensional contact geometry.
3. **Joint dynamical derivations:** embedding an equation into a polar curve is not equivalent to deriving an invariant relation from two different equations. Implement input-specific residual or observable maps and compare against held-out predictions in both sectors.
4. **Continuous optimization:** current candidate search is discrete, not a variational or interval-arithmetic global search. Upgrade with constrained smooth optimization, holonomy loops, singularity branch resolution, and complexity/energy budgets.
5. **Metrology and units:** use dimensionless toy geometry until source physical scales and constraints are specified. Do not import GR coefficients into an assumed definition of the engine.

**Research handling:** mathematical apparatus should be assessed independently of speculative framing; no physical claim is inferred from geometric representability alone. ## Whirligig update: rolling corrected

The revised mechanical version is now committed to `Satobloc/HsH`.

**The ball now rolls against the inner torus wall**, with the required physical spin in the same direction as its orbital motion. This is a change to the contact geometry and rotation equations, not simply an animation reversal.

The default configuration now uses a minimum four-turn, three-axis GrAnn lock. The elbow's revolutions are computed from that lock and the R/Q sweep cycle rather than controlled by an independent slider.

The first executable checks passed:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Inner-wall rolling slip residual | \(3.9\times10^{-16}\) |
| Full orientation return error | \(5.2\times10^{-15}\) |
| Elbow–torus intersections | 1,401 / 1,401 |
| Default GrAnn / elbow winding | 4 / 4 |
| Three R/Q sweeps | 12 locked elbow rotations |

The equal-diameter ball/tube contact is still a limiting geometric construction. These checks verify the nominated inner contact, not global no-slip over an extended contact region.

**[Updated Whirligig source](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html)**

## Comparator library expanded

The updated application now contains **42 equation profiles**: the original 14, plus 28 additional examples covering classical mechanics, field equations, statistical mechanics, special functions, potentials, solitons, and band geometry.

Two new discovery series are available:

- **Best-known series:** 11 familiar equations, including Kepler, Maxwell, Fourier heat flow, Schrödinger, and Planck.
- **Often overlooked series:** 17 less frequently demonstrated examples, including Jacobi theta, Bessel, Clausen, dilogarithms, Berry curvature, Mathieu, KdV, and sine–Gordon.

Instead of selecting pairs according to whether they produce appealing Curvy Lisa traces, the **Next pair** control walks through the series in deterministic order. The combined library offers **861 unique unordered pairs**, without aesthetic filtering.

The mathematical descriptions distinguish exact solutions from sampled observables, coefficient functions, approximate special-function evaluations, and periodic scans of otherwise nonperiodic solutions.

**[Expanded equation library in HsH](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html)**

## Saved and verified

The revised source, mathematical specification, equation library, and integration instructions have been saved to GitHub and independently read back.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html" title="Whirligig application"/> | Updated interactive mechanism and 42-equation selectors |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md" title="Updated GrAnn specification"/> | Inner-wall rolling derivation, three-axis locking, minimum return and elbow gearing |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/tools/whirligig_rq/grann_rotational_lock.py" title="Python rotational-lock prototype"/> | Updated inner-contact numerical model |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/EQUATION_LIBRARY.md" title="Equation library documentation"/> | All comparator series, assumptions and sampling limitations |
| <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md" title="Website integration instructions"/> | Builder handoff and live-site verification requirements |

The expanded JavaScript regression ran **84 configurations totaling 117,684 geometry samples**, with no missing torus-wall intersections, no east/west hemisphere violations, and perpendicularity and selected-contact residuals at floating-point precision.

An independent Python numerical check also confirmed positive inner-wall rolling spin, nonzero rotational components through all three axes, and full orientation closure. The standalone updated Python CLI itself has not yet been executed separately.

One distinction is preserved in the documentation: the older full Python R/Q engine still models an **outer-wall** contact branch. It has not been silently converted or represented as equivalent to this new implementation.

**Current status:** Saved in HsH and numerically checked. The original GrAnn self-intersection and full physical-contact behavior remain open research questions. Live Glass Sausage Factory deployment and graphical browser testing remain unverified.
