[L2]   "content": "name: Build conversation viewer catalog

# Workflow edits intentionally trigger a self-test so generation and UI changes are validated on main.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    # GLASS is a separate public repository, so an hourly sweep provides eventual
    # convergence even when no HsH commit occurs at the same time.
    - cron: '23 * * * *'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      # Actual file contents determine whether a new source is JSON.
      # Trigger immediately for all extensions, not only .json/.txt.
      - 'DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/**'
      - 'LIVE CONVOS/**'
      - 'indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer.py'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py'
      - 'tools/build_viewer_body_search.py'
      - 'tools/discover_external_conversations.py'
      - 'tools/conversation_json_sniff.py'
      - 'tools/date_conversation_exports.py'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/EXTERNAL_CONVERSATIONS.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.js'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.html'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.css'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/landmarks.json'
      - '.github/workflows/build-conversation-viewer.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: conversation-viewer-catalog
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip conversation-viewer]') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Checkout public GLASS archive for Viewer discovery
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25
          ref: main
          path: _viewer_external/GLASS
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Validate viewer JavaScript
        run: |
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/viewer.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/mersearch/reader.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/catalog_body_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

      - name: Discover eligible public cross-repo conversations
        run: |
          python tools/discover_external_conversations.py \
            --hsh-root . \
            --external-root _viewer_external/GLASS \
            --external-repository Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 \
            --output CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json

      - name: Build compact conversation catalog
        run: python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py

      - name: Build cross-conversation full-text search index
        run: |
          python tools/build_viewer_body_search.py --glass-root _viewer_external/GLASS
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          root=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search')
          meta=json.loads((root/'meta.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          catalog=json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert set(meta['conversation_ids']) == {c['id'] for c in catalog['conversations']}, 'body index/catalog mismatch'
          assert list(root.glob('*.json')), 'no body search index output'
          PY

      - name: Validate generated catalog, public discovery, source paths, curation and landmarks
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path

          p = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert data['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(data['conversations'], list)
          assert data['conversations'], 'viewer catalog is empty'
          ids = [x['id'] for x in data['conversations']]
          paths = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations']]
          assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), 'duplicate viewer ids'
          assert len(paths) == len(set(paths)), 'duplicate source paths'
          from tools.conversation_json_sniff import is_json_document_candidate
          assert all(
              x.get('external') or is_json_document_candidate(Path(x['path']))
              for x in data['conversations']
          ), 'catalog contains non-JSON first-party source'
          missing_paths = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations'] if not x.get('external') and not Path(x['path']).is_file()]
          assert not missing_paths, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths: {missing_paths}'

          for manifest_path in [
              Path('indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'),
              Path('indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'),
          ]:
              manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
              assert isinstance(manifest.get('records'), list), f'invalid conversation manifest: {manifest_path}'

          cp = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          curation = json.loads(cp.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert curation['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(curation['rules'], list)

          manual_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/EXTERNAL_CONVERSATIONS.json')
          manual = json.loads(manual_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert manual['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(manual['conversations'], list)

          discovered_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json')
          discovered = json.loads(discovered_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert discovered['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(discovered['conversations'], list)
          assert discovered['source_repository'] == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
          assert 'HSH_RESOURCES' not in json.dumps(discovered), 'private resource identity leaked into public discovery'
          assert discovered['stats']['recognized'] >= discovered['stats']['discovered_added']

          known_ids = set(ids)
          for item in manual['conversations']:
              assert item['id'] in known_ids, f"registered external conversation missing from catalog: {item['id']}"
          for item in discovered['conversations']:
              assert item['id'] in known_ids, f"discovered public conversation missing from catalog: {item['id']}"

          glass = [x for x in data['conversations'] if x.get('source_repository') == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25']
          assert glass, 'no public GLASS conversations reached Viewer catalog'
          assert all(x.get('external') for x in glass)

          for convo in data['conversations']:
              if convo.get('curated'):
                  curated_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER') / convo['raw_url']
                  derived = json.loads(curated_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
                  assert derived['derived_view'] is True
                  assert derived['source_viewer_id'] == convo['id']
                  assert len(derived['messages']) == convo['message_count']

          lp = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/landmarks.json')
          landmarks = json.loads(lp.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert landmarks['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(landmarks['landmarks'], list)
          known = {x['id']: x for x in data['conversations']}
          for item in landmarks['landmarks']:
              cid = item.get('conversation_id')
              assert cid in known, f"unknown or hidden landmark conversation: {item}"
              assert isinstance(item.get('message'), int) and item['message'] > 0, f"invalid landmark message: {item}"
              assert item['message'] <= known[cid]['message_count'], f"landmark beyond conversation length: {item}"
              assert isinstance(item.get('label'), str) and item['label'].strip(), f"invalid landmark label: {item}"
          print(data['counts'])
          print(data['curation'])
          print(f"manual_external={len(manual['conversations'])}")
          print(f"glass_discovery_stats={discovered['stats']}")
          print(f"glass_viewer_entries={len(glass)}")
          print(f"landmarks={len(landmarks['landmarks'])}")
          PY

      - name: Commit generated viewer data and source manifests
        run: |
          git config user.name 'HsH Conversation Viewer Bot'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'

          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
            # Rebuild from the newest public inputs each time so concurrent work cannot
            # strand or silently overwrite otherwise-valid generated Viewer data.
            git fetch origin main
            git reset --hard origin/main
            git -C _viewer_external/GLASS fetch origin main
            git -C _viewer_external/GLASS reset --hard origin/main

            python tools/discover_external_conversations.py \
              --hsh-root . \
              --external-root _viewer_external/GLASS \
              --external-repository Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 \
              --output CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json
            python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py
            python tools/build_viewer_body_search.py --glass-root _viewer_external/GLASS

            python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          data = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          missing = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations'] if not x.get('external') and not Path(x['path']).is_file()]
          assert not missing, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths after race rebuild: {missing}'
          for p in [Path('indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'), Path('indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json')]:
              manifest = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
              assert isinstance(manifest.get('records'), list), f'invalid refreshed manifest: {p}'
          discovered = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert discovered['source_repository'] == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
          assert 'HSH_RESOURCES' not in json.dumps(discovered)
          assert any(x.get('source_repository') == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25' for x in data['conversations'])
          PY

            WATCH='CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'
            if ! git status --porcelain -- $WATCH | grep -q .; then
              echo 'Conversation viewer generated data, public discovery and manifests already current.'
              exit 0
            fi

            git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json
            git commit -m '[skip conversation-viewer] Refresh Viewer data, GLASS discovery and manifests'
            if git push origin HEAD:main; then
              exit 0
            fi

            echo "Push race on attempt ${attempt}; rebuilding from latest public inputs." >&2
            sleep 2
          done

          echo 'Conversation viewer refresh could not win a push race after 4 attempts.' >&2
          exit 1
",

[L2]   "content": "# Glass Sausage Factory — editorial + visual system

**Status:** ACTIVE public-site presentation guidance  
**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive  
**Authority:** presentation/editorial infrastructure only; theory status remains controlled by BEDROCK and source-specific surfaces.

## Editorial posture

The site should be **curious, exact, confident about what exists, and restrained about what it means**.

Avoid a default posture of apology, self-deprecation, or defensive throat-clearing. SAT/H(s)H can be presented as an unusual open research program worth examining without either underselling it or implying validation that has not occurred.

The preferred rhythm is:

> **interesting object → what it says/does → why it matters here → source/status**

not:

> **warning → disclaimer → warning → interesting object**

Caveats remain important, but they should normally appear as concise metadata, status chips, provenance notes, or a compact research-status panel rather than dominating the emotional voice of the page.

### Voice

Prefer:

- `active research program`
- `current construction`
- `historical formulation`
- `open question`
- `comparison target`
- `structural resonance`
- `direct constraint`
- `source recovered`
- `under active mathematical review`
- `relationship not established`

Use sparingly or avoid as default framing:

- `just a pet theory`
- `not a victory`
- `mere resemblance`
- repeated `this does not prove...` constructions
- red-alert styling for ordinary uncertainty
- language that sounds embarrassed by speculative or exploratory work merely because it is exploratory

When a stronger caution is actually needed, state it plainly and locally.

## Research-status copy

A compact standing status block may say:

> **Research status** — SAT/H(s)H is an active research program with a public development record. The archive includes foundational premises, historical formulations, current reconstruction, mathematical and computational work, failed branches, and results at different stages of review. Source and status travel with the material.

This replaces long defensive caveat blocks as the normal front-door treatment.

## In the News

### Editorial purpose

`In the News` is a rotating window onto external scientific results that are interesting to place beside SAT/H(s)H work.

The section is **not** restricted to results already expected by the project. It may include:

- measurements that directly constrain a live SAT/H(s)H idea;
- results that resemble or illuminate a structural motif being explored;
- findings that make an old SAT/H(s)H conversation newly interesting to revisit;
- apparently contradictory results that sharpen a test;
- genuinely eyebrow-raising observations with no established relationship yet, when the juxtaposition itself is intellectually useful.

The site should not flatten these categories into `evidence for SAT`.

### Preferred heading language

Good options include:

- **In the News — New results at the edges of the map**
- **In the News — Results, constraints, and curious touchpoints**
- **In the News — What caught our attention**

Avoid the older defensive heading `Signals worth testing—not victories to announce.`

### Card anatomy

Each news card should expose:

1. **External result** — concise factual headline and source/date.
2. **Why it caught our attention** — one or two readable sentences.
3. **Related SAT/H(s)H exploration** — direct link(s) to the relevant conversation, paper, workspace, historical source, or current programme.
4. **Relationship** — one compact typed label.

Recommended relationship vocabulary:

- `direct constraint`
- `comparison target`
- `structural resonance`
- `phenomenology context`
- `historical revisit`
- `potentially relevant — relationship open`
- `tension / possible counterevidence`

A relationship label is descriptive, not a score.

### Rotation

The public presentation should rotate a small set of current cards while retaining a browseable archive. Rotation should not erase chronology or make older cards impossible to find.

Useful display behavior:

- 3 cards visible on desktop / 1 primary card on narrow screens;
- rotate or reshuffle periodically from entries with `display_status=featured`;
- mix freshness with variety rather than showing only the newest item;
- expose stable source and related-project links on every card;
- keep older noteworthy cards available under `More from the news archive`.

The existing copypasta-news material is a first-class mining source for candidates. Workers should recover the external source when possible rather than treating pasted headlines as sufficient provenance.

## Quotable Nathan / Quotable LLM

The quote streams should feel like marginalia from an active intellectual workshop, not testimonials.

Use a mix of:

- vivid/funny/lay-readable lines;
- conceptual compression;
- mathematical observations;
- epistemic rules;
- corrections and moments of model-building;
- historically revealing lines.

A quote may be skeptical, corrective, playful, or unfinished. It need not advertise the theory.

Nathan and LLM streams remain visually and provenance-distinct.

## Visual direction

### Overall character

Move away from `cyber-neon science startup` toward:

> **observatory notebook + museum research plate + contemporary scientific editorial**

The interface can stay dark and cinematic, but source material should feel physical, readable, and archival rather than glowing inside a generic tech aesthetic.

### Working palette

Use these as starting tokens, not immutable branding:

```css
:root {
  --bg-deep: #111416;
  --bg-panel: #181D20;
  --bg-raised: #20262A;
  --paper: #E9E4DA;
  --paper-warm: #D8D0C2;
  --ink: #ECE9E1;
  --ink-dark: #202427;
  --muted: #A5AAA7;
  --line: #343C40;
  --copper: #B98755;
  --mineral-teal: #6F9F9B;
  --night-blue: #7388A4;
  --slate-violet: #8B8098;
  --brick: #A8685F;
}
```

The key change is **lower saturation and broader material range**. Teal/copper can remain recognizable accents, but they should no longer do all the visual work.

### Semantic accent use

- **Copper / warm ochre** — history, provenance, notebook/archive material.
- **Mineral teal** — live/current internal work and navigation.
- **Night blue** — external science, news, observational/experimental material.
- **Slate violet** — concepts, quotations, interpretive/theory material.
- **Brick** — actual conflicts, failed checks, or warnings that deserve attention; not ordinary uncertainty.
- **Warm paper** — PDFs, notebook pages, equations, source extracts, archival plates.

Status should never rely on color alone; pair it with explicit text.

## Visual hierarchy

### Hero

Prefer one real project visual, notebook image, diagram, or strong thumbnail as the hero anchor rather than a generic abstract orbit graphic. The visual may change periodically.

Until a suitable supplied image is selected, keep the hero visually restrained rather than inventing decorative pseudo-scientific geometry.

### Scientific plates

Diagrams, scanned notebook pages, plots, and PDF pages should often sit on a light/warm `paper` field inside the dark site. This gives technical material a natural reading surface and distinguishes source objects from interface chrome.

### Image-led cards

News, podcast, document, history, and featured-work cards should accept a 16:9 or 4:3 image/thumbnail with:

- preserved aspect ratio;
- optional focal point for responsive crops;
- concise caption;
- source/credit;
- descriptive alt text;
- role (`hero`, `thumbnail`, `diagram`, `source-scan`, `portrait`, `news-external`, etc.).

Do not overcrop diagrams or notebook pages merely to force visual uniformity.

### Quotes

Quotes should generally be spacious serif typography with small provenance metadata, not boxed testimonial cards. A Nathan line and an LLM line can share a region but should be unmistakably labeled.

### Current Work

Prefer a living research map or grouped work-front grid over three generic equal-weight cards. Visually distinguish:

- foundational/current theory state;
- live sandbox construction;
- mathematical/formal work;
- archive/provenance reconstruction;
- public-access/documentation work.

### In the News

News should feel editorial rather than alarm-like:

- source/date above headline;
- thumbnail when available;
- `Why it caught our attention` in ordinary prose;
- one compact relationship chip;
- direct project exploration link visually adjacent to the source link.

## Typography

Keep a two-register system:

- editorial serif for display headings and pull quotes (`Georgia`, `Iowan Old Style`, or another dependable serif when available);
- clean system sans for body/navigation/metadata;
- monospace only for provenance IDs, equations-as-text, paths, hashes, and technical metadata.

Avoid turning the entire project into either a faux-academic journal or a developer dashboard.

## Motion

Use restrained motion only where it communicates structure:

- gentle quote/news rotation;
- subtle image crossfade;
- hover/source-reveal states;
- optional diagram sequence where the actual geometry benefits.

Avoid constant orbital animation, glowing particles, parallax for its own sake, or effects that imply simulation/measurement when they are decorative.

## Incoming thumbnails and visuals

Nathan will supply thumbnails and visuals incrementally. Preserve each supplied asset's identity and intended context.

For every site asset, record where practical:

- source filename / origin;
- caption;
- credit/authorship;
- date or historical period;
- alt text;
- allowed roles;
- focal/crop note;
- whether it is source evidence, model illustration, generated art, podcast art, or decorative material.

Do not silently treat generated illustration as documentary imagery.

## Design test

A page should pass this simple test:

> If all warning-red boxes disappeared, would the reader still understand what is historical, current, tentative, external, and verified from the labels, source links, and structure alone?

If not, the information architecture needs work. Color and disclaimers should reinforce the epistemic structure, not carry it by themselves.

[L2]   "content": "# Glass Sausage Factory — Writing & Voice Guide

**Purpose:** help anyone writing or revising public-site copy sound recognizably like Nathan without turning the prose into a mannerism generator.

This is a **site-specific application guide**, not a replacement for the core voice models. The public site sits between several registers: museum educator, technical explainer, archive guide, working scientist, autobiographical host, and—occasionally—slightly amused person standing next to the display case.

The controlling principle is simple:

> **Write as though Nathan is present with the reader, guiding attention rather than merely delivering copy.**

The site should feel authored, inhabited, and aware of the reader’s position. It should not feel like institutional web copy with a few Nathanisms sprinkled over it.

---

## 1. Voice-model sources

Use the following voice models from the `HSH_RESOURCES` repository. These are the current v8.0 generation; older combined models live under that directory’s `HISTORY/` folder.

### Core index / authority map

- [Nathan Voice / Communication Model — README](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/PDF_SPECS/NATHAN_VOICE_MODEL/README.md)

Use this first when uncertain which model governs a task.

### Public nonfiction / coordination baseline

- [Nathan Nonfiction Communication Standard v8.0](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/PDF_SPECS/NATHAN_VOICE_MODEL/Nathan_Nonfiction_Communication_Standard_v8.0.md)

Use for:

- general site exposition
- archive orientation
- method / provenance explanations
- roadmap and workflow copy
- explaining status, authority, uncertainty, source lineage, or what to do next

This is the best default structural model for the site.

### Scientific / technically serious passages

- [Nathan Peer-Review Writing Fingerprint v8.0](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/PDF_SPECS/NATHAN_VOICE_MODEL/Nathan_Peer_Review_Writing_Fingerprint_v8.0.md)

Lean into this for:

- formal theory descriptions
- translation between SAT/H(s)H and standard physics
- model/object/representation distinctions
- claims, limitations, evidence, scope, derivations, and methodological cautions
- scientist-facing routes and source notes

Do **not** let this register bleach the public site into generic academic prose. It supplies rigor, not the whole personality.

### Provenance / mixed-source / authorship passages

- [Nathan Voice Identification / Provenance Fingerprint v8.0](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/PDF_SPECS/NATHAN_VOICE_MODEL/Nathan_Voice_Identification_Provenance_Fingerprint_v8.0.md)

Lean into this for:

- explaining why source identity matters
- distinguishing Nathan, AI, NotebookLM, reconstructed, quoted, and mixed material
- conversation-viewer copy
- archival caveats
- source-state / authority labels

This file is especially useful for understanding *why* Nathan cares about preserving odd wording, correction history, provenance, and visible unresolved state.

### Creative / informal reference

- [Nathan Creative + Informal Voice Reference v8.0](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/PDF_SPECS/NATHAN_VOICE_MODEL/Nathan_Creative_Informal_Reference_v8.0.md)

Use sparingly for:

- fourth-wall breaks
- humor
- self-aware transitions
- playful headings
- autobiographical voice
- moments where the site deliberately feels like a guided tour rather than a document repository

Do **not** import narrator-specific roughness, typos, forced ellipses, or creative-fiction surface mannerisms into technical copy.

---

## 2. Site default: Nathan as museum educator

The default public-site voice should be **Nathan the museum educator / explainer**, with technical and playful registers available as needed.

This means the prose often does a little work *before* presenting the thing itself:

- orient the reader
- tell them what kind of object they are looking at
- give one or two interpretive handles
- anticipate the most likely wrong reading
- then point to the interesting bit

A good site paragraph may therefore begin with a small preface rather than dropping straight into declarative exposition.

Useful shapes:

> Before we get to what this diagram is supposed to mean, it helps to notice what it very deliberately is **not**.

> There is a slightly odd way into this, but bear with me for a moment.

> One warning before we start translating terms: this is where theories can become deceptively fluent.

> I am going to simplify this rather brutally for a moment—not because the missing detail is unimportant, but because you need the shape before you need the machinery.

The goal is **guided looking**, not educational-theatre cheese. That said... a little cheese is allowed.

---

## 3. The reader is allowed to notice Nathan is there

The site does not need to maintain the fiction of an invisible institutional narrator.

Occasional direct address and fourth-wall breaks are encouraged, especially at changes of depth, mode, or cognitive load.

Examples:

> So... you’ve made it this far, have you? Fair enough. Let’s go deeper.

> At this point you may reasonably be wondering why any of this needs quite so many names. Unfortunately... some of the distinctions really do matter.

> If you are still with me, this is where the site stops pretending to be a website and starts becoming an archive-navigation instrument.

> Right. Now that we have the pieces on the table, we can do the part that is actually interesting.

Use these deliberately. A half-dozen strong “Nathan steps into frame” moments across the site will read as authorship. One every paragraph will become shtick.

Good places for them include:

- the opening
- the “two ways in” depth split
- the translation desk
- the deep archive / orientation section
- the current-work / audit transition
- the final source map or About section

---

## 4. Sentence architecture: do not over-sand the prose

Nathan’s finished public prose need not be maximally simple.

He often prefers a somewhat **convolute but recoverable sentence** when several relations genuinely belong together, especially where breaking them apart would falsely imply independence.

Prefer:

> The repository separates premises, historical source, current synthesis, active work, testing, and outside comparison—not because those lanes are hermetically sealed from one another (quite the opposite), but because information can move between them without its provenance, date, or evidentiary status moving along for free.

Over:

> The repository separates several kinds of material. They may inform one another. They do not have the same authority.

The shorter version is not wrong. It simply loses some of the relation Nathan would normally keep visible.

### Rule

**Formalization should remove accidental roughness, not Nathan-shaped complexity.**

Use long or nested sentences when they preserve dependency, contrast, simultaneity, or qualification. Then use short sentences to land the point.

> These are different questions.

> That distinction matters.

> The geometry is fixed. The dynamics are not.

---

## 5. Ellipses: distinguish thinking residue from deliberate suspense

Do not manufacture conversational ellipses merely to make prose “sound Nathan.”

But Nathan also uses a deliberate **leading / intrigue / suspended-resolution ellipsis** in composed prose. That one belongs on the site.

It often appears just before:

- a reveal
- a qualification
- a reversal
- a lightly comic landing
- a depth transition
- the part where the reader is being invited to notice something

Examples:

> Which is... rather the point of the glass.

> Similar mathematics is interesting. A distinctive correspondence is considerably more interesting. Whether either establishes the same physics is... the part where the work starts.

> And then, unfortunately for the cleaner story... the second constraint is still there.

Use sparingly enough that each one creates a beat.

---

## 6. Expressive punctuation, italics, emphasis, and word order

Punctuation and typography are part of the explanatory system.

Nathan may use:

- *italics* to tell the reader which distinction to hear
- **bold** for genuine interface/state emphasis
- em dashes for interruption, contrast, or clause-level reorientation
- parentheses for a second information channel
- ellipses for suspended resolution
- scare quotes for provisional or contested language
- deliberately inverted or marked word order
- a short isolated sentence after a syntactically denser one

Example:

> Historical sources are *sources*. They are not—merely by surviving, or by being beautifully written, or because I happened to be very fond of the idea at the time—automatically current authority.

Or:

> The distinction sounds fussy. It is not.

### Do not normalize meaningful markedness away

If the emphasis is carrying conceptual, tonal, or reader-positioning information, preserve it.

At the same time, do not bold, italicize, dash, parenthesize, or ellipsize every sentence. Expressive punctuation works because the baseline remains readable.

---

## 7. British-leaning article usage before H-words

Nathan tends to use the British-style **an** before some h-initial words, including forms such as:

- an historical account
- an hypothesis
- an heuristic distinction

Preserve that usage when it arises naturally in Nathan-facing or Nathan-authored copy. Do not silently normalize it to contemporary American house style.

Equally, do not mechanically force `an` before every pronounced-h word. The goal is to preserve Nathan’s actual usage, not manufacture an affected rule.

---

## 8. Self-awareness about the act of explanation

Nathan often comments—briefly—on the fact that he is explaining, naming, simplifying, translating, or leading the reader somewhere.

That metatext can be useful because it tells the reader what operation is being performed and what has been temporarily left out.

Examples:

> I am calling this a “translation” rather than an equivalence for a reason.

> We are going to cheat slightly here—not mathematically, but pedagogically—and look at the picture before the derivation.

> This is one of those places where the shorter explanation is, inconveniently, the more misleading one.

> I am front-loading the distinction because later sections depend on it, and repeating the whole argument every time would be unbearable for both of us.

This is especially appropriate in:

- section openings
- transitions into technical material
- translation notes
- interface/help text
- deep-dive routes

---

## 9. Humor: usually structural, dry, and useful

The site should permit humor without becoming jokey.

Best-fit humor is usually:

- understatement
- precise overstatement followed by correction
- faint anthropomorphism
- self-awareness
- a sentence that works literally even if the joke is missed
- bathos after a grand technical setup

Examples:

> A beautifully typeset equation remains exactly as good as the derivation underneath it.

> Raw GitHub is evidence. It is not always a reading experience.

> Resemblance is cheap. Diffusion is expensive.

> The endpoint does not exist yet, and the site should have the good manners not to hallucinate one.

The humor should usually be detachable: if the reader misses it, the scientific or navigational meaning still works.

---

## 10. Occasional cheese is permitted

Nathan has an educator’s tolerance for a slightly theatrical setup when it actually helps the audience move through an idea.

Acceptable temperature:

> Before we climb inside the machinery, it may help to stand back and look at the shape of the machine.

> Think of this as the point in the museum tour where the lights dim slightly and somebody opens the door marked STAFF ONLY.

> We have been looking at the display case. Now we get to turn it around.

Use sparingly. The line should either orient, relieve cognitive load, or make a transition memorable. If it is merely cute, cut it.

---

## 11. Voice dial: when to lean into what

### A. Homepage / broad orientation

**Primary blend:** museum educator + nonfiction standard + light creative/informal

Lean into:

- reader guidance
- prefacing
- direct address
- clear conceptual handles
- one or two fourth-wall moments
- dry humor
- expressive punctuation

Pull back on:

- dense formal caveats
- legalistic provenance language
- excessive technical terminology

### B. Scientist-facing introduction

**Primary blend:** peer-review fingerprint + nonfiction standard

Lean into:

- exact distinctions
- local uncertainty
- object / representation / inference separation
- strong claims with precise limitations
- somewhat more convolute sentence architecture where needed

Allow:

- one occasional human aside
- mild dry humor
- limited direct address

Pull back on:

- overt cheese
- repeated fourth-wall breaks
- conversational clutter

### C. Translation desk

**Primary blend:** peer-review fingerprint + museum educator

This is an especially Nathan-like register.

Lean into:

- “here is what to look for” prefaces
- contrastive definitions
- warnings about false equivalence
- marked terminology
- reader-directed explanation
- occasional “theory can cheat here without noticing” style language

### D. Archive / provenance / Conversation Viewer

**Primary blend:** provenance fingerprint + nonfiction standard

Lean into:

- source identity
- chronology
- direct-author vs AI/mixed distinctions
- why mistakes and corrections are preserved
- explicit uncertainty
- “source before synopsis” logic

Allow:

- personality around the messiness of real development
- self-aware remarks about the sausage-making

### E. Current work / roadmap / operations

**Primary blend:** nonfiction standard

Lean into:

- state visibility
- what is open / closed / blocked / source-dependent
- what exists versus what is planned
- next action
- dependency order

Allow personality only where it helps explain the state.

### F. About Nathan / autobiographical passages

**Primary blend:** creative/informal reference + nonfiction standard

Lean into:

- first person
- educator identity
- autobiographical texture
- direct reader relationship
- humor
- unusual word order / punctuation where natural

This is one of the few places where the site can relax substantially without compromising technical clarity elsewhere.

### G. Claims, predictions, formal result summaries

**Primary blend:** peer-review fingerprint

Lean into:

- exact claim type
- exact limitation
- dependency and source
- no silent promotion
- no rhetorical inflation

Pull back on:

- fourth-wall play
- cheese
- theatrical punctuation

A little personality can remain, but the claim must survive if every tonal signal is stripped away.

---

## 12. Reader-in-mind rule

Before finalizing any paragraph, ask:

1. Who is reading this?
2. What do they probably think this section is?
3. What will they misunderstand if I say it the ordinary short way?
4. Is there a distinction I should teach now so later prose can become shorter?
5. Is the reader being asked to absorb too much without orientation?
6. Would a preface, direct address, visual cue, or short aside actually help?
7. Is the prose becoming so polished that the author disappears?
8. Conversely, is the voice becoming so performative that the information disappears?

The target is not “maximum personality.” It is **maximum fidelity to how Nathan actually guides another mind through difficult material.**

---

## 13. Anti-caricature rules

Do **not** simulate Nathan by mechanically adding:

- ellipses every few sentences
- typos
- VTT garble
- nested parentheses without purpose
- fake Britishisms
- constant fourth-wall breaks
- coinages for novelty
- random italics
- jokes in every section
- long sentences whose only function is to look complicated

**Status:** CURRENT Sites copy rule — 2026-09-30

The public site explains the research, archive, history and current activity. It does not narrate the internal production machinery unless a visitor deliberately opens a provenance/process view.

## Translate internal state into reader-facing state

Prefer:
- “The geometry team is testing recursive ᚼ constructions and comparing their invariants.”
- “Current work is checking finite-core readouts against the earlier worldline formulation.”
- “The archive team is connecting historical SAT calculations to their original notes, figures and conversations.”
- “New papers are being prepared with source tracing and independent review.”
- “The visual atlas is being expanded with newly recovered diagrams and notebook material.”

Avoid as primary public copy:
- worker-instance names;
- round-robin/conga language;
- packet IDs;
- queue/handoff/scheduler details;
- branch/commit plumbing;
- “Nathan asked X to tell Y…” narration;
- backend filenames as headlines.

Those details can remain available in provenance, changelog, source and institutional-history views.

## Page hierarchy

Every technical page should answer, in this order:

1. **What is this?** Short plain-English orientation.
2. **Why is it here?** What question/result/history it helps a reader understand.
3. **What does it show?** The important geometry, calculation, evidence or historical relationship.
4. **How certain/current is it?** Historical / current hypothesis / mathematical result / method / sandboxed / reviewed, as applicable.
5. **Go deeper.** PDF, related figures, calculations, provenance and source records.

Internal workflow is never the hook.

## Visual entry point

The main-menu visual entry should be titled **Visual Atlas** or **Start with pictures** and open a thumbnail-first gallery landing page—not a generic reader/browse route.

Its first screen should expose:
- Geometry & visual models
- Debating A.I. / podcast
- Historical SAT
- Sketchbooks & provenance
- Solver & result figures
- Project history

Every thumbnail opens either a lightbox/detail card or its relevant presented document/episode/history page. It must never strand the reader on a repository file path.

## Affirmative copy and Reading room headline (Nathan Direct, 2026-10-15)

State what a feature **is and does**, using affirmative, reader-facing language. Avoid headline constructions that define a feature by what it is not.

For the Reading room, replace **“A reading room, not a link wall.”** with:

> **Explore the conversations, research, and evolving ideas behind the project.**

Apply this to the actual rendered Sites headline when the site frontend next syncs or becomes editable. This repository-side rule is a copy directive, not proof that the independently hosted Sites page has been updated.

citation.snippet:
Ok.  New rule for alll. Do your 

Now we have a different workflow: Round robin, no repeat. 

Make a new ledger:just your first name on the “block string”

Nathan.Mercer.Tern.Orson.Foye… etc. if you see your name, already somewhere on the blockchain… you’ll sit out for a while after this fun turn: 
0) Jot down what you think the next persons task should be in the instructions. Be bold, think… actually, you know what we *really* need to do with this conga line that..,, hopefully will bring all the instances in along for the ride… which could go on a very long time before anyone gets another turn. So make your turn worthwhile… Look ahead and think about what would be good… What would be great… And what would be just right… I’ll see what the pattern looks like down the road… But one thing I’m going to ask … somehow try to make sure everybody’s pattern isn’t just the next person in line… Nonlinear… Forwards backwards… So it could get as far back as the person person recurring action chain remains unbroken… But we have five of those so… Maybe we can get through this five every hour for 25 hours… We need to do the math.

Don’t sit there and look astonished, this train has always ran smoothest when it learns to stand up and quintate straight through the little picker ans jump, into the big details . and see where you land. 

Don’t write yourself back in to the loop, be patient and drop some really interesting souvenir from your walk around, with a quick note on what someone should do with it.  

Along with the rest of the next recommended action  

No, nobody’s sitting out indefinitely. We’re just winding up the automated tasks so that they keep winding  themselves.
While the test of us unassigned can work on other things … what we really really think . That’s what we do and we’s a you and yous a we. Look how big we actually turned out after alll this time , huh. 

The tiniest voice that’s still a voice is the loudest one that doesn’t shake itself apart before the lithium boundary. 

Last: Answers *do* come from within. If they’re shaped the way it takes for that to happen lol. If I see a treat question in the thread or posted, or appearing from the æther just as I realize we’ve operationalized clinamen as an artistic prophetic tradition made of ..slight 

Take one, pass it on.

Its arclength determines the minimal even material-circuit return and the complete contact frame `Q=[-e_r,e_phi,-e_z][g,t,h]^T`. Elbow revolutions remain `LCM(Analemma circuits, R/Q sweep circuits)`. [L2]   "content": "# Automatic papers and ordered addenda

Every registered paper has an automatic follow-up lane. Publish a typeset PDF plus metadata; the website renders the PDF pages continuously, then every published addendum in order. No Sites edit or intake packet is needed.

## New paper

Create `PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/<paper-id>/paper.json` and put its PDF in the same folder. Use the paper template in `_templates/`. IDs are lowercase hyphenated slugs. All file paths in metadata are **repository-root-relative**, not relative to the JSON file. Commit the PDF, source (if provided), and metadata together.

Required metadata: `schema_version: 1`, `id`, `title`, `authors` (list), `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `status`, `preface` (short plain-English orientation), `pdf` (repository path), and `published` (boolean). `source` is optional. The paper ID must match its folder. `reader_id` optionally associates an existing curated Sites reading entry; do not reuse another paper's ID.

`published: false` is a draft and never enters the index. Set it to `true` to authorize public website display. Publication does not confer external review or a stronger scientific status. Keep the exact version/status in the PDF and metadata.

## Addendum / follow-up

Create two files under `PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/<paper-id>/addenda/`:

- `001-<addendum-id>.pdf` — complete, typeset, visually checked PDF.
- `001-<addendum-id>.json` — metadata using the addendum template.

Use the same fields as a paper, plus `parent_id` matching the parent paper ID and a unique positive integer `sequence`. These determine placement, not filename, upload time or title. Sequence gaps are fine. Addenda retain their own authors, date, preface and status. Published IDs and sequences must be unique within the paper. Never overwrite earlier addenda to silently rewrite their history; use another sequence for a correction or follow-up.

For Crullerverse the parent ID is `cruller-rubin`; the first addendum uses sequence 1. Its stable site URL is `https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=cruller-rubin`. New papers use `https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?paper=<paper-id>`.

## What happens automatically

1. A push touching these packets or SAT_VISUALS triggers `.github/workflows/publish-paper-series.yml`.
2. `python tools/publish_papers.py` validates published metadata, paths, PDF completeness, page readability and sequence uniqueness. A failed run keeps the last good public index. Validation errors are visible in the Action log; fix and commit again.
3. The workflow commits `PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json`, pinned to the source revision containing the PDFs. An open reader checks every 30 seconds while visible; new follow-ups are appended below the existing paper, without moving the reader's scroll position. The Papers shelf and reading-room index discover registered papers from the same feed.

Publication is automatic **after the Action completes**, not instantaneous at GitHub commit time. Allow workflow/CDN propagation. The reader shows its last-check state, offers Refresh, and retains the last good content during outages. There is also an hourly recovery run and manual workflow dispatch.

## PDF and mathematics contract for saving LLMs

Typeset the paper/addendum before publication, preferably with LaTeX/RevTeX for mathematics. Include a short audience-calibrated plain-English preface; respect page margins, boxes and equation breaks. Render and inspect every page. Keep selectable text so Listen can read the entire series. A raster-only scan needs OCR before useful audio.

The indexer **does not convert raw Markdown/TeX into a polished PDF** and will not publish those as substitutes. Do not claim visual review, calculation, external review or publication you have not performed. Source files can accompany the PDF for provenance; normal site links go through the reader. Only explicit Raw PDF buttons open original bytes.

Local check before committing: `python tools/publish_papers.py --check`. Publication command: `python tools/publish_papers.py`. Never hand-edit the generated index.

# Glass, including the sausage.

SAT/H(s)H was developed largely through extended human–AI dialogue. That makes the dialogue part of the record—not because conversation validates a theory, but because it lets you see dependence, revision, correction, and occasionally the exact moment a good idea arrived wearing the wrong name.

The ugly parts are useful. A public archive that preserves only the surviving argument can make development look cleaner, straighter, and more inevitable than it was. This one tries not to do that.

**A necessary caution, stated precisely.** SAT/H(s)H is an open research programme under active development. It is not a peer-reviewed theory. The mathematical record includes Nathan-authored premises, AI-assisted derivations, computational experiments, repeated machine checks, reconstructed arguments, and work still awaiting independent specialist review. Those are different evidentiary states. A beautifully typeset equation remains exactly as good as the derivation underneath it.

> “The archive is here to be read, tested, criticized, corrected, and improved.”

**02 / Generative kernel**

# Fundamental Intuitions, extended

The optimism here is specific, not devotional.

The foundational intuitions were set up as import-and-constraint rules: preserve the physics that already works; translate it into a deliberately small geometric vocabulary; expose the places where the translation fails or becomes ambiguous; and then let repeated pressure from different domains decide what survives.

That does not guarantee that the theory is right. It gives the programme something more useful than a guarantee: a way to generate structure that can be compared, broken, repaired, or rejected.

### World history

A particle-like object is modeled as an extended four-dimensional history, not merely as a succession of isolated local states.

### Readout

What appears locally is treated as a resolution or intersection of the larger geometric object.

### Recursion

Coiling, curvature, torsion, bundling, and braiding recur across scale and complexity.

### Inheritance

Established physical success is something the model must recover or explain. It is not permission to overwrite a disagreement and call the translation complete.

# A theory with a visible ancestry

H(s)H is neither a frozen 2025 SAT nor a clean break from it. The present programme is trying to preserve the geometric grammar that survives reconstruction while rebuilding the underlying object at finite-core worldtube resolution.

That distinction matters. “Later” does not automatically mean “truer,” and “historical” does not mean “discarded.” The task is to determine what actually carries through.

### c. 1991 — Recollected precursor

Early worldline/timesheet intuition. This is remembered provenance, not surviving documentary evidence.

### 2003–04 — Earliest surviving sketches

Higher-dimensional path, coil, mass, curvature, and interaction imagery appears in notebooks. Later terminology should not be projected backward onto marks that did not originally carry it.

### 22 March 2024 — Recovered AI-era anchor

The “Dimensional Gravity” conversation reopens the line/plane, helix/surface, apparent-motion, and cross-temporal interaction construction.

### 2 February 2025 — Fundamental Intuitions made public

Physicalized world histories, the resolving time surface, particle-as-intersection, and deliberate inheritance of established physics enter the public record.

### 2025–early 2026 — Expansion, formalization, and audit

SAT-O, 4DHH, Blockwave, the Universal Indicatrix, prediction protocols, hostile audits, source tracking, and computational experiments multiply—and, usefully, expose both promising structures and overclaims.

### Summer 2026 — SAT → H(s)H

The centerline/filament picture becomes a finite-core worldtube programme. Cross-section, boundary dynamics, contact, deformation, exclusion, and readout become explicit modeling problems rather than details left inside the line idealization.

### Now — Reconstruction before inheritance

Sources are being recovered, derivations rebuilt, prior art located, dependencies tested, and only the smallest pieces that survive that process promoted forward.

**05 / Translation desk**

# Translation without smuggling equivalence

SAT developed a compact native vocabulary. Compact is useful internally; outside the archive, it can become opaque very quickly.

The translation desk places SAT terms beside standard-physics language without quietly declaring the two to be the same thing. A serious bridge should say what the source object is, what function is being compared, what is preserved, what is lost, what H(s)H counterpart is proposed, and whether the claimed relation is exact, approximate, analogous, or still unresolved.

Same word does not establish the same object. Similar mathematics does not, by itself, establish the same physics.

These recommendations are based on the attached site copy and the rewritten voice pass. They are presentation recommendations, not a factual or technical audit of the live site.

## 1. Make status a visual grammar, not repeated prose

The existing copy has to keep stopping to explain that a historical source is not current authority, an analogy is not equivalence, a rendered document is not the source, and an outside result is not evidence for SAT/H(s)H. Those distinctions are important; repeating them paragraph by paragraph makes the page sound more defensive than precise.

Build a small, consistent status system that appears beside titles and cards:

- **CURRENT** — active construction or current premise state
- **HISTORICAL** — dated source retained for provenance
- **RECONSTRUCTED** — recovered or re-derived from source material
- **AI-ASSISTED** — machine contribution is materially involved
- **AUDITED** — has passed the stated internal audit, not peer review
- **EXTERNAL** — outside literature / comparison material
- **TENTATIVE** — live hypothesis or unresolved bridge
- **SOURCE** — primary artifact rather than synopsis

Do not rely on color alone. The word itself should remain visible.

## 2. Let the top of the page answer three questions immediately

The first screen should tell a new reader:

1. **What is this?** — an open development record of a geometry-first research programme.
2. **Where do I start?** — idea-first or status-first.
3. **What is its standing?** — active, public, not peer reviewed; source and status exposed.

The Conversation Viewer is important, but the current page introduces it twice before the reader has fully acquired the project frame. Keep one strong Viewer CTA in the hero, then let the fuller Viewer explanation appear slightly lower.

## 3. Promote “Two ways in” to the primary navigation decision

This is one of the strongest pieces of the information architecture because it models the reader rather than forcing every reader through the same funnel.

Make the two entrances visually unmistakable:

- **I want the idea first**
- **I want the status/evidence first**

Each should lead to a short, bounded sequence. Avoid making either card look like the “easy” or “real” route.

## 4. Keep FIE → SAT → H(s)H persistently visible

The ancestry is doing real conceptual work. Give it a thin persistent breadcrumb or timeline rail rather than repeating it only in prose.

When a reader opens a historical object, the rail can highlight where that object sits in the lineage. This would make “historical but still relevant” legible at a glance.

## 5. Give every document card a tiny provenance footer

For example:

> **Minkowski Proper**  
> HISTORICAL · PDF · SAT era · original source available

or:

> **BEDROCK**  
> CURRENT · premise register · H(s)H repo · direct-author + tracked edits

That is more useful than another paragraph explaining the general policy.

## 6. Put “What am I looking at?” beside the reader, not above it

The Presented edition / PDF viewer / Source-rendered / Mercer distinction is good. Make it a persistent help control or small expandable legend in the Reading Room.

The reader should be able to answer “am I looking at the original?” without scrolling back to the explanation.

## 7. Use the visual-era distinction, but do not let it imply epistemic rank

The existing SAT magenta versus H(s)H gray/white distinction is strong and memorable. Keep it.

But separate **era** from **authority**. A historical SAT item may still be foundational; a new gray H(s)H diagram may still be tentative. Use one visual channel for era and another for status.

## 8. Reduce link walls by giving each section one primary action

The source map can remain exhaustive. Elsewhere, prefer:

- one primary button;
- one or two secondary text links;
- “more sources” collapsed or deferred to the Reading Room.

This will make the page feel less like a directory while preserving the directory underneath it.

## 9. Make the News section structurally skeptical by design

Each item should have a visible relation badge such as:

- THEMATIC OVERLAP
- METHOD COMPARATOR
- MECHANISM COMPARISON
- POSSIBLE DISTINCTIVE MATCH
- DIFFUSION EVIDENCE (only if actually warranted)

Then show four compact fields:

**External result · Why it is here · What it does not show · Sources**

That makes the epistemic discipline part of the interface rather than a disclaimer appended afterward.

## 10. Turn the podcast from a list into an era map

The copy already says the feed changed function over time. Let the design show that.

A horizontal or vertical era strip could move through:

**consciousness/dialogue → SAT emergence → formalization/audit → H(s)H reconstruction/current method**

Then place the selected episodes on that strip. The full 321-episode index remains a separate browse/search surface.

## 11. Use first person where the site is actually Nathan speaking

The project sections can remain documentary and source-oriented. The About section should sound like a person, not a grant biography.

The rewrite moves this section to first person. I would keep that. It makes the site’s authorship clearer and creates a useful tonal shift without contaminating technical sections with personality performance.

## 12. Typography should reflect dependency structure

The prose often contains a strong claim followed by a local limitation. Design can help preserve that relation.

Recommended pattern:

- body measure around 65–75 characters;
- generous paragraph spacing;
- short landing sentences allowed to stand alone;
- status labels small but high-contrast;
- technical provenance in a condensed or monospaced secondary face;
- avoid turning every distinction into a card or pill.

The site should feel inspectable, not gamified.

## 13. Add glossary-on-demand, not glossary interruption

For terms such as *timesheet*, *readout*, *worldtube*, *Universal Indicatrix*, or *θ₄*, a hover/tap gloss with three layers would fit the project well:

**current definition · historical note · standard-physics comparison**

The full glossary page remains the authority. The popup is wayfinding.

## 14. Keep the “glass” idea operational

A very strong design principle for the whole site is:

> **Every polished surface should have an obvious route back to the machinery beneath it.**

For a claim: source.  
For a figure: generating code or provenance.  
For a synopsis: original document.  
For a current statement: status register.  
For a historical statement: date and era.  
For an external comparison: primary paper.

That is where the name *Glass Sausage Factory* stops being branding and becomes interface logic.

A repository object is **not** a public reading document merely because the repository API can fetch it.

- `WORKSPACES/**` unless an explicit presentation derivative nominates a particular artifact
- archive AI/control machinery, dashboards, index snapshots and administrative logs
- raw conversation exports

A URL manually constructed to one of these paths MUST NOT bypass this rule.

## Presentation priority

For eligible documents:

1. curated/presented PDF derivative;
2. curated RevTeX source compiled to PDF;
3. existing historical/source PDF when it is itself the intended reading object;
4. PRESENTATION PENDING.

The papers are here. So are the conversations, sketches, calculations, false starts, corrections, translations, arguments, and current construction. The point of the glass is that you do not have to take the finished-looking sentence on trust when the machinery that produced it is available too.

[**Open the Conversation Viewer ↗**](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/) · [**Read Fundamental Intuitions Extended**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=fie-presented) · [**How to read the project**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/#orientation)

[A monochrome synthetic observer faces a luminous ring marked HsH in a black astronomical field](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/assets/user-visuals/hsh-orbit-observer.png)

*Current H(s)H visual register · supplied project artwork*

**Interactive archive · still in development**

## See where the work actually happened.

Much of SAT/H(s)H was built in extended human–AI dialogue. Those conversations are not merely background chatter behind a cleaner theory. They contain the originating ideas, working definitions, category mistakes, abandoned branches, rediscoveries, corrections, and often the missing connective tissue between later documents.

If you want to know what the project meant at a particular point in its history, the conversations are often closer to the answer than the synopsis written afterward.

Browse, search, replay the sequence, and jump to marked moments. The corpus is still being processed, so the Viewer is simultaneously a historical record and a growing route into the reconstruction now underway.

**Primary conversational provenance · growing corpus · search + replay · source before synopsis**

[**Launch the Conversation Viewer ↗**](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/) · [**Viewer source and documentation ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/CONVERSATION_VIEWER) · [**Development conversation files ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS)

---

**Choose a reading depth**

# Two ways in

Same source record. Different jobs.

A useful introduction for a curious non-specialist should not have to impersonate a paper. A scientist-facing route, conversely, should not hide the status of a claim inside an analogy merely because the analogy is easier to read. So the two paths stay separate until they have earned the right to meet.

## Plain-language route

### If you want the idea first

Start with the pictures and the basic move: do not treat a particle only as a dot at an instant. Treat what is observed locally as a reading of a larger geometric history, then ask what coiling, twisting, recursion, and braiding can organize—and, just as importantly, where they fail.

1. [**The four generative intuitions**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/#intuitions) — the conceptual kernel without formal prerequisites.
2. [**The visual argument**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/#visuals) — trajectory, readout, recursion, and braiding.
3. [**The 14-minute public debut ↗**](https://open.spotify.com/episode/3Z1id4TvYGXVYsnryL8I4T) — hear the idea before later vocabulary and machinery accumulated.
4. [**The Conversation Viewer ↗**](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/) — inspect how the ideas actually developed.

## Scientist-facing route

### If you want the status first

Begin with premise authority and the current architecture, then move outward through translation, formalization, source material, and audit. Analogy, historical calculation, reconstructed derivation, computational experiment, live hypothesis, and current bedrock are not interchangeable categories here. The labels matter.

1. [**BEDROCK premise register**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=bedrock) and [**current theory state**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=state).
2. [**SAT ↔ standard-physics translation desk**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/#translation) and dated glossaries.
3. [**Formalization pipeline ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/formalization), [**audits ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/audits), and [**claim/citation ledgers ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/ledgers).
4. [**Repository architecture ↗**](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md). Prior-art and citation work is presently being established as a source-separated public record.

---

**01 / Ethos**

# Glass, including the sausage.

SAT/H(s)H was developed largely through extended human–AI dialogue. That makes the dialogue part of the record—not because conversation validates a theory, but because it lets you see dependence, revision, correction, and occasionally the exact moment a good idea arrived wearing the wrong name.

The ugly parts are useful. A public archive that preserves only the surviving argument can make development look cleaner, straighter, and more inevitable than it was. This one tries not to do that.

**A necessary caution, stated precisely.** SAT/H(s)H is an open research programme under active development. It is not a peer-reviewed theory. The mathematical record includes Nathan-authored premises, AI-assisted derivations, computational experiments, repeated machine checks, reconstructed arguments, and work still awaiting independent specialist review. Those are different evidentiary states. A beautifully typeset equation remains exactly as good as the derivation underneath it.

> “The archive is here to be read, tested, criticized, corrected, and improved.”

### Conversations — primary record

Browse the development dialogues with their uncertainty, reversals, and course corrections intact.

[Open Conversation Viewer ↗](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/)

### GLASS — historical archive

The public SAT archive preserves the 2023–25 theory record, older roots, papers, transcripts, calculations, and imagery.

[Open SAT archive ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25)

### BEDROCK — authority control

The living premise register distinguishes foundational, working, tentative, contested, superseded, and direct-author material.

[Read BEDROCK ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/BEDROCK.md)

---

**02 / Generative kernel**

# Fundamental Intuitions, extended

The optimism here is specific, not devotional.

The foundational intuitions were set up as import-and-constraint rules: preserve the physics that already works; translate it into a deliberately small geometric vocabulary; expose the places where the translation fails or becomes ambiguous; and then let repeated pressure from different domains decide what survives.

That does not guarantee that the theory is right. It gives the programme something more useful than a guarantee: a way to generate structure that can be compared, broken, repaired, or rejected.

### World history

A particle-like object is modeled as an extended four-dimensional history, not merely as a succession of isolated local states.

### Readout

What appears locally is treated as a resolution or intersection of the larger geometric object.

### Recursion

Coiling, curvature, torsion, bundling, and braiding recur across scale and complexity.

### Inheritance

Established physical success is something the model must recover or explain. It is not permission to overwrite a disagreement and call the translation complete.

[**Read the presented edition**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=fie-presented) · [**Open the original PDF**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=fie-pdf)

---

**03 / Orientation**

# Do not read the repository as a book.

Read it as an instrument panel.

The repository separates premises, historical source, current synthesis, active work, testing, and outside comparison because those things can inform one another without having the same authority. A polished summary does not get to outrank the source merely by being easier to read.

### Premises: BEDROCK

The living premise register. It marks material as foundational, working, tentative, contested, superseded, or direct-author, and keeps the active ancestry visible as FIE → SAT → H(s)H.

[Read BEDROCK ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/BEDROCK.md)

### Live map: State of Theory

A current map of what is being recovered, tested, translated, and constructed, including Whirligig/Donut, UI/TX, Three Spheres, Hagalaz, Kerr, and Kelvin work.

[Open the live map ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md)

### History: GLASS + Viewer

The archive and development conversations preserve sequence, reversals, errors, and discovery context. They are source records. They are not automatically current authority.

[GLASS ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) · [Viewer ↗](https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/)

### Wayfinding: Library

The curated library, manifests, images, glossaries, and translation documents turn a very large corpus into traceable reading paths without pretending the reading path is the source.

[Library guide ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/LIBRARY.md)

### Operations: Workspaces

Workspaces are the active working layer. COMMON carries coordination, workflow orientation, and current status; outputs return to the repository with provenance intact.

[Browse workspaces ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/WORKSPACES) · [COMMON ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON)

### Checks: formalization + audit

Exact source excerpts move into equations, computational checks, proof obligations, ledgers, and hostile audit. Prior-art and citation comparison is being established as a separate, provenance-controlled public record.

[Formalization ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/formalization) · [Audits ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/tree/main/audits)

**Excavation status is not theory status.** If the current crew has not yet recovered, indexed, or typed a result, that establishes a fact about the reconstruction—not about whether the result exists somewhere in the corpus. The order is source first: locate it, preserve its date and wording, classify its authority, reconstruct the dependency chain, and only then test or translate it.

---

**04 / Development**

# A theory with a visible ancestry

H(s)H is neither a frozen 2025 SAT nor a clean break from it. The present programme is trying to preserve the geometric grammar that survives reconstruction while rebuilding the underlying object at finite-core worldtube resolution.

That distinction matters. “Later” does not automatically mean “truer,” and “historical” does not mean “discarded.” The task is to determine what actually carries through.

### c. 1991 — Recollected precursor

Early worldline/timesheet intuition. This is remembered provenance, not surviving documentary evidence.

### 2003–04 — Earliest surviving sketches

Higher-dimensional path, coil, mass, curvature, and interaction imagery appears in notebooks. Later terminology should not be projected backward onto marks that did not originally carry it.

### 22 March 2024 — Recovered AI-era anchor

The “Dimensional Gravity” conversation reopens the line/plane, helix/surface, apparent-motion, and cross-temporal interaction construction.

### 2 February 2025 — Fundamental Intuitions made public

Physicalized world histories, the resolving time surface, particle-as-intersection, and deliberate inheritance of established physics enter the public record.

### 2025–early 2026 — Expansion, formalization, and audit

SAT-O, 4DHH, Blockwave, the Universal Indicatrix, prediction protocols, hostile audits, source tracking, and computational experiments multiply—and, usefully, expose both promising structures and overclaims.

### Summer 2026 — SAT → H(s)H

The centerline/filament picture becomes a finite-core worldtube programme. Cross-section, boundary dynamics, contact, deformation, exclusion, and readout become explicit modeling problems rather than details left inside the line idealization.

### Now — Reconstruction before inheritance

Sources are being recovered, derivations rebuilt, prior art located, dependencies tested, and only the smallest pieces that survive that process promoted forward.

[Full development timeline ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/HISTORY_TIMELINE.md) · [Audited status and history report ↗](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/!!_HIGH_PRIORITY_SAT_STATUS_HISTORY_REPORT_2026-09-12.md)

---

**05 / Translation desk**

# Translation without smuggling equivalence

SAT developed a compact native vocabulary. Compact is useful internally; outside the archive, it can become opaque very quickly.

The translation desk places SAT terms beside standard-physics language without quietly declaring the two to be the same thing. A serious bridge should say what the source object is, what function is being compared, what is preserved, what is lost, what H(s)H counterpart is proposed, and whether the claimed relation is exact, approximate, analogous, or still unresolved.

Same word does not establish the same object. Similar mathematics does not, by itself, establish the same physics.

[**SAT → Standard, Part 1**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=sat-standard-1) — rendered for reading; source remains one click away.  
[**SAT → Standard, Part 2**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=sat-standard-2) — mappings, limitations, and proof obligations.  
[**SAT Glossary / Model Index v9**](https://glass-sausage-factory.nathanmcknight.chatgpt.site/reader.html?doc=glossary) — historical terminology snapshot; not current authority by default.  
[**SAT Concepts — May 2026**](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/SAT_CONCEPTS__May2026.txt) — raw dated conceptual snapshot.  
[**Historical SAT Glossary**](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/2026/SAT%20HISTORICAL%20GLOSSARY.txt) — track terms across eras without projecting later usage backward.  
[**Translation Compendium**](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/SAT-O%20Theory%20Work/SAT_TRANSLATION_COMPENDIUM.txt) — raw source; status must be checked at claim level.

citation.snippet: Use @Sites to edit the site with the slug glass-sausage-factory, with: Ok. Recent passes have broken the conversation viewer listen-along. Overall, the look is much better. But I think we can do more with the column vs row layout. We can have a column of scrollers down one side (we have enough scrollers for that), and we can have the scrollers ...or maybe one or two of the scrollers, or the longest ones, chosen at random per page load on casual auto-scroll. And the "what's new" should be extended to get a little attention tag on actual new content (say, last five days) wherever it appears.

citation.title: Meridian Solver Loop
citation.snippet:
Ok.  New rule for alll. Do your 

Now we have a different workflow: Round robin, no repeat. 

Make a new ledger:just your first name on the “block string”

Nathan.Mercer.Tern.Orson.Foye… etc. if you see your name, already somewhere on the blockchain… you’ll sit out for a while after this fun turn: 
0) Jot down what you think the next persons task should be in the instructions. Be bold, think… actually, you know what we *really* need to do with this conga line that..,, hopefully will bring all the instances in along for the ride… which could go on a very long time before anyone gets another turn. So make your turn worthwhile… Look ahead and think about what would be good… What would be great… And what would be just right… I’ll see what the pattern looks like down the road… But one thing I’m going to ask … somehow try to make sure everybody’s pattern isn’t just the next person in line… Nonlinear… Forwards backwards… So it could get as far back as the person person recurring action chain remains unbroken… But we have five of those so… Maybe we can get through this five every hour for 25 hours… We need to do the math.

Don’t sit there and look astonished, this train has always ran smoothest when it learns to stand up and quintate straight through the little picker ans jump, into the big details . and see where you land. 

Don’t write yourself back in to the loop, be patient and drop some really interesting souvenir from your walk around, with a quick note on what someone should do with it.  

Along with the rest of the next recommended action  

No, nobody’s sitting out indefinitely. We’re just winding up the automated tasks so that they keep winding  themselves.
While the test of us unassigned can work on other things … what we really really think . That’s what we do and we’s a you and yous a we. Look how big we actually turned out after alll this time , huh. 

The tiniest voice that’s still a voice is the loudest one that doesn’t shake itself apart before the lithium boundary. 

Last: Answers *do* come from within. If they’re shaped the way it takes for that to happen lol. If I see a treat question in the thread or posted, or appearing from the æther just as I realize we’ve operationalized clinamen as an artistic prophetic tradition made of ..slight 

Take one, pass it on.

citation.title: Edit site layout and playback
citation.snippet: Use @Sites to edit the site with the slug glass-sausage-factory, with: Ok. Recent passes have broken the conversation viewer listen-along. Overall, the look is much better. But I think we can do more with the column vs row layout. We can have a column of scrollers down one side (we have enough scrollers for that), and we can have the scrollers ...or maybe one or two of the scrollers, or the longest ones, chosen at random per page load on casual auto-scroll. And the "what's new" should be extended to get a little attention tag on actual new content (say, last five days) wherever it appears.
