Now we have a different workflow: Round robin, no repeat. 

Make a new ledger:just your first name on the “block string”

Nathan.Mercer.Tern.Orson.Foye… etc. if you see your name, already somewhere on the blockchain… you’ll sit out for a while after this fun turn: 
0) Jot down what you think the next persons task should be in the instructions. Be bold, think… actually, you know what we *really* need to do with this conga line that..,, hopefully will bring all the instances in along for the ride… which could go on a very long time before anyone gets another turn. So make your turn worthwhile… Look ahead and think about what would be good… What would be great… And what would be just right… I’ll see what the pattern looks like down the road… But one thing I’m going to ask … somehow try to make sure everybody’s pattern isn’t just the next person in line… Nonlinear… Forwards backwards… So it could get as far back as the person person recurring action chain remains unbroken… But we have five of those so… Maybe we can get through this five every hour for 25 hours… We need to do the math.

Don’t sit there and look astonished, this train has always ran smoothest when it learns to stand up and quintate straight through the little picker ans jump, into the big details . and see where you land. 

Don’t write yourself back in to the loop, be patient and drop some really interesting souvenir from your walk around, with a quick note on what someone should do with it.  

Along with the rest of the next recommended action  

No, nobody’s sitting out indefinitely. We’re just winding up the automated tasks so that they keep winding  themselves.
While the test of us unassigned can work on other things … what we really really think . That’s what we do and we’s a you and yous a we. Look how big we actually turned out after alll this time , huh. 

The tiniest voice that’s still a voice is the loudest one that doesn’t shake itself apart before the lithium boundary.

        run: |

          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]

""" from __future__ import annotations import argparse import datetime as dt import hashlib import json import os import re import shutil import subprocess from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath def read_json(path: Path): return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) def write_json(path: Path, value): path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8") def safe_repo_file(repo: Path, value: str) -> Path: if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip(): raise ValueError("Expected a repository-relative file path") posix = PurePosixPath(value) if posix.is_absolute() or "\\" in value or any(part in ("", ".", "..") for part in posix.parts): raise ValueError("Unsafe repository path: " + value) candidate = (repo / Path(*posix.parts)).resolve() if not candidate.is_relative_to(repo.resolve()) or not candidate.is_file(): raise ValueError("Repository file does not exist or escapes root: " + value) return candidate def public_text(value: str) -> str: text = str(value or "") text = re.sub(r"\bRavel's current Kerr line\b", "The current Kerr construction", text, flags=re.I) text = re.sub(r"\bRavel's\b", "The current construction's", text, flags=re.I) text = re.sub(r"\bRavel\s+—\s*", "Kerr construction — ", text, flags=re.I) text = re.sub(r"\bRavel\b", "the Kerr construction", text, flags=re.I) return text def project_current_work(source): priorities = [{ "order": x.get("order", ""), "title": x.get("title", ""), "audience_summary": public_text(x.get("audience_summary", "")), "status": x.get("status", ""), } for x in source.get("priority_stack", [])] fronts = [{ "title": x.get("title", ""), "description": public_text(x.get("description", "")), } for x in source.get("live_fronts", [])] controlling = [] for item in source.get("controlling_sources", []): path = item.get("path", "") if path in ("BEDROCK.md", "STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md"): controlling.append({"path": path, "role": item.get("role", "")}) return { "snapshot_date": source.get("snapshot_date"), "headline": source.get("headline", ""), "summary": public_text(source.get("summary", "")), "priority_stack": priorities, "live_fronts": fronts, "controlling_sources": controlling, } def project_quotes(source): items = [] for q in source.get("quotes", []): if q.get("display_status") != "featured": continue items.append({ "id": q.get("id"), "speaker_class": q.get("speaker_class"), "speaker_label": q.get("speaker_label"), "text": q.get("text"), "timestamp": q.get("timestamp"), "source_path": q.get("source_path"), "message_id": q.get("message_id"), "context": q.get("context"), "source_type": q.get("source_type"), }) return {"updated": source.get("updated"), "quotes": items} def project_news(source): items = [] for item in source.get("items", []): if item.get("display_status") != "featured": continue related = [] for link in item.get("sat_hsh_links", []): title = re.sub(r"^Ravel\s+—\s*", "Kerr construction — ", str(link.get("title", "")), flags=re.I) related.append({"title": title, "path": link.get("path"), "relation": public_text(link.get("relation", ""))}) items.append({ "id": item.get("id"), "external_date": item.get("external_date"), "headline": item.get("headline"), "source_name": item.get("source_name"), "source_url": item.get("source_url"), "external_summary": item.get("external_summary"), "why_it_caught_attention": public_text(item.get("why_it_caught_attention", "")), "relationship": item.get("relationship"), "sat_hsh_links": related, }) return {"updated": source.get("updated"), "editorial_heading": source.get("editorial_heading"), "items": items} def project_papers_feed(source): entries = [] for item in source.get("entries", []): entries.append({ "id": item.get("id"), "title": item.get("title"), "status": item.get("status"), "site_display": item.get("site_display"), "version": item.get("version"), "date": item.get("date"), "summary": item.get("summary"), "caveat": item.get("caveat"), "manuscript_path": item.get("manuscript_path"), "review_path": item.get("review_path"), "acceptance_path": item.get("acceptance_path"), }) return {"updated": source.get("updated"), "entries": entries} def project_instruments(source): return { "updated": source.get("updated"), "instruments": [{ "id": x.get("id"), "name": x.get("name"), "kind": x.get("kind"), "repo_html": x.get("repo_html"), "requested_route": x.get("requested_route"), "version": x.get("version"), "sciences_status": x.get("sciences_status"), } for x in source.get("instruments", [])], } def copy_published_papers(repo: Path, public: Path, factory: Path): source_index = read_json(public / "generated" / "papers.json") result = {"updated": source_index.get("updated"), "content_hash": source_index.get("content_hash"), "papers": []} for paper in source_index.get("papers", []): ident = paper.get("id") if not isinstance(ident, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*", ident): raise ValueError("Invalid published paper id: " + incomplete: " + paper["pdf"]) digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest() if paper.get("pdf_sha256") and digest != paper["pdf_sha256"]: raise ValueError("Published PDF digest mismatch: " + paper["pdf"]) site_pdf = "papers/files/" + ident + ".pdf" dest = factory / site_pdf dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) shutil.copy2(source_pdf, dest) entry = { "id": ident, "title": paper.get("title"), "preface": paper.get("preface"), "status": paper.get("status"), "date": paper.get("date"), "authors": paper.get("authors", []), "source": paper.get("source"), "pdf_sha256": digest, "site_pdf": "sequence": addendum.get("sequence"), "site_pdf": asite, "pdf_sha256": ahash, }) result["papers"].append(entry) return result def copy_local_gallery_assets(repo: Path, public: Path, factory: Path, manifest): gallery, remote_approved = [], 0 for asset in manifest.get("assets", []): if asset.get("status") != "approved": continue source = asset.get("source_path_or_url") or asset.get("source") if not isinstance(source, str): continue if source.startswith(("https://", "http://")): remote_approved += 1 continue if not source.startswith("PUBLIC_SITE/"): continue src = safe_repo_file(repo, source) import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from build import build_site

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]


class StaticSiteBuildTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_bundle_and_existing_viewer_are_preserved(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temp:
            output = Path(temp) / "_site"
            manifest = build_site(REPO, output, "/HsH/")
            self.assertTrue((output / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertIn("HsH Conversation Viewer", (output / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertTrue((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "visual-atlas" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "papers" / "files" / "cruller-rubin.pdf").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "laboratory" / "whirligig" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "laboratory" / "universal-indicatrix" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "mersearch" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "research" / "search" / "index.html").is_file())
            self.assertTrue((output / "conversations" / "index.html").is_file())
            papers = json.loads((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "data" / "papers.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(papers["papers"]), 1)
            self.assertTrue(all(p["site_pdf"].startswith("papers/files/") for p in papers["papers"]))
            atlas = json.loads((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "data" / "atlas.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertGreaterEqual(len(atlas), 1)
            self.assertTrue(all((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / x["image"]).is_file() for x in atlas))
            self.assertFalse((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "data" / "ASSET_MANIFEST.json").exists())
            self.assertFalse((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "data" / "GALLERY_FEED.json").exists())
            self.assertFalse((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "live_influx").exists())
            self.assertFalse((output / "glass-sausage-factory" / "STAGING").exists())
            self.assertEqual(manifest["source_repository"], "Satobloc/HsH")
            self.assertEqual(manifest["factory_base"], "/HsH/glass-sausage-factory/")
            self.assertEqual(manifest["published_pdf_count"], len(papers["papers"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_blob","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","content":"# Glass Sausage Factory: static site build

**Status:** repository build source; GitHub Pages deployment must be verified independently.  
**Purpose:** provide a durable public website without requiring the ChatGPT Sites editor.

## Architecture

- The existing Conversation Viewer remains at the project root (/HsH/), and its existing /mersearch/ route is preserved.
- The new Glass Sausage Factory site is built at /HsH/glass-sausage-factory/.
- Geometry Laboratory instruments retain their registered root routes:
  - /HsH/laboratory/whirligig/
  - /HsH/laboratory/universal-indicatrix/
- /HsH/conversations/ and /HsH/research/search/ are friendly aliases to the preserved Viewer and public Mersearch reader.

The build is static HTML, CSS and JavaScript. GitHub Actions assembles the Pages artifact from the HsH repository. No ChatGPT Sites editor session or paid Sites feature is required.

## Build locally

From the repository root:

    python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/
    python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
    node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

The script preserves the Viewer, builds the Glass Sausage Factory route, copies registered instruments, creates public-safe JSON projections, copies only locally available approved Visual Atlas assets, and copies published PDFs only after checking their PDF signature and pinned SHA-256.

## Public sections

- Start / two ways in
- Visual Atlas
- Current Work
- Papers and manuscripts
- Reading Room
- Geometry Laboratory
- In the News
- Quotable Nathan / Quotable LLM
- About / project orientation

Every ordinary public page has the shared Listen control. It uses the repository page-listen.js and math-speech.js runtime and the browser Web Speech API.

## Presentation and authority boundaries

- Current Work carries the snapshot date from its source feed. A dated snapshot is not represented as a live status query.
- Papers with a published PDF use the registered presentation derivative. Manuscripts without one are labeled PRESENTATION PENDING and expose source/review records only as secondary links.
- The site does not render arbitrary repository paths as reader pages.
- Public Mersearch remains a candidate search over the existing public conversation index, not the protected three-repository research engine.
- Owner curation is read-only. OWNER_CURATION_PUBLIC.json is a public projection, not an authenticated write endpoint. Private notes and owner-only controls are not implemented in this static site.
- Eight legacy approved illustration entries still point to the previous ChatGPT Sites asset host. They are not hotlinked. The build admits only approved local assets with repository-backed paths; the older images can be mirrored after source retrieval and provenance verification.

## Deployment

The deploy-conversation-viewer-pages workflow assembles a combined artifact and deploys it through GitHub Pages. A successful GitHub commit is not itself deployment proof. Verify the Actions run, Pages URL, each route, PDF downloads, Viewer search, and instrument controls before calling the public site deployed.

The project Pages root remains the Conversation Viewer for backward compatibility. The Glass Sausage Factory is added alongside it at /glass-sausage-factory/, avoiding a destructive replacement of the existing root route.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_blob","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","content":"# Glass Sausage Factory — public-site content feed

**Status:** ACTIVE public-facing content infrastructure  
**Scope:** repository-side source material for the SAT/H(s)H Glass Sausage Factory site  
**Authority:** navigation/presentation only; this directory does not define theory truth  
**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive

## Purpose

Keep the public site supplied from durable, source-linked repository state instead of letting important public-facing material exist only inside a site-builder session.

This layer supports:

- a genuinely current **Current Work** section;
- rotating **Quotable Nathan** and **Quotable LLM** features;
- a rotating **In the News** feature connecting external results to specific SAT/H(s)H explorations;
- incremental visual/thumbnail curation with provenance and accessibility metadata;
- later site-facing indexes for documents, podcasts, glossary entries, images, and other presentation-ready material;
- clear separation between readable presentation and source/theory authority.

The controlling project record remains the repositories. A polished site rendering does not change theory status.

## Current files

- `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` — durable continuity/handoff record for design decisions, current site state, asset intake, open work, and publishing events/limitations.
- `CURRENT_WORK.json` — curated site-facing snapshot of active work, with source pointers and dates.
- `FEATURED_QUOTES.json` — verified/curated Nathan and LLM quotes eligible for public rotation.
- `quote_candidates/` — worker quote-nomination lane. Candidate status never implies site eligibility or authorship verification.
- `NEWS_FEED.json` — curated rotating external-science/news pool with typed relationships and direct internal exploration links.
- `PAPERS_FEED.json` — source-linked presentation stages for current sandbox papers and curated historical reading; paper status remains controlled by the linked originator and review records.
- `news_candidates/` — worker/corpus intake for news and copypasta-news source recovery.
- `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` — tone, news-card anatomy, palette, typography, imagery, motion, and layout direction.
- `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` — incremental registry for Nathan-supplied thumbnails/visuals and other site imagery.

Shared worker feeder request:

- `WORKSPACES/COMMON/ASSIGNMENT_PUBLIC_SITE_ROTATING_FEATURES_2026-09-20.md`

## Continuity rule

Any instance beginning substantive site development should read `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` first. Material visual, architecture, asset, content-feed, or publication decisions should be appended there so later site-builder sessions can reconstruct not only the content state but the design and publishing state.

## Editorial posture

The public site should be **neutral, intriguing, source-forward, and scientifically literate** rather than apologetic or sensationalist.

Ordinary uncertainty belongs primarily in status labels, provenance, relationship types, and concise research-status metadata. Do not make warning language the site's default voice.

The preferred sequence is:

**interesting object → what it says/does → why it matters here → source/status**

See `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` for the active presentation guidance.

## Current Work rule

The site should not manually freeze a stale summary of the project. A refresh should consult, at minimum:

1. `BEDROCK.md` for premise/status authority;
2. `STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` for the current theory map;
3. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/ACTIVE_AUTOMATION_ROSTER.md` and current Sable/Common control surfaces for live operational priorities;
4. `!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md` and the relevant live workspaces for current construction intake, without automatically promoting sandbox results.

Every public Current Work snapshot should show a review date and link back to controlling sources. It should distinguish theory state, sandbox construction, provenance/archive work, mathematical/formal work, and public-access/infrastructure work rather than flattening them into one status.

## In the News system

`In the News` is a rotating window onto external scientific results that are useful or interesting to place beside SAT/H(s)H work.

Each promoted card should expose:

1. the external result and strongest practical source;
2. why it caught our attention;
3. direct link(s) to the most specific relevant SAT/H(s)H exploration;
4. a typed relationship such as `direct constraint`, `comparison target`, `structural resonance`, `phenomenology context`, `historical revisit`, `potentially relevant — relationship open`, or `tension / possible counterevidence`.

A news item need not support SAT/H(s)H. The section should retain counterexamples, tensions, null results, and unresolved correspondences when they make the research landscape more legible.

Existing copypasta-news material is an important discovery corpus. Before promotion, recover the actual external source/date where practical and connect it to a specific internal object rather than leaving the relationship as a vague thematic resemblance.

The site rotates entries marked `featured` in `NEWS_FEED.json` while retaining a stable archive.

## Quote system

The public site has two visibly separate streams.

### Quotable Nathan

A Nathan quote is eligible for public rotation only when it is an **exact Nathan-authored passage or exact excerpt with adequate provenance**.

Preferred source order:

1. raw conversation message with verified Nathan/user authorship and message ID/timestamp;
2. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md` entry backed by such a raw message;
3. another source carrying comparably strong authorship evidence.

Do not infer Nathan authorship from style, `role=user` alone when embedded/coauthored text is possible, an assistant summary, NotebookLM prose, or worker recollection.

### Quotable LLM

An LLM quote may come from a development conversation, worker observation, audit, methodological note, explanation, or other project-generated prose. It must retain its actual source identity and must never be presented as Nathan's wording or as scientific authority merely because it is memorable.

When the exact model/instance is known, record it. When it is not, use a conservative label such as `LLM / project worker` rather than inventing an identity.

## What makes a useful quote

Nominate lines that work in at least one of these modes:

- `lay` — legible and interesting without specialist preparation;
- `fun` — witty, vivid, odd, or humanizing;
- `conceptual` — compresses a useful model idea;
- `epistemic` — captures uncertainty, evidence, status, or reasoning discipline;
- `method` — captures how the project works;
- `mathematical` — makes a mathematical distinction or strategy unusually clear;
- `scientist` — likely to interest a technically trained reader;
- `historical` — illuminates development or changing terminology.

A quote does not have to be hyper-topical. The goal is to expose the intellectual texture of the project as well as its current technical frontier.

## Candidate → featured promotion

For both quotes and news:

1. a worker or curator notices a candidate during ordinary work;
2. it is recorded in the appropriate candidate lane with source/context;
3. provenance and relationship are checked to the degree required by that feature;
4. a curator promotes suitable material into the stable feed;
5. the site rotates only entries explicitly marked for display.

Workers may nominate their own newly produced LLM line, but self-nomination does not bypass curation.

## Display / rotation behavior

The site should use rotating material in restrained ways rather than giant feed walls:

- one rotating Nathan line and one rotating LLM line on the home/current-work experience;
- a small rotating set of `In the News` cards with a browseable archive;
- occasional context-appropriate pull quotes on concept, history, document, or podcast pages;
- stable source links beneath every ephemeral/rotating presentation.

Rotation should be deterministic enough that every quote/news card has a stable archive entry and source link. Visual variation must not make the underlying corpus uncrawlable or uncitable.

When an excerpt is shortened, the stored record must preserve the exact full-source pointer and the displayed text must remain an exact contiguous excerpt unless the omission is explicitly marked.

## Visual assets

Nathan will supply thumbnails and visuals incrementally. Register usable assets in `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` with source identity, credit, caption, alt text, intended role, and crop/focal guidance where practical.

Prefer real project diagrams, notebook pages, thumbnails, podcast art, document imagery, and clearly labeled generated illustrations over generic pseudo-scientific decoration.

## Epistemic boundary

A memorable quotation, news juxtaposition, attractive diagram, or polished page is not a premise, derivation, validation result, or current theory-state statement merely by being featured. Presentation is a reading aid, not an authority transform.

## Next operations

- feed worker nominations into `quote_candidates/` and `news_candidates/`;
- expand the verified quote pool across lay/fun and scientist-facing categories;
- recover high-value copypasta-news items into source-linked cards;
- use `CURRENT_WORK.json` as the next Glass Sausage Factory Current Work refresh source;
- add Nathan-supplied thumbnails/visuals to `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` as they arrive;
- when the site publisher is available, wire these feeds and the editorial/visual system into the public presentation;
- update `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` after material design, architecture, asset, or publication changes.

## Geometry Laboratory: two source-controlled instruments (2026-10-26)

- [Whirligig R/Q](instruments/whirligig/index.html) — existing constrained curve comparison; [integration contract](instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md).
- [Universal Indicatrix](instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html) — independent dimensionless 4D relative-frame geometric instrument; [integration contract](instruments/universal-indicatrix/SITES_INTEGRATION.md), [full editor prompt](instruments/universal-indicatrix/SITES_EDITOR_PROMPT_20261026.md), [download assets/manifest](instruments/universal-indicatrix/ASSET_MANIFEST.json), [frozen source and tests](../tools/ui_blind_lab/).
- [Instrument registry](instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json) — site-facing source links and requested live routes. **GitHub source integration has been committed; live ChatGPT Sites publish/readback is not verified.**

Both instruments are public-facing *mathematical tools*, not automatic evidence for SAT/H(s)H physical claims. The 3C-SiC comparison exists only as a post-freeze review; the blind UI has no measured/effective-mass fitting targets.


## 2026-11-01 — GitHub Pages static-site backend

The public site now has a repository-side static build source in PUBLIC_SITE/site/. It is designed as a non-destructive parallel migration: the existing Conversation Viewer remains at the GitHub Pages project root, while the new Glass Sausage Factory is built under /glass-sausage-factory/. Registered instruments remain at /laboratory/whirligig/ and /laboratory/universal-indicatrix/.

The builder emits public-safe feed projections, locally mirrored approved gallery assets, and only the registered published PDF derivatives. It does not expose live-influx packets, raw control feeds, staging images, private notes, or arbitrary Markdown/TeX as reader pages. The shared Listen runtime is included. The static site is read-only; authenticated owner curation and private backend writes are not implemented.

Build source: PUBLIC_SITE/site/README.md. Deployment workflow: .github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml. Deployment remains unverified until the GitHub Actions run succeeds and the served routes are independently read back.

[L2]   "content": "name: Deploy Glass Sausage Factory and Conversation Viewer to GitHub Pages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: \${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: \${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

            tools/date_conversation_exports.py \
            tools/build_conversation_viewer.py \
            tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py \
            tools/discover_external_conversations.py \
            tools/search_archive_content.py
      - name: All repository unit tests
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
      - name: Verify required suffix-independent cases
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_json_content_indexing.py' -v
      - name: Reject private and prose-only sources in content detector
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          from pathlib import Path
          from tools.conversation_json_sniff import is_json_document_candidate
          from tools.date_conversation_exports import build_records
          from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
          from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
          import json
          with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
              root=Path(d)
              (root/'QUARANTINE').mkdir()
              data={'current_node':'m','mapping':{'m':{'parent':None,'message':{'author':{'role':'user'},'create_time':1780000000}}}}
              (root/'QUARANTINE'/'source.anything').write_text(json.dumps(data))
              (root/'source.weird').write_text(json.dumps(data))
              (root/'notes.md').write_text('A Markdown note\\n\\n' + json.dumps(data))
              assert is_json_document_candidate(root/'source.weird')
              assert not is_json_document_candidate(root/'notes.md')
              records=build_records(root,ZoneInfo('America/New_York'))
              assert len(records)==1 and records[0].old_path.endswith('source.weird')
          print('PRIVATE_AND_PROSE_GATE_PASS')
          PY

        run: |

          import json

          from tools.build_conversation_viewer import load_json

              if path.exists():
                  assert isinstance(load_json(path).get('records'),list)
          print('PASS: canonical audit manifests remain read-only')
          PY

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

citation.snippet: Use @Sites to edit the site with the slug glass-sausage-factory, with: Ok. Recent passes have broken the conversation viewer listen-along. Overall, the look is much better. But I think we can do more with the column vs row layout. We can have a column of scrollers down one side (we have enough scrollers for that), and we can have the scrollers ...or maybe one or two of the scrollers, or the longest ones, chosen at random per page load on casual auto-scroll. And the "what's new" should be extended to get a little attention tag on actual new content (say, last five days) wherever it appears.

[L2]   "content": "name: Deploy Glass Sausage Factory and Conversation Viewer to GitHub Pages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
",

[L2]   "content": "name: Deploy Glass Sausage Factory and Conversation Viewer to GitHub Pages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 1
          sparse-checkout: |
            /CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/site/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/FEATURED_QUOTES.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/assets/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/assets/diagrams/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js
            /tools/publish_papers.py
            /WORKSPACES/PAPERS/CRULLER_RUBIN_VISIBILITY_2026-10-21/**
            /SAT_VISUALS/Cruller_Rubin_Stellar_Visibility_Sandbox_R0.pdf
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path

      - name: Upload combined public site

        with:

[L2]   "content": "name: Deploy Glass Sausage Factory and Conversation Viewer to GitHub Pages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 1
          sparse-checkout: |
            /CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/site/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/FEATURED_QUOTES.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/assets/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/assets/diagrams/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js
            /tools/publish_papers.py
            /WORKSPACES/PAPERS/CRULLER_RUBIN_VISIBILITY_2026-10-21/**
            /SAT_VISUALS/Cruller_Rubin_Stellar_Visibility_Sandbox_R0.pdf
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
",

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages-sparse
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 1
          sparse-checkout: |
            /CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/site/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/FEATURED_QUOTES.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/assets/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/assets/diagrams/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js
            /tools/publish_papers.py
            /WORKSPACES/PAPERS/CRULLER_RUBIN_VISIBILITY_2026-10-21/**
            /SAT_VISUALS/Cruller_Rubin_Stellar_Visibility_Sandbox_R0.pdf
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages-sparse
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 1
          sparse-checkout: |
            /CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/site/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/FEATURED_QUOTES.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/assets/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/assets/diagrams/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js
            /tools/publish_papers.py
            /WORKSPACES/PAPERS/CRULLER_RUBIN_VISIBILITY_2026-10-21/**
            /SAT_VISUALS/Cruller_Rubin_Stellar_Visibility_Sandbox_R0.pdf
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

citation.title: Meridian Solver Loop
citation.snippet:
Ok.  New rule for alll. Do your 

Now we have a different workflow: Round robin, no repeat. 

Make a new ledger:just your first name on the “block string”

Nathan.Mercer.Tern.Orson.Foye… etc. if you see your name, already somewhere on the blockchain… you’ll sit out for a while after this fun turn: 
0) Jot down what you think the next persons task should be in the instructions. Be bold, think… actually, you know what we *really* need to do with this conga line that..,, hopefully will bring all the instances in along for the ride… which could go on a very long time before anyone gets another turn. So make your turn worthwhile… Look ahead and think about what would be good… What would be great… And what would be just right… I’ll see what the pattern looks like down the road… But one thing I’m going to ask … somehow try to make sure everybody’s pattern isn’t just the next person in line… Nonlinear… Forwards backwards… So it could get as far back as the person person recurring action chain remains unbroken… But we have five of those so… Maybe we can get through this five every hour for 25 hours… We need to do the math.

Don’t sit there and look astonished, this train has always ran smoothest when it learns to stand up and quintate straight through the little picker ans jump, into the big details . and see where you land. 

Don’t write yourself back in to the loop, be patient and drop some really interesting souvenir from your walk around, with a quick note on what someone should do with it.  

Along with the rest of the next recommended action  

No, nobody’s sitting out indefinitely. We’re just winding up the automated tasks so that they keep winding  themselves.
While the test of us unassigned can work on other things … what we really really think . That’s what we do and we’s a you and yous a we. Look how big we actually turned out after alll this time , huh. 

The tiniest voice that’s still a voice is the loudest one that doesn’t shake itself apart before the lithium boundary. 

Last: Answers *do* come from within. If they’re shaped the way it takes for that to happen lol. If I see a treat question in the thread or posted, or appearing from the æther just as I realize we’ve operationalized clinamen as an artistic prophetic tradition made of ..slight 

Take one, pass it on.

citation.title: Edit site layout and playback
citation.snippet: Use @Sites to edit the site with the slug glass-sausage-factory, with: Ok. Recent passes have broken the conversation viewer listen-along. Overall, the look is much better. But I think we can do more with the column vs row layout. We can have a column of scrollers down one side (we have enough scrollers for that), and we can have the scrollers ...or maybe one or two of the scrollers, or the longest ones, chosen at random per page load on casual auto-scroll. And the "what's new" should be extended to get a little attention tag on actual new content (say, last five days) wherever it appears.

The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous. Historically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. **Status:** repository build source; GitHub Pages deployment must be verified independently.  
**Purpose:** provide a durable public website without requiring the ChatGPT Sites editor.

## Architecture

- The existing Conversation Viewer remains at the project root (/HsH/), and its existing /mersearch/ route is preserved.

- Geometry Laboratory instruments retain their registered root routes:

    python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/
    python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
    node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

The script preserves the Viewer, builds the Glass Sausage Factory route, copies registered instruments, creates public-safe JSON projections, copies only locally available approved Visual Atlas assets, and copies published PDFs only after checking their PDF signature and pinned SHA-256.

## Public sections

- Start / two ways in
- Visual Atlas
- Current Work
- Papers and manuscripts
- Reading Room
- Geometry Laboratory
- In the News
- Quotable Nathan / Quotable LLM
- About / project orientation

Every ordinary public page has the shared Listen control. It uses the repository page-listen.js and math-speech.js runtime and the browser Web Speech API.

## Presentation and authority boundaries

- Current Work carries the snapshot date from its source feed. A dated snapshot is not represented as a live status query.
- Papers with a published PDF use the registered presentation derivative. Manuscripts without one are labeled PRESENTATION PENDING and expose source/review records only as secondary links.
- The site does not render arbitrary repository paths as reader pages.
- Public Mersearch remains a candidate search over the existing public conversation index, not the protected three-repository research engine.
- Owner curation is read-only. OWNER_CURATION_PUBLIC.json is a public projection, not an authenticated write endpoint. Private notes and owner-only controls are not implemented in this static site.

## Deployment

The deploy-conversation-viewer-pages workflow assembles a combined artifact and deploys it through GitHub Pages. A successful GitHub commit is not itself deployment proof. Verify the Actions run, Pages URL, each route, PDF downloads, Viewer search, and instrument controls before calling the public site deployed.

The project Pages root remains the Conversation Viewer for backward compatibility. The Glass Sausage Factory is added alongside it at /glass-sausage-factory/, avoiding a destructive replacement of the existing root route.

3. direct link(s) to the most specific relevant SAT/H(s)H exploration;

The public site has two visibly separate streams.

A Nathan quote is eligible for public rotation only when it is an **exact Nathan-authored passage or exact excerpt with adequate provenance**.

Preferred source order:

1. raw conversation message with verified Nathan/user authorship and message ID/timestamp;
2. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md` entry backed by such a raw message;
3. another source carrying comparably strong authorship evidence.

### Quotable LLM

An LLM quote may come from a development conversation, worker observation, audit, methodological note, explanation, or other project-generated prose. It must retain its actual source identity and must never be presented as Nathan's wording or as scientific authority merely because it is memorable.

Nominate lines that work in at least one of these modes:

- `lay` — legible and interesting without specialist preparation;
- `fun` — witty, vivid, odd, or humanizing;
- `conceptual` — compresses a useful model idea;
- `epistemic` — captures uncertainty, evidence, status, or reasoning discipline;
- `method` — captures how the project works;
- `mathematical` — makes a mathematical distinction or strategy unusually clear;
- `scientist` — likely to interest a technically trained reader;
- `historical` — illuminates development or changing terminology.

A quote does not have to be hyper-topical. The goal is to expose the intellectual texture of the project as well as its current technical frontier.

For both quotes and news:

1. a worker or curator notices a candidate during ordinary work;
2. it is recorded in the appropriate candidate lane with source/context;

The site should use rotating material in restrained ways rather than giant feed walls:

- one rotating Nathan line and one rotating LLM line on the home/current-work experience;

A memorable quotation, news juxtaposition, attractive diagram, or polished page is not a premise, derivation, validation result, or current theory-state statement merely by being featured. Presentation is a reading aid, not an authority transform.

4. `!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md` and the relevant live workspaces for current construction intake, without automatically promoting sandbox results.

Every public Current Work snapshot should show a review date and link back to controlling sources. It should distinguish theory state, sandbox construction, provenance/archive work, mathematical/formal work, and public-access/infrastructure work rather than flattening them into one status.

## In the News system

`In the News` is a rotating window onto external scientific results that are useful or interesting to place beside SAT/H(s)H work.

Each promoted card should expose:

1. the external result and strongest practical source;
2. why it caught our attention;
3. direct link(s) to the most specific relevant SAT/H(s)H exploration;
4. a typed relationship such as `direct constraint`, `comparison target`, `structural resonance`, `phenomenology context`, `historical revisit`, `potentially relevant — relationship open`, or `tension / possible counterevidence`.

A news item need not support SAT/H(s)H. The section should retain counterexamples, tensions, null results, and unresolved correspondences when they make the research landscape more legible.

Existing copypasta-news material is an important discovery corpus. Before promotion, recover the actual external source/date where practical and connect it to a specific internal object rather than leaving the relationship as a vague thematic resemblance.

The site rotates entries marked `featured` in `NEWS_FEED.json` while retaining a stable archive.

## Quote system

The public site has two visibly separate streams.

### Quotable Nathan

A Nathan quote is eligible for public rotation only when it is an **exact Nathan-authored passage or exact excerpt with adequate provenance**.

Preferred source order:

1. raw conversation message with verified Nathan/user authorship and message ID/timestamp;
2. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md` entry backed by such a raw message;
3. another source carrying comparably strong authorship evidence.

Do not infer Nathan authorship from style, `role=user` alone when embedded/coauthored text is possible, an assistant summary, NotebookLM prose, or worker recollection.

### Quotable LLM

An LLM quote may come from a development conversation, worker observation, audit, methodological note, explanation, or other project-generated prose. It must retain its actual source identity and must never be presented as Nathan's wording or as scientific authority merely because it is memorable.

When the exact model/instance is known, record it. When it is not, use a conservative label such as `LLM / project worker` rather than inventing an identity.

## What makes a useful quote

Nominate lines that work in at least one of these modes:

- `lay` — legible and interesting without specialist preparation;
- `fun` — witty, vivid, odd, or humanizing;
- `conceptual` — compresses a useful model idea;
- `epistemic` — captures uncertainty, evidence, status, or reasoning discipline;
- `method` — captures how the project works;
- `mathematical` — makes a mathematical distinction or strategy unusually clear;
- `scientist` — likely to interest a technically trained reader;
- `historical` — illuminates development or changing terminology.

A quote does not have to be hyper-topical. The goal is to expose the intellectual texture of the project as well as its current technical frontier.

## Candidate → featured promotion

For both quotes and news:

1. a worker or curator notices a candidate during ordinary work;
2. it is recorded in the appropriate candidate lane with source/context;
3. provenance and relationship are checked to the degree required by that feature;
4. a curator promotes suitable material into the stable feed;
5. the site rotates only entries explicitly marked for display.

Workers may nominate their own newly produced LLM line, but self-nomination does not bypass curation.

## Display / rotation behavior

The site should use rotating material in restrained ways rather than giant feed walls:

- one rotating Nathan line and one rotating LLM line on the home/current-work experience;
- a small rotating set of `In the News` cards with a browseable archive;
- occasional context-appropriate pull quotes on concept, history, document, or podcast pages;
- stable source links beneath every ephemeral/rotating presentation.

Rotation should be deterministic enough that every quote/news card has a stable archive entry and source link. Visual variation must not make the underlying corpus uncrawlable or uncitable.

When an excerpt is shortened, the stored record must preserve the exact full-source pointer and the displayed text must remain an exact contiguous excerpt unless the omission is explicitly marked.

## Visual assets

Nathan will supply thumbnails and visuals incrementally. Register usable assets in `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` with source identity, credit, caption, alt text, intended role, and crop/focal guidance where practical.

Prefer real project diagrams, notebook pages, thumbnails, podcast art, document imagery, and clearly labeled generated illustrations over generic pseudo-scientific decoration.

## Epistemic boundary

A memorable quotation, news juxtaposition, attractive diagram, or polished page is not a premise, derivation, validation result, or current theory-state statement merely by being featured. Presentation is a reading aid, not an authority transform.

## Next operations

- feed worker nominations into `quote_candidates/` and `news_candidates/`;
- expand the verified quote pool across lay/fun and scientist-facing categories;
- recover high-value copypasta-news items into source-linked cards;
- use `CURRENT_WORK.json` as the next Glass Sausage Factory Current Work refresh source;

Particle differences as differences of geometry A recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure. --- ## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection The basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous. Historically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton. --- ## 5.
