on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/index.html'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/mersearch/**'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.js'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.css'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/**'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer.py'
      - 'tools/conversation_json_sniff.py'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py'
      - 'indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/EXTERNAL_CONVERSATIONS.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: conversation-viewer-pages
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Validate resolved catalog, rather than overwriting public GLASS discovery
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',
                len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload conversation viewer
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: CONVERSATION_VIEWER

      - name: Deploy conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

[L2]   "content": "name: Deploy Glass Sausage Factory and Conversation Viewer to GitHub Pages

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/site/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/*.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/assets/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js'
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js'
      - 'tools/publish_papers.py'
      - 'SAT_VISUALS/**'
      - '.github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: glass-sausage-factory-pages-sparse
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 1
          sparse-checkout: |
            /CONVERSATION_VIEWER/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/site/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/CURRENT_WORK.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/FEATURED_QUOTES.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/NEWS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS_FEED.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/ASSET_MANIFEST.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/generated/papers.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/PAPERS/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html
            /PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/universal-indicatrix/assets/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/assets/diagrams/**
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/page-listen.js
            /PUBLIC_SITE/runtime/math-speech.js
            /tools/publish_papers.py
            /WORKSPACES/PAPERS/CRULLER_RUBIN_VISIBILITY_2026-10-21/**
            /SAT_VISUALS/Cruller_Rubin_Stellar_Visibility_Sandbox_R0.pdf
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Validate resolved Viewer catalog and curation
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Validate published paper PDFs
        run: python tools/publish_papers.py --check

      - name: Test static site builder
        run: |
          python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
          node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

      - name: Build combined public site artifact
        run: python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload combined public site
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy combined public site
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
",

[L2]   "content": "# Glass Sausage Factory — public-site content feed

**Status:** ACTIVE public-facing content infrastructure  
**Scope:** repository-side source material for the SAT/H(s)H Glass Sausage Factory site  
**Authority:** navigation/presentation only; this directory does not define theory truth  
**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive

## Purpose

Keep the public site supplied from durable, source-linked repository state instead of letting important public-facing material exist only inside a site-builder session.

This layer supports:

- a genuinely current **Current Work** section;

[L2]   "content": "# Glass Sausage Factory — public-site content feed

**Status:** ACTIVE public-facing content infrastructure  
**Scope:** repository-side source material for the SAT/H(s)H Glass Sausage Factory site  
**Authority:** navigation/presentation only; this directory does not define theory truth  
**Established:** 2026-09-20 by Nathan directive

## Purpose

Keep the public site supplied from durable, source-linked repository state instead of letting important public-facing material exist only inside a site-builder session.

This layer supports:

- a genuinely current **Current Work** section;
- rotating **Quotable Nathan** and **Quotable LLM** features;
- a rotating **In the News** feature connecting external results to specific SAT/H(s)H explorations;
- incremental visual/thumbnail curation with provenance and accessibility metadata;
- later site-facing indexes for documents, podcasts, glossary entries, images, and other presentation-ready material;
- clear separation between readable presentation and source/theory authority.

The controlling project record remains the repositories. A polished site rendering does not change theory status.

## Current files

- `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` — durable continuity/handoff record for design decisions, current site state, asset intake, open work, and publishing events/limitations.
- `CURRENT_WORK.json` — curated site-facing snapshot of active work, with source pointers and dates.
- `FEATURED_QUOTES.json` — verified/curated Nathan and LLM quotes eligible for public rotation.
- `quote_candidates/` — worker quote-nomination lane. Candidate status never implies site eligibility or authorship verification.
- `NEWS_FEED.json` — curated rotating external-science/news pool with typed relationships and direct internal exploration links.
- `PAPERS_FEED.json` — source-linked presentation stages for current sandbox papers and curated historical reading; paper status remains controlled by the linked originator and review records.
- `news_candidates/` — worker/corpus intake for news and copypasta-news source recovery.
- `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` — tone, news-card anatomy, palette, typography, imagery, motion, and layout direction.
- `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` — incremental registry for Nathan-supplied thumbnails/visuals and other site imagery.

Shared worker feeder request:

- `WORKSPACES/COMMON/ASSIGNMENT_PUBLIC_SITE_ROTATING_FEATURES_2026-09-20.md`

## Continuity rule

Any instance beginning substantive site development should read `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` first. Material visual, architecture, asset, content-feed, or publication decisions should be appended there so later site-builder sessions can reconstruct not only the content state but the design and publishing state.

## Editorial posture

The public site should be **neutral, intriguing, source-forward, and scientifically literate** rather than apologetic or sensationalist.

Ordinary uncertainty belongs primarily in status labels, provenance, relationship types, and concise research-status metadata. Do not make warning language the site's default voice.

The preferred sequence is:

**interesting object → what it says/does → why it matters here → source/status**

See `EDITORIAL_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md` for the active presentation guidance.

## Current Work rule

The site should not manually freeze a stale summary of the project. A refresh should consult, at minimum:

1. `BEDROCK.md` for premise/status authority;
2. `STATE_OF_THE_THEORY.md` for the current theory map;
3. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/ACTIVE_AUTOMATION_ROSTER.md` and current Sable/Common control surfaces for live operational priorities;
4. `!!_RUNNING_COTHEORIST_LOG.md` and the relevant live workspaces for current construction intake, without automatically promoting sandbox results.

Every public Current Work snapshot should show a review date and link back to controlling sources. It should distinguish theory state, sandbox construction, provenance/archive work, mathematical/formal work, and public-access/infrastructure work rather than flattening them into one status.

## In the News system

`In the News` is a rotating window onto external scientific results that are useful or interesting to place beside SAT/H(s)H work.

Each promoted card should expose:

1. the external result and strongest practical source;
2. why it caught our attention;
3. direct link(s) to the most specific relevant SAT/H(s)H exploration;
4. a typed relationship such as `direct constraint`, `comparison target`, `structural resonance`, `phenomenology context`, `historical revisit`, `potentially relevant — relationship open`, or `tension / possible counterevidence`.

A news item need not support SAT/H(s)H. The section should retain counterexamples, tensions, null results, and unresolved correspondences when they make the research landscape more legible.

Existing copypasta-news material is an important discovery corpus. Before promotion, recover the actual external source/date where practical and connect it to a specific internal object rather than leaving the relationship as a vague thematic resemblance.

The site rotates entries marked `featured` in `NEWS_FEED.json` while retaining a stable archive.

## Quote system

The public site has two visibly separate streams.

### Quotable Nathan

A Nathan quote is eligible for public rotation only when it is an **exact Nathan-authored passage or exact excerpt with adequate provenance**.

Preferred source order:

1. raw conversation message with verified Nathan/user authorship and message ID/timestamp;
2. `WORKSPACES/COMMON/NATHAN_VERIFIED_WORDS_COMPENDIUM.md` entry backed by such a raw message;
3. another source carrying comparably strong authorship evidence.

Do not infer Nathan authorship from style, `role=user` alone when embedded/coauthored text is possible, an assistant summary, NotebookLM prose, or worker recollection.

### Quotable LLM

An LLM quote may come from a development conversation, worker observation, audit, methodological note, explanation, or other project-generated prose. It must retain its actual source identity and must never be presented as Nathan's wording or as scientific authority merely because it is memorable.

When the exact model/instance is known, record it. When it is not, use a conservative label such as `LLM / project worker` rather than inventing an identity.

## What makes a useful quote

Nominate lines that work in at least one of these modes:

- `lay` — legible and interesting without specialist preparation;
- `fun` — witty, vivid, odd, or humanizing;
- `conceptual` — compresses a useful model idea;
- `epistemic` — captures uncertainty, evidence, status, or reasoning discipline;
- `method` — captures how the project works;
- `mathematical` — makes a mathematical distinction or strategy unusually clear;
- `scientist` — likely to interest a technically trained reader;
- `historical` — illuminates development or changing terminology.

A quote does not have to be hyper-topical. The goal is to expose the intellectual texture of the project as well as its current technical frontier.

## Candidate → featured promotion

For both quotes and news:

1. a worker or curator notices a candidate during ordinary work;
2. it is recorded in the appropriate candidate lane with source/context;
3. provenance and relationship are checked to the degree required by that feature;
4. a curator promotes suitable material into the stable feed;
5. the site rotates only entries explicitly marked for display.

Workers may nominate their own newly produced LLM line, but self-nomination does not bypass curation.

## Display / rotation behavior

The site should use rotating material in restrained ways rather than giant feed walls:

- one rotating Nathan line and one rotating LLM line on the home/current-work experience;
- a small rotating set of `In the News` cards with a browseable archive;
- occasional context-appropriate pull quotes on concept, history, document, or podcast pages;
- stable source links beneath every ephemeral/rotating presentation.

Rotation should be deterministic enough that every quote/news card has a stable archive entry and source link. Visual variation must not make the underlying corpus uncrawlable or uncitable.

When an excerpt is shortened, the stored record must preserve the exact full-source pointer and the displayed text must remain an exact contiguous excerpt unless the omission is explicitly marked.

## Visual assets

Nathan will supply thumbnails and visuals incrementally. Register usable assets in `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` with source identity, credit, caption, alt text, intended role, and crop/focal guidance where practical.

Prefer real project diagrams, notebook pages, thumbnails, podcast art, document imagery, and clearly labeled generated illustrations over generic pseudo-scientific decoration.

## Epistemic boundary

A memorable quotation, news juxtaposition, attractive diagram, or polished page is not a premise, derivation, validation result, or current theory-state statement merely by being featured. Presentation is a reading aid, not an authority transform.

## Next operations

- feed worker nominations into `quote_candidates/` and `news_candidates/`;
- expand the verified quote pool across lay/fun and scientist-facing categories;
- recover high-value copypasta-news items into source-linked cards;
- use `CURRENT_WORK.json` as the next Glass Sausage Factory Current Work refresh source;
- add Nathan-supplied thumbnails/visuals to `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` as they arrive;
- when the site publisher is available, wire these feeds and the editorial/visual system into the public presentation;
- update `SITE_DEVELOPMENT_WORK_LOG.md` after material design, architecture, asset, or publication changes.

## Geometry Laboratory: two source-controlled instruments (2026-10-26)

- [Whirligig R/Q](instruments/whirligig/index.html) — existing constrained curve comparison; [integration contract](instruments/whirligig/SITES_INTEGRATION.md).
- [Universal Indicatrix](instruments/universal-indicatrix/index.html) — independent dimensionless 4D relative-frame geometric instrument; [integration contract](instruments/universal-indicatrix/SITES_INTEGRATION.md), [full editor prompt](instruments/universal-indicatrix/SITES_EDITOR_PROMPT_20261026.md), [download assets/manifest](instruments/universal-indicatrix/ASSET_MANIFEST.json), [frozen source and tests](../tools/ui_blind_lab/).
- [Instrument registry](instruments/INSTRUMENT_REGISTRY.json) — site-facing source links and requested live routes. **GitHub source integration has been committed; live ChatGPT Sites publish/readback is not verified.**

Both instruments are public-facing *mathematical tools*, not automatic evidence for SAT/H(s)H physical claims. The 3C-SiC comparison exists only as a post-freeze review; the blind UI has no measured/effective-mass fitting targets.


## 2026-11-01 — GitHub Pages static-site backend

The public site now has a repository-side static build source in PUBLIC_SITE/site/. It is designed as a non-destructive parallel migration: the existing Conversation Viewer remains at the GitHub Pages project root, while the new Glass Sausage Factory is built under /glass-sausage-factory/. Registered instruments remain at /laboratory/whirligig/ and /laboratory/universal-indicatrix/.

The builder emits public-safe feed projections, locally mirrored approved gallery assets, and only the registered published PDF derivatives. It does not expose live-influx packets, raw control feeds, staging images, private notes, or arbitrary Markdown/TeX as reader pages. The shared Listen runtime is included. The static site is read-only; authenticated owner curation and private backend writes are not implemented.

Build source: PUBLIC_SITE/site/README.md. Deployment workflow: .github/workflows/deploy-conversation-viewer-pages.yml. Deployment remains unverified until the GitHub Actions run succeeds and the served routes are independently read back.

## 2026-11-02 — GitHub Pages publication

The repository-backed static site has now been deployed successfully through GitHub Actions. The public Factory route is https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/glass-sausage-factory/. The existing Conversation Viewer remains at https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/, with /conversations/ as an alias; public Mersearch remains at /mersearch/, with /research/search/ as an alias. The two registered instruments are built at /laboratory/whirligig/ and /laboratory/universal-indicatrix/.

[L2]   "content": "# Glass Sausage Factory: static site build

**Status:** repository build source; GitHub Pages deployment must be verified independently.  
**Purpose:** provide a durable public website without requiring the ChatGPT Sites editor.

## Architecture

- The existing Conversation Viewer remains at the project root (/HsH/), and its existing /mersearch/ route is preserved.
- The new Glass Sausage Factory site is built at /HsH/glass-sausage-factory/.
- Geometry Laboratory instruments retain their registered root routes:
  - /HsH/laboratory/whirligig/
  - /HsH/laboratory/universal-indicatrix/
- /HsH/conversations/ and /HsH/research/search/ are friendly aliases to the preserved Viewer and public Mersearch reader.

The build is static HTML, CSS and JavaScript. GitHub Actions assembles the Pages artifact from the HsH repository. No ChatGPT Sites editor session or paid Sites feature is required.

## Build locally

From the repository root:

    python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/
    python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
    node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

The script preserves the Viewer, builds the Glass Sausage Factory route, copies registered instruments, creates public-safe JSON projections, copies only locally available approved Visual Atlas assets, and copies published PDFs only after checking their PDF signature and pinned SHA-256.

## Public sections

- Start / two ways in
- Visual Atlas
- Current Work
- Papers and manuscripts
- Reading Room
- Geometry Laboratory
- In the News
- Quotable Nathan / Quotable LLM
- About / project orientation

Every ordinary public page has the shared Listen control. It uses the repository page-listen.js and math-speech.js runtime and the browser Web Speech API.

## Presentation and authority boundaries

- Current Work carries the snapshot date from its source feed. A dated snapshot is not represented as a live status query.
- Papers with a published PDF use the registered presentation derivative. Manuscripts without one are labeled PRESENTATION PENDING and expose source/review records only as secondary links.
- The site does not render arbitrary repository paths as reader pages.
- Public Mersearch remains a candidate search over the existing public conversation index, not the protected three-repository research engine.
- Owner curation is read-only. OWNER_CURATION_PUBLIC.json is a public projection, not an authenticated write endpoint. Private notes and owner-only controls are not implemented in this static site.
- Eight legacy approved illustration entries still point to the previous ChatGPT Sites asset host. They are not hotlinked. The build admits only approved local assets with repository-backed paths; the older images can be mirrored after source retrieval and provenance verification.

## Deployment

The deploy-conversation-viewer-pages workflow assembles a combined artifact and deploys it through GitHub Pages. A successful GitHub commit is not itself deployment proof. Verify the Actions run, Pages URL, each route, PDF downloads, Viewer search, and instrument controls before calling the public site deployed.

The project Pages root remains the Conversation Viewer for backward compatibility. The Glass Sausage Factory is added alongside it at /glass-sausage-factory/, avoiding a destructive replacement of the existing root route.

## Deployment status — 2026-11-02

The initial GitHub Pages deployment succeeded (Actions run 41390830237; source commit 4614672c157772cb1544384679e4cd47ecb9abd1). The new Factory route is https://satobloc.github.io/HsH/glass-sausage-factory/. The existing Viewer root is preserved. A subsequent confirmation deploy is running against the latest workflow revision. Deployment action success is verified; a separate visual browser smoke-test is still pending.

# Whirligig | Glass Sausage Factory integration

**Status:** REPOSITORY-PUBLISHED / SITES FRONTEND NOT VERIFIED
**Date:** 2026-10-16
**Presentation class:** interactive geometry instrument (executable HTML), not a reader document or machine/control dump.

## Visitor object
- Public title: **Whirligig — Interactive Geometry Laboratory**
- Subtitle: **Two rotations, one evolving trace**
- Recommended Sites route: `/laboratory/whirligig/`
- Canonical source: `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html`
- Primary experience: 3D sphere / torus mapping; 4D Indicatrix rotation mode
- Interactions: independent rotor rates, phase, amplitude, coupling, radius, scrubbable observation parameter, orbit camera, pause/play, SVG export.
- Position within site: Geometry / solvers and Visual Atlas, with a homepage laboratory teaser where editorially appropriate.
- Accessibility: responsive layout, labeled sliders and buttons, text explanation; native canvas needs supplementary explanatory text and alternative presentation for non-visual use.

## Relationship to research engine
The existing `tools/whirligig_rq/` research reconstruction is **not replaced**. Its actual rolling sphere, orthogonal internal gimbals, R–Q connector, Bishop frame and torus quartic ray intersection tests are numerically developed and documented in `tools/whirligig_rq/README.md` and `RESULTS.md`. **Date:** 2026-10-17

## Design

Each input must provide an explicit dimensionless periodic *scalar representative* `f(λ)`, with λ ranging from zero to 2π and a periodic closed result. The instrument applies independent R and Q selection, R/Q **display** gain, and a Q sampling phase. The source's scalar value changes the spherical polar aperture through the existing bounded mapping, preserving opposite E/W hemispheres. Distinct input equations are mapped to the same sphere using an explicitly chosen adapter, not assumed to be isomorphic. Geometry coupling remains unchanged: independent source curves, simultaneous equal-fraction arc-length traversal, one variable-length crossbar, one perpendicular projecting elbow, minimum shared return clock, torus-wall Curvy Lisa output. The numerical comparison readout displays root-mean-square difference between the two **ungained scalar profile samples**, not an equation-isomorphism criterion or field-theory test.

| Code | Mathematical object | Specific selected closed representative | Epistemic scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harm_r` | synthetic harmonic R | cos(2λ)+(3/11)sin(3λ) | demonstration |
| `harm_q` | synthetic harmonic Q | sin(3λ)+(1/6)cos(5λ) | demonstration |

| `schwarz_orbit` | Schwarzschild timelike circular geodesic | x/r₀=cos λ at equatorial r₀=8M | coordinate x projection, λ is **orbital phase**, not proper time |
| `schwarz_lapse` | Schwarzschild metric lapse | 10[√(1−2M/r(λ))−√(1−2/8)], r/M=8+1.5cos λ | prescribed radial scan, **not a geodesic** |
| `kerr_drag` | Kerr equatorial ZAMO frame dragging | ω(r)=2Ma/(r³+a²r+2Ma²); a/M=0.5; r/M=8+cos λ; f=ω(r)/ω(8M)−1 | prescribed radial scan, **not an orbit** |

[L2]   "content": "# Whirligig / Analemma: terminology and functional reconstruction

**Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.

A fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.

**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \(\cos\lambda\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \(0.11\) model units and the largest step was about \(0.347\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.

**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \(Q\text{ wrt }R\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \(b=a\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.

jobs:
  deploy:
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Validate resolved catalog, rather than overwriting public GLASS discovery
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import hashlib,json
          from pathlib import Path
          catalog=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          curation=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          data=json.loads(catalog.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert isinstance(data.get('conversations'),list) and data['conversations']
          assert len(data['conversations'])==data['counts']['conversations']
          sha=hashlib.sha256(curation.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:16]
          assert data.get('curation',{}).get('sha256_16')==sha, 'stale Viewer curation'
          assert any(item.get('source_repository')=='Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
                     for item in data['conversations']), 'public GLASS discovery missing'
          print('Publishing resolved, curated Viewer catalog with',
                len(data['conversations']),'conversations')
          PY

      - name: Test and assemble the Whirligig-only route
        run: |
          python -m unittest tools.test_build_whirligig_pages
          python tools/build_whirligig_pages.py --root . --output _site

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload existing Viewer plus Whirligig
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: _site

      - name: Deploy conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

**Status:** repository build source; GitHub Pages deployment must be verified independently.  
**Purpose:** provide a durable public website without requiring the ChatGPT Sites editor.

## Architecture

- The existing Conversation Viewer remains at the project root (/HsH/), and its existing /mersearch/ route is preserved.
- The new Glass Sausage Factory site is built at /HsH/glass-sausage-factory/.
- Geometry Laboratory instruments retain their registered root routes:
  - /HsH/laboratory/whirligig/
  - /HsH/laboratory/universal-indicatrix/
- /HsH/conversations/ and /HsH/research/search/ are friendly aliases to the preserved Viewer and public Mersearch reader.

The build is static HTML, CSS and JavaScript. GitHub Actions assembles the Pages artifact from the HsH repository. No ChatGPT Sites editor session or paid Sites feature is required.

## Build locally

From the repository root:

    python PUBLIC_SITE/site/build.py --root . --output _site --base-path /HsH/
    python -m unittest discover -s PUBLIC_SITE/site -p 'test_*.py'
    node --input-type=module --check < PUBLIC_SITE/site/site.js

The script preserves the Viewer, builds the Glass Sausage Factory route, copies registered instruments, creates public-safe JSON projections, copies only locally available approved Visual Atlas assets, and copies published PDFs only after checking their PDF signature and pinned SHA-256.

## Public sections

- Start / two ways in
- Visual Atlas
- Current Work
- Papers and manuscripts
- Reading Room
- Geometry Laboratory
- In the News
- Quotable Nathan / Quotable LLM
- About / project orientation

Every ordinary public page has the shared Listen control. It uses the repository page-listen.js and math-speech.js runtime and the browser Web Speech API.

## Presentation and authority boundaries

- Current Work carries the snapshot date from its source feed. A dated snapshot is not represented as a live status query.
- Papers with a published PDF use the registered presentation derivative. Manuscripts without one are labeled PRESENTATION PENDING and expose source/review records only as secondary links.
- The site does not render arbitrary repository paths as reader pages.
- Public Mersearch remains a candidate search over the existing public conversation index, not the protected three-repository research engine.
- Owner curation is read-only. OWNER_CURATION_PUBLIC.json is a public projection, not an authenticated write endpoint. Private notes and owner-only controls are not implemented in this static site.
- Eight legacy approved illustration entries still point to the previous ChatGPT Sites asset host. They are not hotlinked. The build admits only approved local assets with repository-backed paths; the older images can be mirrored after source retrieval and provenance verification.

## Deployment

The deploy-conversation-viewer-pages workflow assembles a combined artifact and deploys it through GitHub Pages. A successful GitHub commit is not itself deployment proof. Verify the Actions run, Pages URL, each route, PDF downloads, Viewer search, and instrument controls before calling the public site deployed.

The project Pages root remains the Conversation Viewer for backward compatibility. The Glass Sausage Factory is added alongside it at /glass-sausage-factory/, avoiding a destructive replacement of the existing root route.

A subsequent confirmation deploy is running against the latest workflow revision. Deployment action success is verified; a separate visual browser smoke-test is still pending.

Current premise authority/status belongs in BEDROCK unless a newer Nathan Direct instruction says otherwise. > **Read the pictures first if you want the fastest conceptual route. Read BEDROCK first if you are going to build on the theory.** --- ## 1. One geometric construction, many familiar descriptions SAT's organizing move is not to invent a separate geometric story for every physical sector. It asks whether familiar descriptions can be understood as different projections, interaction regimes, or effective descriptions of one underlying geometric construction. The labels in historical figures should be read as **SAT mappings and research claims**, not as a substitute for the standard theories themselves. --- ## 2. Particle differences as differences of geometry A recurring SAT idea is that the apparent catalog of particle types may be reorganized as a catalog of trajectory geometries: simple traveling excitation, persistent coiling, and increasingly interdependent or braided structures. The current H(s)H program is working to replace the simplified centerline picture with a finite-core worldtube treatment while preserving the same geometric dependency structure. --- ## 3. The basic readout: trajectory and time-surface intersection The basic visual grammar is a higher-dimensional trajectory intersecting a lower-dimensional time slice or readout surface. The intersection can move, rotate, close, open, or change shape even when the underlying trajectory remains continuous. Historically SAT used an angular measure, usually written **θ₄**, to track the orientation of the trajectory relative to the time direction/surface normal. The notation and exact formal role have evolved; the geometric relationship is the durable part of the picture. --- ## 4. Not just a straight helix: recursion and carrier geometry The model is not simply "everything is a helix." A local coil may itself propagate along a curved carrier, and that carrier may participate in still larger-scale structure. The present H(s)H work is focused on making this recursive, finite-core geometry explicit rather than leaving it compressed into a worldline skeleton. --- ## 5. Interaction as geometric braiding SAT's braid-centered interaction picture treats multi-filament organization as a geometric relation rather than merely adding a new label to otherwise independent particles. In the historical worldline model this was represented by interweaving centerlines; H(s)H asks what the corresponding finite-core worldtube mechanics actually are: **bundle geometry + finite extent + intersection/readout + deformation**. --- ## 6. A worldline can generate an evolving family of observed patterns Successive slices through one continuous construction need not look alike. SAT repeatedly uses this fact to distinguish the full trajectory from the lower-dimensional pattern available at any one slice. The same distinction is central to the move from worldline to worldtube. --- ## 7. The construction is intended to close at cosmological scale SAT was developed as a whole-physics translation program rather than a particle model alone. Its historical materials therefore extend the same geometric vocabulary into gravitation, large-scale structure, expansion, fluids, and cosmology. Some specific equations and historical mechanisms have since been revised or retired; the broad structural ambition remains part of H(s)H. --- ## 8. Historical continuity is part of the record The public H(s)H repository is not the primary historical archive. The larger [SAT Theory Archive 2023–25](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25) preserves the developmental record. The quick provenance window below deliberately spans both ends of that record: surviving 2003 material and the much more explicit 2025 SAT notebooks. ### Earliest surviving notebook/sketch material — 2003
The Archive dates the Ireland-trip notebook period to **February–June 2003** and preserves the surviving sketches as their own source layer. The point here is not to retrofit every later SAT term onto those pages, but to show the early geometric ancestry directly rather than beginning the visual history in 2025. ### Explicit SAT notebook development — 2025
The point of preserving the sketches alongside later renderings is not that every current H(s)H statement was already explicit in the earliest work. It is that the **recognizable generative geometry appears early and persists while the physical identifications, mathematical machinery, and resolution of the model accumulate around it**. [Browse the 2003 sketch folder →](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2003%20SKETCHES) · [Browse the historical SAT visuals →](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/SAT%20VISUALS) · [Browse the curated H(s)H visual package →](SAT_VISUALS/VISUALS_1/) --- # History in brief SAT/H(s)H did not begin as a finished theory and then acquire illustrations afterward. The geometry came first and was repeatedly revisited, renamed, formalized, tested, simplified, and broadened. The historical archive records the path in much greater detail, but several turning points make the overall development legible: **c. 1991 → 2003–04:** Minkowski worldline/timesheet thinking develops into surviving higher-dimensional path, coil, mass and curvature sketches. **2024:** the old construction is reopened explicitly as Proto-SAT; line/plane and helix/hypersurface geometry becomes the center of sustained theory-building. **2 February 2025:** the Fundamental Intuitions are presented publicly: physicalized worldlines/filaments, a time surface, particle-as-intersection, and deliberate import of successful Standard Model, relativity and quantum structure. **Spring–summer 2025:** SAT expands rapidly into an all-physics translation program. θ₄, torsion/twist, particle mappings, QCD-like locking/braiding, 4D-covariant integration, Hopf/Borromean structures, SAT-O modules, mathematical-backbone work, prediction protocols and hostile audits all enter the record. **Late 2025 → early 2026:** the project becomes increasingly formal and source-conscious: 4DHH, SAT-O, worldline/holonomy work, explicit prediction documents, Lean-oriented rebuilding, provenance tracking, and adversarial validation become central. **Mid-2026:** the finite-core problem becomes unavoidable. The centerline/filament picture is generalized into **H(s)H — Hyper(super)Helical Worldtube**, with explicit worldtube cross-section, recursive coiling, braid/bundle geometry, and a cleaner separation between full higher-dimensional structure and lower-dimensional readout. The current project is therefore best read neither as a frozen 2025 theory nor as a clean break from it. H(s)H is the attempt to retain the durable geometric grammar while rebuilding the mathematical object at higher resolution. --- # Reading the archive responsibly This repository intentionally mixes several kinds of material that should not be collapsed into one evidentiary category: - **Nathan-authored conceptual statements** — primary evidence for what the model is intended to mean. - **Historical derivations and calculations** — evidence of mathematical development, with varying levels of checking. - **AI-generated formalizations and reconstructions** — useful working mathematics, but not automatically authoritative. - **Computational experiments** — evidence for what a particular implementation produced under specified assumptions. - **Visualizations** — often the clearest route into the geometry, but not themselves proofs. - **External-source comparisons** — context for comparison and vocabulary, not evidence that SAT/H(s)H inherits the validity of the compared theory. The repository's vetting/status labels are intended to keep those categories visible. Where a document has not yet been independently checked, it should be read as part of an active research record rather than as settled result. --- # Where to go next For theory work, return to **[BEDROCK.md](BEDROCK.md)**. For historical reconstruction, use the **[SAT Theory Archive 2023–25](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25)** and the derivation/provenance indices.               "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi
          if [ -d "LIVE CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \
              "LIVE CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi

      - name: Refresh repository structural index before tag cross-check
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Build archive-wide conversation autotag indexes
        run: |

        run: |
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v2.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v3.py

          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/provenance_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path

          data = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          missing = [
              item['path']
              for item in data['conversations']

        if: ${{ steps.development_dates.outcome == 'failure' || steps.live_dates.outcome == 'failure' }}

          echo "::warning::At least one date-tagging pass reported a collision or parse-level failure. Generated manifests were retained; structural/chronology indexing continued."

          set -euo pipefail

          git add -A -- "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" "LIVE CONVOS" || true

          git add indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true
          git add indexes/manifests indexes/autotag || true
          git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated || true

        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload current conversation viewer
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: CONVERSATION_VIEWER

      - name: Deploy current conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

[L2]   "content": "name: Build conversation viewer catalog

# Workflow edits intentionally trigger a self-test so generation and UI changes are validated on main.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    # GLASS is a separate public repository, so an hourly sweep provides eventual
    # convergence even when no HsH commit occurs at the same time.
    - cron: '23 * * * *'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      # Actual file contents determine whether a new source is JSON.
      # Trigger immediately for all extensions, not only .json/.txt.
      - 'DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/**'
      - 'LIVE CONVOS/**'
      - 'indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer.py'
      - 'tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py'
      - 'tools/build_viewer_body_search.py'
      - 'tools/discover_external_conversations.py'
      - 'tools/conversation_json_sniff.py'
      - 'tools/date_conversation_exports.py'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/EXTERNAL_CONVERSATIONS.json'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.js'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.html'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/*.css'
      - 'CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/landmarks.json'
      - '.github/workflows/build-conversation-viewer.yml'

permissions:
  contents: write

concurrency:
  group: conversation-viewer-catalog
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip conversation-viewer]') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Checkout public GLASS archive for Viewer discovery
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25
          ref: main
          path: _viewer_external/GLASS
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Validate viewer JavaScript
        run: |
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/viewer.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/mersearch/reader.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/catalog_body_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

      - name: Discover eligible public cross-repo conversations
        run: |
          python tools/discover_external_conversations.py \
            --hsh-root . \
            --external-root _viewer_external/GLASS \
            --external-repository Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 \
            --output CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json

      - name: Build compact conversation catalog
        run: python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py

      - name: Build cross-conversation full-text search index
        run: |
          python tools/build_viewer_body_search.py --glass-root _viewer_external/GLASS
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          root=Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search')
          meta=json.loads((root/'meta.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          catalog=json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert set(meta['conversation_ids']) == {c['id'] for c in catalog['conversations']}, 'body index/catalog mismatch'
          assert list(root.glob('*.json')), 'no body search index output'
          PY

      - name: Validate generated catalog, public discovery, source paths, curation and landmarks
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path

          p = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json')
          data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert data['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(data['conversations'], list)
          assert data['conversations'], 'viewer catalog is empty'
          ids = [x['id'] for x in data['conversations']]
          paths = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations']]
          assert len(ids) == len(set(ids)), 'duplicate viewer ids'
          assert len(paths) == len(set(paths)), 'duplicate source paths'
          from tools.conversation_json_sniff import is_json_document_candidate
          assert all(
              x.get('external') or is_json_document_candidate(Path(x['path']))
              for x in data['conversations']
          ), 'catalog contains non-JSON first-party source'
          missing_paths = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations'] if not x.get('external') and not Path(x['path']).is_file()]
          assert not missing_paths, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths: {missing_paths}'

          for manifest_path in [
              Path('indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'),
              Path('indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'),
          ]:
              manifest = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
              assert isinstance(manifest.get('records'), list), f'invalid conversation manifest: {manifest_path}'

          cp = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/CURATION.json')
          curation = json.loads(cp.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert curation['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(curation['rules'], list)

          manual_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/EXTERNAL_CONVERSATIONS.json')
          manual = json.loads(manual_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert manual['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(manual['conversations'], list)

          discovered_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json')
          discovered = json.loads(discovered_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert discovered['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(discovered['conversations'], list)
          assert discovered['source_repository'] == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
          assert 'HSH_RESOURCES' not in json.dumps(discovered), 'private resource identity leaked into public discovery'
          assert discovered['stats']['recognized'] >= discovered['stats']['discovered_added']

          known_ids = set(ids)
          for item in manual['conversations']:
              assert item['id'] in known_ids, f"registered external conversation missing from catalog: {item['id']}"
          for item in discovered['conversations']:
              assert item['id'] in known_ids, f"discovered public conversation missing from catalog: {item['id']}"

          glass = [x for x in data['conversations'] if x.get('source_repository') == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25']
          assert glass, 'no public GLASS conversations reached Viewer catalog'
          assert all(x.get('external') for x in glass)

          for convo in data['conversations']:
              if convo.get('curated'):
                  curated_path = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER') / convo['raw_url']
                  derived = json.loads(curated_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
                  assert derived['derived_view'] is True
                  assert derived['source_viewer_id'] == convo['id']
                  assert len(derived['messages']) == convo['message_count']

          lp = Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/landmarks.json')
          landmarks = json.loads(lp.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert landmarks['schema_version'] == 1
          assert isinstance(landmarks['landmarks'], list)
          known = {x['id']: x for x in data['conversations']}
          for item in landmarks['landmarks']:
              cid = item.get('conversation_id')
              assert cid in known, f"unknown or hidden landmark conversation: {item}"
              assert isinstance(item.get('message'), int) and item['message'] > 0, f"invalid landmark message: {item}"
              assert item['message'] <= known[cid]['message_count'], f"landmark beyond conversation length: {item}"
              assert isinstance(item.get('label'), str) and item['label'].strip(), f"invalid landmark label: {item}"
          print(data['counts'])
          print(data['curation'])
          print(f"manual_external={len(manual['conversations'])}")
          print(f"glass_discovery_stats={discovered['stats']}")
          print(f"glass_viewer_entries={len(glass)}")
          print(f"landmarks={len(landmarks['landmarks'])}")
          PY

      - name: Commit generated viewer data and source manifests
        run: |
          git config user.name 'HsH Conversation Viewer Bot'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'

          for attempt in 1 2 3 4; do
            # Rebuild from the newest public inputs each time so concurrent work cannot
            # strand or silently overwrite otherwise-valid generated Viewer data.
            git fetch origin main
            git reset --hard origin/main
            git -C _viewer_external/GLASS fetch origin main
            git -C _viewer_external/GLASS reset --hard origin/main

            python tools/discover_external_conversations.py \
              --hsh-root . \
              --external-root _viewer_external/GLASS \
              --external-repository Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 \
              --output CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json
            python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py
            python tools/build_viewer_body_search.py --glass-root _viewer_external/GLASS

            python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          data = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          missing = [x['path'] for x in data['conversations'] if not x.get('external') and not Path(x['path']).is_file()]
          assert not missing, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths after race rebuild: {missing}'
          for p in [Path('indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json'), Path('indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json')]:
              manifest = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
              assert isinstance(manifest.get('records'), list), f'invalid refreshed manifest: {p}'
          discovered = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          assert discovered['source_repository'] == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25'
          assert 'HSH_RESOURCES' not in json.dumps(discovered)
          assert any(x.get('source_repository') == 'Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25' for x in data['conversations'])
          PY

            WATCH='CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json'
            if ! git status --porcelain -- $WATCH | grep -q .; then
              echo 'Conversation viewer generated data, public discovery and manifests already current.'
              exit 0
            fi

            git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/discovered_external_conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/body_search indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json
            git commit -m '[skip conversation-viewer] Refresh Viewer data, GLASS discovery and manifests'
            if git push origin HEAD:main; then
              exit 0
            fi

            echo "Push race on attempt ${attempt}; rebuilding from latest public inputs." >&2
            sleep 2
          done

          echo 'Conversation viewer refresh could not win a push race after 4 attempts.' >&2
          exit 1

[L2]   "content": "name: Refresh automatic website docket
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 * * * *'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      - 'PUBLIC_SITE/generated/**'
permissions:
  contents: write
concurrency:
  group: public-site-discovery
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  discover:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - run: pip install 'Pillow>=10,<12'
      - name: Discover both public archives and prepare the rolling docket
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python tools/site_discovery.py --out PUBLIC_SITE/generated
      - name: Validate generated data
        run: |
          python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('PUBLIC_SITE/generated/discovery.json')); assert d['schema_version']==1; assert d['documents']; assert all(r['status']=='complete' for r in d['repositories'].values())"
      - name: Persist presentation docket and gallery thumbnails
        run: |
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add PUBLIC_SITE/generated
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then exit 0; fi
          git commit -m 'Refresh automatic public display docket and square artwork'
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            git pull --rebase origin main
            if git push; then exit 0; fi
          done
          exit 1

That establishes an important geometric constraint, and it exposes a fundamental problem with the current Analemma implementation.

I checked the original *Finding the Donut* archive, page 26. It describes two distinct features:

1. The **crosspoint**, where the Analemma intersects itself.
2. A separate **self-tangency at the antipode** of that crosspoint.

Your new description gives those features a definite orientation:

- **North and South:** the two projected-curve directions.
- **East:** the Analemma's transverse waist crossing.
- **West:** the antipodal kissing point, where the two branches share a tangent.

The two self-contact points must be exactly antipodal, not merely opposite-looking points in a drawing.

**The existing implementation cannot do this.** Its curve is

\[
G_A(t)=
\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin 2t+0.27\sin t))}
{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin 2t+0.27\sin t))\|}
\]

Its first coordinate is always negative. Consequently, it cannot contain an antipodal pair. This is a geometric incompatibility, not a rendering problem.

One coordinate decision before I alter the implementation: should I now move the R and Q projected curves from their existing east/west hemispheres to the **north/south hemispheres**, superseding the earlier R-east/Q-west arrangement? <MemoryCite />

That determines how the Analemma, moving followers, crossbar, and contact frame must be oriented together.

parts: Well, the original specification was to project the polar curves about the north and south poles. But it doesn't matter, as long as the curves are projected around one set of poles, and the analemma crossing and kissing are at the opposite set. That way the figure 8 loops around the north pole in the northern hemisphere, and the south pole in the southern.

[L2]   "content": "name: Maintain H(s)H navigation

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths-ignore:
      - "indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md"
      - "indexes/index-state.json"
      - "indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md"
      - "indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md"
      - "indexes/manifests/**"
      - "indexes/autotag/**"
      - "CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json"
      - "CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated/**"

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

concurrency:
  group: hsh-navigation-main
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  maintain:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' || !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip hsh-maintenance]') }}
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
      - name: Check out current main branch
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Date-tag stable developmental exports
        id: development_dates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          mkdir -p indexes/manifests
          if [ -d "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/date_conversation_exports.py \
              "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" \
              --apply \
              --resolve-collisions \
              --manifest indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json
          else
            echo "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS not present; skipping"
          fi

      - name: Date-tag LIVE CONVOS preserving original source content
        id: live_dates
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          mkdir -p indexes/manifests
          if [ -d "LIVE CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/date_conversation_exports.py \
              "LIVE CONVOS" \
              --apply \
              --resolve-collisions \
              --manifest indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json
          else
            echo "LIVE CONVOS not present; skipping"
          fi

      - name: Verify every datable source now has the right filename date prefix
        run: python tools/audit_conversation_date_tags.py --output indexes/manifests/date-tag-audit.json --strict

      - name: Build conversation viewer from the fresh manifests
        run: python tools/build_conversation_viewer_resolved.py

      - name: Build conversation chronology indexes
        run: |
          if [ -d "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \
              "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi
          if [ -d "LIVE CONVOS" ]; then
            python tools/index_conversation_chronology.py \
              "LIVE CONVOS" \
              --output indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md
          fi

      - name: Refresh repository structural index before tag cross-check
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Build archive-wide conversation autotag indexes
        run: |
          mkdir -p WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis indexes/autotag
          python WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v3.py . \
            --out WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl \
            --summary indexes/autotag/AUTOTAG_SUMMARY.md \
            --index indexes/autotag/CONVERSATION_TAG_INDEX.md \
            --manifest indexes/autotag/conversation-tag-manifest.json \
            --user-tag-index indexes/autotag/user-message-tags.jsonl \
            --structural-index-state indexes/index-state.json \
            --window 4

      - name: Refresh structural index with autotag surfaces included
        run: python tools/index_archive.py --root .

      - name: Validate Python tooling
        run: |
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v2.py
          python -m py_compile WORKSPACES/COMMON/scripts/layered_autotag_nathan_v3.py

      - name: Validate viewer JavaScript
        run: |
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/annotations.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/viewer.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/argus_followup.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/provenance_search.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/landmarks.js
          node --check CONVERSATION_VIEWER/presentation.js

      - name: Run repository tests
        run: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

      - name: Validate generated navigation state
        run: |
          python -m json.tool indexes/index-state.json >/dev/null
          if [ -f indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json ]; then
            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/development-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null
          fi
          if [ -f indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json ]; then
            python -m json.tool indexes/manifests/live-conversation-dates.json >/dev/null
          fi
          python -m json.tool indexes/autotag/conversation-tag-manifest.json >/dev/null
          test -s indexes/autotag/CONVERSATION_TAG_INDEX.md
          test -s indexes/autotag/user-message-tags.jsonl
          python -m json.tool CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json >/dev/null
          python - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path

          data = json.loads(Path('CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
          missing = [
              item['path']
              for item in data['conversations']
              if not item.get('external') and not Path(item['path']).is_file()
          ]
          assert not missing, f'viewer catalog contains missing repository source paths: {missing}'
          PY
          test -f indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md
          test -f indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true

      - name: Report date-tagging warnings
        if: ${{ steps.development_dates.outcome == 'failure' || steps.live_dates.outcome == 'failure' }}
        run: |
          echo "::warning::At least one date-tagging pass reported a collision or parse-level failure. Generated manifests were retained; structural/chronology indexing continued."

      - name: Commit maintained navigation, tag indexes, and viewer artifacts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "H(s)H Navigation Bot"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add -A -- "DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS" "LIVE CONVOS" || true
          git add indexes/STRUCTURAL_INDEX.md indexes/index-state.json || true
          git add indexes/CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md indexes/LIVE_CONVERSATION_CHRONOLOGY.md || true
          git add indexes/manifests indexes/autotag || true
          git add -A CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/conversations.json CONVERSATION_VIEWER/data/curated || true
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "Navigation, tag indexes, and viewer data already current"
          else
            git commit -m "[skip hsh-maintenance] Maintain date/index/tag/viewer navigation"
            if ! git push origin HEAD:main; then
              echo "::error::Main advanced while this run was working. Because this workflow can rename source conversation files as well as regenerate indexes, it will not merge or replay a stale snapshot. A fresh maintenance run must recompute from current main."
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Upload full message-level autotag analysis
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: archive-wide-layered-autotags
          path: WORKSPACES/COMMON/analysis/archive_layered_autotags.jsonl

      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload current conversation viewer
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: CONVERSATION_VIEWER

      - name: Deploy current conversation viewer
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

thoughts.content: I’m interpreting the specification as mapping the two polar curves around the north and south poles: R forms the northern loop, Q the southern loop, while the analemma crosses and kisses at opposite east–west poles.
I’m treating each lobe as a closed northern or southern loop connecting E and W. The branches cross transversely at E, meet tangentially at W, and together create the required spherical figure-eight.

I’m distinguishing the shared contact points carefully: each polar lobe consists of two E–W arcs, enclosing its pole. At E, the combined branches cross transversely; at W, corresponding branches share a tangent, producing tangential contact.

I’m distinguishing “centered around” from “strictly confined.” Strict hemispheric confinement conflicts with transverse crossing at E, so each lobe should primarily surround its pole while allowing local equator crossings near the shared points.
