# GrAnn / R–Q Whirligig: inner-wall rolling and minimum shared rotational lock

**Date:** 2026-10-21  
**Status:** SANDBOXED browser engineering reconstruction, repository-published, real-browser/Sites deployment not independently verified.  
**Source:** `PUBLIC_SITE/instruments/whirligig/index.html` in `Satobloc/HsH`.  
**User correction:** GrAnn is fundamentally rotational locking through **all three spatial axes**, with the **minimum shared return** determining the number of rotations of the single perpendicular gimbal elbow. The sphere rolls on the **inner radial surface of the torus**, not the outer one. The previously visible outward-contact spin looked backward because it was actually the wrong contact branch.

## Selected contact and direction

Let torus major radius be `R`, tube radius and sphere radius both `b=a`, orbital position `C(ψ)=R(cosψ,sinψ,0)=R e_r`, and orbit tangent `e_φ`. The two torus radial equator points are:

```text
Donomphulon = P_inner = (R-b)e_r
P_ivot      = P_outer = (R+b)e_r
r_inner     = P_inner-C = -b e_r
C'          = R e_φ
```

Nominated inner-wall no-slip requires `C' + ω × (-b e_r) = 0` per unit `ψ`, hence the **z component** of angular velocity is `ω_z=+R/b`, in the SAME physical sign as torus progression. For the old **outer** contact `r=+b e_r`, the required sign was `ω_z=-R/b`. Reversing playback alone is not an acceptable fix: switch the selected wall, contact offset, and the resulting orientation/velocity constraint together.

The earlier browser version accidentally labeled its single inner contact as both P_ivot and Donomphulon. This is corrected: P_ivot remains the **outer** circumferential point per the historical source, while Donomphulon is the **inner** selected rolling point; the diameter `2b` separates them. The material GrAnn track passes through both contact and antipode.

## Minimum even three-axis rotational lock

Write `r=R/b`, `δ=r−1`. In this deliberately defined SO(3) locking ansatz, take

```text
n = smallest positive EVEN integer strictly larger than |δ|
σ = sqrt(n²−δ²)                              (nonzero transverse spin)
u = (σ,0,δ)/n                               (unit body axis)
Q(ψ) = Rot_z(ψ) Rot_u(n ψ)
```

Then the world angular velocity per `ψ` is

```text
ω = σ cosψ e_x + σ sinψ e_y + r e_z.
```

The sphere therefore rotates through **x and y over the orbit** as well as the **positive z rolling direction**, without violating the nominated inner-wall slip constraint. Because `n` is an integer and the orbital angle makes a full turn, the complete orientation `Q(2π)=Q(0)`; the **smallest even** `n>|δ|` makes the x/y component strictly nonzero. This is a minimality statement only **within this specified constant-oblique-axis ansatz**, not proof of a globally unique minimal mechanism.

The sphere's body material contact is

```text
g_body(ψ)=Q(ψ)⁻¹(−e_r(ψ))
```

and the torus wall determines `C = P_inner - b Q g_body`. The resulting body track is a generally non-great circular GrAnn contact locus. Its historical self-intersection `GrAnn_Omph`, special antipodal self-tangency `GrAnn_t_ipode` and original R-anchor crossover **have not been reconstructed**. This lock is functional, not a claim to have recovered the exact source-described shape.

## Crossbar and elbow timing

R and Q remain independent E/W **sphere curves**. A common meridional sweep intersects both curves separately, yielding two moving body points `R(ψ)` and `Q(ψ)`. Their freely varying connector has midpoint W_obble; its one and only projecting gimbal elbow is constrained exactly perpendicular to the connector.

The current browser maps each selected input to one closed 2π sphere curve, so one full normalized sweep lap returns both source curves to their represented starting parameters. Let `m` be the selectable **integer** number of complete sweeps per torus orbit. Define

```text
elbow_turns = lcm(n,m)
theta_elbow(ψ) = elbow_turns * ψ
```

This replaces the former separate arbitrary elbow-turn slider and the ad hoc `curvature_gain*(curvature_R−curvature_Q)` phase. The single gimbal elbow intersects the actual torus wall to make Curvy Lisa. The R/Q representation may have shorter scalar periods but a complete spatial curve still carries its azimuth winding; use full curve/orientation closure, not merely scalar equality, to test return.

For `R=1.65,b=.55`: `r=3,δ=2,n=4,σ=sqrt(12)`; default m=1 gives elbow=4, while m=3 gives elbow=12. Other radii choose their own minimal-even n with a floating-point guard at integer boundaries. General source-specific fractional windings, quaternion signs, nonperiodic solutions, nontrivial holonomy and independently varying follower phases would require a more general common-return solver; these are not silently presumed solved.

## Unfiltered comparator series

The browser retains its original **14** equation adapters and adds **28** explicit scalar representatives. They are organized as:
- **11 best-known examples:** harmonic oscillator, Kepler ellipse, Maxwell plane wave, Fourier heat equation, Laplace harmonic, Schrödinger box eigenfunction, standing wave, Lorentz gamma scan, Planck spectrum, Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution, Fermi–Dirac occupation.
- **17 often overlooked examples:** Jacobi theta, Legendre, Chebyshev, Bessel J0 (40-point quadrature), Clausen Cl2 (truncated), Re Li2 (truncated), Berry curvature in a two-band Dirac model, Mathieu coefficient, KdV one-soliton profile, sine–Gordon kink, viscous Burgers shock, Morse and Lennard–Jones potentials, Kitaev chain spectrum, Pöschl–Teller potential, Fresnel C (Simpson quadrature), U(1) Wilson phase.

These category labels are **editorial** and not an objective ranking of physical importance or novelty. Every profile remains selectable independently as R or Q, with a displayed formula, chosen representative and limitations. A deterministic no-ranking pair iterator traverses every unordered pair in the selected series: 55 best-known pairs, 136 overlooked pairs, or **861 combinations across all 42**. No automated beauty/tuning selection is applied to Curvy Lisa. Some source mathematical objects are nonperiodic; **the prescribed sample parameter is periodic**, not the original soliton, kink or trajectory.

## Executed test record

All executed checks use the browser's JavaScript with a **stub DOM/canvas**, not a real graphical browser.
- Default `R=1.65,b=.55,m=1`: `n=4,` `elbow_turns=4`, nonzero `σ=3.4641`, inner contact slip residual under `3.9e−16`, full SO(3) orientation return residual under `5.3e−15`, 1,401/1,401 first-forward elbow/torus ray intersections.

**Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.

A fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.

**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \(\cos\lambda\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \(0.11\) model units and the largest step was about \(0.347\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.

**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \(Q\text{ wrt }R\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \(b=a\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.

- [Previous equation catalog and revisions](EQUATION_LIBRARY.md)
- [Older GrAnn functional investigations (historical, not controlling)](../../../tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_FUNCTIONAL_RECONSTRUCTION_2026-10-18.md)

Each input must provide an explicit dimensionless periodic *scalar representative* `f(λ)`, with λ ranging from zero to 2π and a periodic closed result. The instrument applies independent R and Q selection, R/Q **display** gain, and a Q sampling phase. The source's scalar value changes the spherical polar aperture through the existing bounded mapping, preserving opposite E/W hemispheres. Distinct input equations are mapped to the same sphere using an explicitly chosen adapter, not assumed to be isomorphic. Geometry coupling remains unchanged: independent source curves, simultaneous equal-fraction arc-length traversal, one variable-length crossbar, one perpendicular projecting elbow, minimum shared return clock, torus-wall Curvy Lisa output. The numerical comparison readout displays root-mean-square difference between the two **ungained scalar profile samples**, not an equation-isomorphism criterion or field-theory test.

| Code | Mathematical object | Specific selected closed representative | Epistemic scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| `harm_r` | synthetic harmonic R | cos(2λ)+(3/11)sin(3λ) | demonstration |
| `harm_q` | synthetic harmonic Q | sin(3λ)+(1/6)cos(5λ) | demonstration |
| `u1_phase` | U(1) relative phase | Re exp(i[λ+0.25 sin(2λ)]) | fixed-reference gauge phase; **not gauge invariant** |
| `su2_character` | SU(2) fundamental character | ½Tr diag(exp(iφ),exp(−iφ))=cos φ, φ=2λ+0.35sin λ | group path only; not an SU(2) Yang–Mills field |
| `su3_character` | SU(3) fundamental character | (1+2cos φ)/3, φ=2λ+0.25sin(3λ) | diagonal group path; not QCD dynamics or a Wilson loop |
| `gw_plus` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h₊/h₀=cos(2λ) | TT-gauge wave component, phase-normalized |
| `gw_cross` | linearized vacuum GR wave | h×/h₀=sin(2λ) | TT-gauge component, not gauge-independent complete spacetime |
| `schwarz_orbit` | Schwarzschild timelike circular geodesic | x/r₀=cos λ at equatorial r₀=8M | coordinate x projection, λ is **orbital phase**, not proper time |
| `schwarz_lapse` | Schwarzschild metric lapse | 10[√(1−2M/r(λ))−√(1−2/8)], r/M=8+1.5cos λ | prescribed radial scan, **not a geodesic** |
| `kerr_drag` | Kerr equatorial ZAMO frame dragging | ω(r)=2Ma/(r³+a²r+2Ma²); a/M=0.5; r/M=8+cos λ; f=ω(r)/ω(8M)−1 | prescribed radial scan, **not an orbit** |
| `qm_rabi` | two-level Schrödinger solution | H=(ℏΩ/2)σₓ, Pₑ=sin²(λ/2); 2Pₑ−1=−cos λ | ideal resonant system, λ=Ωt |

**Important gauge distinction:** the trace of a chosen group element is a class function under conjugation, but these chosen paths are *not* derived from a gauge connection integrated along physical closed spacetime loops. Do not present them as gauge-invariant Yang–Mills Wilson-loop measurements or solutions to the gauge field equations.

**Important GR distinction:** a selected metric is an exact gravitational solution in its stated idealized setting, but sampling one metric component along an arbitrarily imposed periodic radius does not automatically yield a geodesic or solve a new Einstein field equation. **Important QM distinction:** phase, expectation value, and population probability are different objects. Each input explicitly states which is sampled. Do not equate scalar trace similarity with quantum-state equivalence.

- Two independent selectors: **Equation R / East** and **Equation Q / West**, each containing all 14 profiles.

The HTML file was independently read back from GitHub after its committed write. The synthetic and physical examples are never declared automatically equivalent by curve appearance.

**Uncurated traversal:** `Next pair in series` deterministically walks all unordered pairs of the chosen set in lexicographic order, with a visible index; counts are 55 familiar, 136 overlooked, or 861 among all 42. This avoids auto-selecting outputs for beauty, similarity, or expected theory claims. Manual R/Q selection and original named pairs are preserved.

**Source and tests:** [Current GrAnn mechanism plus complete test record](../../../tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_INNER_WALL_ROTATIONAL_LOCK_2026-10-21.md). 42 scalar representatives verified finite and closed under `f(0)=f(2π)`, with 84 complete R- and Q-side apparatus configurations and 117,684 samples meeting torus-wall, E/W, and perpendicularity numerical checks. \beta(t)&=\kappa\sin t\cos^2t,\\

\end{aligned}

import numpy as np, math
from scipy.integrate import quad
from scipy.optimize import brentq, minimize_scalar

def shape_beta(t,a,c):
    return a*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**2 + c*np.sin(t)*np.cos(t)**4
def shape_b1(t,a,c):
    s=np.sin(t); co=np.cos(t)
    return a*(co**3-2*s**2*co) + c*(co**5-4*s**2*co**3)
def shape_b2(t,a,c):
    s=np.sin(t); co=np.cos(t)
    # differentiate terms:
    # d(co^3 -2s²co) = -3co²s -4s co² +2s³ = 2s³ -7s co²
    # d(co^5 -4s²co³)= -5s co^4 -8s co^4 +12s³ co² = 12s³co² -13s co^4
    return a*(2*s**3-7*s*co**2) + c*(12*s**3*co**2-13*s*co**4)

def speed(t,a,c):
    bb=shape_beta(t,a,c)
    return math.sqrt(shape_b1(t,a,c)**2 + 4*math.cos(bb)**2)

def kg(t,a,c):
    bb=shape_beta(t,a,c); b1=shape_b1(t,a,c); b2=shape_b2(t,a,c)
    spd=speed(t,a,c)
    det=2*(2*math.sin(bb)*b1*b1 + math.sin(bb)+math.sin(3*bb)+math.cos(bb)*b2)
    return det/spd**3

def area_lobe_ac(a,c):
    return 2*quad(lambda x: 1-math.sin(shape_beta(x,a,c)),0,math.pi,epsabs=1e-11)[0]

def find_a(c):
    # area lobe = pi; search a positive. c is dimensionless; need a+c cos² >=0
    # lower bound a > max(0,-c)
    lo=max(0,-c)+1e-8
    hi=20
    f=lambda a: area_lobe_ac(a,c)-math.pi
    # ensure no β > pi/2 maybe constrain max beta
    # increase high until area below pi, but avoid nonmonotonic beyond hemisphere
    grid=np.linspace(lo,hi,500)
    vals=[]
    prev=(grid[0],f(grid[0]))
    for x in grid[1:]:
        fx=f(x)
        if prev[1]*fx<=0:
            return brentq(f,prev[0],x,xtol=1e-12)
        prev=(x,fx)
    return None

def smooth_energy(c):
    a=find_a(c)
    if a is None: return np.inf
    # Check beta max under pi/2
    vals=np.linspace(0,math.pi,2001)
    betas=np.array([shape_beta(x,a,c) for x in vals])
    if np.max(betas)>=math.pi/2: return np.inf
    # kg derivative numerical complex? use central finite diff at high N for quick objective
    N=3000
    ts=np.linspace(0,math.pi,N+1)
    kgs=np.array([kg(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # periodic endpoints? lobe branch t 0 to pi has crossing E different tangent. k_g at t0 vs tpi maybe sign? For full curve curvature continuity across seam at t=pi to next lobe? This parameterization changes sign etc. But objective on full 2pi.
    # derivative np.gradient with second-order edge; integrate on lobe, both branches. use periodic full 2pi instead.
    ts=np.linspace(0,2*math.pi,2*N+1)
    kgs=np.array([kg(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # derivative wrt t central periodic
    dt=ts[1]-ts[0]
    kgp=(np.roll(kgs,-1)-np.roll(kgs,1))/(2*dt)
    spds=np.array([speed(x,a,c) for x in ts])
    # full curve J = int kgp^2 / speed dt
    return np.trapz(kgp**2/spds,ts)

for c0 in [-1,-.5,0,.5,1,1.5,2]:
    a0=find_a(c0)
    print(c0,a0,smooth_energy(c0))

That gives us a much better design constraint. The Analemma's shape can be determined by **area balance**, rather than arbitrarily choosing how broad or narrow its lobes should be. Then its total length determines the torus gearing.

I have worked through a candidate construction numerically.

## 1. Equal-area Analemma

I'll interpret *inner area* as the combined areas of the northern and southern lobes, and *outer area* as the remaining equatorial region of the sphere.

The desired condition is:

\[
A_{\text{north}}+A_{\text{south}}
=A_{\text{equatorial remainder}}
=2\pi b^2
\]

where \(b\) is the sphere radius.

A useful spherical construction is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi(t)&=2t\\
\beta(t)&=k\sin t\cos^2t\\
G(t)&=b
\begin{pmatrix}
\cos\beta(t)\cos\phi(t)\\
\cos\beta(t)\sin\phi(t)\\
\sin\beta(t)
\end{pmatrix}
\end{aligned}
\qquad 0\leq t\leq2\pi
\]

This gives us:

- Northern lobe around the north pole, \(0<t<\pi\).
- Southern lobe around the south pole, \(\pi<t<2\pi\).
- Transverse crossing at east, \(E=(b,0,0)\).
- Tangential kissing point at west, \(W=(-b,0,0)\).

The branches cross at E with distinct tangent directions. At W they share a tangent line but have opposite transverse curvature. Both conditions are built into the geometry.

<badge color="success">Numerically solved</badge> **The equal-area condition gives**

\[
\boxed{k=2.6349970963}
\]

The maximum latitude of either lobe is approximately \(58.11^\circ\).

Each lobe encloses exactly one quarter of the sphere's total surface area. Together, they occupy half the sphere, leaving the other half in the equatorial region.

## 2. Total Analemma length

The spherical arc-length integral is

\[
L_A=2b\int_0^\pi
\sqrt{
\left(\frac{d\beta}{dt}\right)^2+
4\cos^2\beta
}\,dt
\]

Numerical integration gives:

\[
\boxed{L_A=13.2691350396\,b}
\]

This is a useful result. The topology itself imposes a lower bound of \(4\pi b\), because each lobe must connect two antipodal points by two arcs. Our equal-area construction exceeds that minimum by approximately 5.59%.

## 3. The torus gearing

Your latest instruction establishes the gearing condition:

\[
2\pi(R-b)=2nL_A
\]

where \(n\) is a positive integer. Thus the inner torus circumference contains an even number of complete Analemma circuits.

For the smallest possible even multiple, \(n=1\):

\[
\boxed{\frac{R}{b}=5.2236968642}
\]

Higher even multiples produce:

| Analemma circuits per inner circumference | Required \(R/b\) |
|---:|---:|
| 2 | 5.2237 |
| 4 | 9.4474 |
| 6 | 13.6711 |
| 8 | 17.8948 |

<text color="secondary" size="xs">These are calculated ratios for the equal-area candidate, not arbitrary preset values.</text>

### What this means for the current instrument

The current browser defaults are \(R=1.65\) and \(b=0.55\), giving \(R/b=3\). Their inner circumference is only about 94.7% of one complete equal-area Analemma.

For the minimum two-circuit gearing, we have two choices:

- Preserve \(b=0.55\): increase the major radius to \(R=2.87303\).
- Preserve \(R=1.65\): reduce the sphere and tube radius to \(b=0.31587\).

The existing dimensions cannot satisfy the new geometry and gearing simultaneously.

## 4. One further refinement: actual rotational smoothness

There is an important distinction between equal-area balance and minimum rotational acceleration.

In the current inner-wall rolling model, the sphere's radial angular-velocity component is proportional to the Analemma's signed geodesic curvature, \(\kappa_g\). Consequently, the way that curvature changes along the Analemma directly affects the smoothness of the rotation.

I recommend treating equal area as a hard geometric constraint, then optimizing the shape against a rotational smoothness functional:

\[
J_{\mathrm{rot}}=
\int_0^{2\pi}
\left\|
\frac{d}{d\psi}
\left(\frac{\boldsymbol{\omega}}{\dot\psi}\right)
\right\|^2d\psi
\]

That gives us an actual mathematical target rather than assuming equal areas automatically minimize acceleration. We can explore a richer family of curves, preserve the crossing, kissing, pole and area conditions, and numerically minimize this quantity.

---

**One dimensional choice before I rebuild the instrument:** should I preserve the current sphere/tube radius of 0.55 and enlarge the torus major radius to 2.87303, using the minimum two-circuit gearing as the new default?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent validation of the Whirligig equal-area spherical Analemma."""
from __future__ import annotations
import math

PI = math.pi
TAU = 2.0 * PI


def simpson(f, a: float, b: float, n: int = 8192) -> float:
    if n % 2:
        raise ValueError("Simpson interval count must be even")
    h = (b - a) / n
    total = f(a) + f(b)
    total += 4.0 * sum(f(a + (2*i - 1)*h) for i in range(1, n//2 + 1))
    total += 2.0 * sum(f(a + 2*i*h) for i in range(1, n//2))
    return total * h / 3.0


def beta(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    return k * math.sin(t) * math.cos(t)**2


def beta_p(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s, c = math.sin(t), math.cos(t)
    return k * c * (1.0 - 3.0*s*s)


def beta_pp(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s = math.sin(t)
    return k * s * (9.0*s*s - 7.0)


def lobe_area(k: float) -> float:
    # d(longitude)/dt = 2; north-polar lobe area = integral(1-sin(latitude)) d(longitude).
    return 2.0 * simpson(lambda t: 1.0 - math.sin(beta(t, k)), 0.0, PI)


def unit_analemma(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be = beta(t, k)
    return (math.cos(be)*math.cos(2*t),
            math.cos(be)*math.sin(2*t),
            math.sin(be))


def unit_analemma_d1(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be, bp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k)
    cb, sb, cp, sp = math.cos(be), math.sin(be), math.cos(2*t), math.sin(2*t)
    return (-bp*sb*cp - 2*cb*sp,
            -bp*sb*sp + 2*cb*cp,
            bp*cb)


def unit_analemma_d2(t: float, k: float) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    be, bp, bpp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k), beta_pp(t, k)
    cb, sb, cp, sp = math.cos(be), math.sin(be), math.cos(2*t), math.sin(2*t)
    e_beta = (-sb*cp, -sb*sp, cb)
    e_phi = (-sp, cp, 0.0)
    g = unit_analemma(t, k)
    a = bpp + 4.0*sb*cb
    d = -4.0*bp*sb
    q = -(bp*bp + 4.0*cb*cb)
    return tuple(a*e_beta[i] + d*e_phi[i] + q*g[i] for i in range(3))


def dot(a, b):
    return sum(x*y for x, y in zip(a, b))


def cross(a, b):
    return (a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1],
            a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2],
            a[0]*b[1]-a[1]*b[0])


def norm(a):
    return math.sqrt(dot(a, a))


def analemma_speed(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    be, bp = beta(t, k), beta_p(t, k)
    return math.hypot(bp, 2.0*math.cos(be))


def analemma_length(k: float) -> float:
    return simpson(lambda t: analemma_speed(t, k), 0.0, TAU)


def solve_k() -> float:
    lo, hi = 2.5, 3.0
    flo = lobe_area(lo) - PI
    fhi = lobe_area(hi) - PI
    if flo * fhi >= 0:
        raise RuntimeError("Equal-area root is not bracketed")
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = 0.5*(lo+hi)
        fm = lobe_area(mid) - PI
        if flo*fm <= 0:
            hi, fhi = mid, fm
        else:
            lo, flo = mid, fm
    return 0.5*(lo+hi)


def main() -> None:
    k = solve_k()
    area_each = lobe_area(k)
    area_two = 2.0*area_each
    area_remainder = 4.0*PI-area_two
    length_unit = analemma_length(k)
    even_circuits = 2
    ratio = 1.0 + even_circuits*length_unit/TAU
    b = 0.55  # retain the existing tube/sphere radius; absolute scale is free
    R = ratio*b
    length_physical = length_unit*b
    sphere_circ = TAU*b
    tube_circ = TAU*b
    inner_torus_circ = TAU*(R-b)

    # Exact local branch conditions: E is transverse; W is tangential.
    e_branch_1 = (2.0, k)    # (e_phi, e_beta) at t=0
    e_branch_2 = (2.0, -k)   # (e_phi, e_beta) at t=pi
    e_det = e_branch_1[0]*e_branch_2[1] - e_branch_1[1]*e_branch_2[0]
    w_branch_1 = (2.0, 0.0)  # at t=pi/2
    w_branch_2 = (2.0, 0.0)  # at t=3pi/2
    w_tangent_dot = dot(w_branch_1, w_branch_2)/(norm(w_branch_1)*norm(w_branch_2))

    # Check the analytic first and second derivatives against central differences.
    derivative_errors = []
    t0 = 0.713
    for h in (1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4):
        gm, g0, gp = unit_analemma(t0-h,k), unit_analemma(t0,k), unit_analemma(t0+h,k)
        fd1 = tuple((gp[i]-gm[i])/(2*h) for i in range(3))
        fd2 = tuple((gp[i]-2*g0[i]+gm[i])/(h*h) for i in range(3))
        derivative_errors.append((h, norm(tuple(fd1[i]-unit_analemma_d1(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3))),
                                  norm(tuple(fd2[i]-unit_analemma_d2(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3)))))

    # Curvature and speed remain finite and regular over one material circuit.
    min_speed = float("inf")
    max_abs_kg = 0.0
    for i in range(8192):
        t = TAU*i/8192
        g, v1, v2 = unit_analemma(t,k), unit_analemma_d1(t,k), unit_analemma_d2(t,k)
        speed = norm(v1)
        kg = dot(g, cross(v1,v2))/(speed**3)
        min_speed = min(min_speed, speed)
        max_abs_kg = max(max_abs_kg, abs(kg))

    # The latitude maximum occurs at sin^2(t)=1/3.
    max_lat = 2.0*k/(3.0*math.sqrt(3.0))

    assert abs(area_each-PI) < 2e-11

[L2]   "content": "# Whirligig / Analemma: terminology and functional reconstruction

**Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.

A fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.

**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \(\cos\lambda\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \(0.11\) model units and the largest step was about \(0.347\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.

**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \(Q\text{ wrt }R\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \(b=a\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.

- [Older GrAnn functional investigations (historical, not controlling)](../../../tools/whirligig_rq/GRANN_FUNCTIONAL_RECONSTRUCTION_2026-10-18.md)

The browser instrument is a static self-contained HTML document. **Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.

A fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.

**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \(\cos\lambda\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \(0.11\) model units and the largest step was about \(0.347\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.

**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \(Q\text{ wrt }R\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \(b=a\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.

## 2026-11-02 CURRENT: equal-area Analemma, equatorial E/W contacts, polar N/S inputs

This section supersedes the 2026-10-21 material-curve formula above and the earlier 2026-10-17 east/west R/Q placement. The canonical browser file remains [index.html](index.html).

### Confirmed geometry and terminology

- **R** is a closed equation curve around the **north pole**, wholly in the northern hemisphere.
- **Q** is a closed equation curve around the **south pole**, wholly in the southern hemisphere.
- The Analemma is a separate closed spherical figure-eight. Its transverse self-crossing is at the **east equatorial pole** E=(1,0,0); its distinct self-tangential kiss is at the antipodal **west equatorial pole** W=(-1,0,0).
- The northern lobe winds around the north pole; the southern lobe winds around the south pole.
- One Analemma circuit means the complete two-lobed closed curve. The inner torus circumference is an even multiple of that complete length.
- Sphere radius equals torus tube minor radius: b=a, so the sphere great-circle circumference equals the tube cross-section circumference.

The historical source gives the self-crossing and antipodal self-tangency relationship; the E/W versus N/S placement and the equal-area condition above are the user's later explicit geometric refinements.

### Equal-area curve family and solved shape

On the unit sphere, define

[
 eta(t)=ksin tcos^2t,qquad phi(t)=2t,
]

[
G(t)= igl(cos etacosphi,;cos etasinphi,;sin eta igr),quad 0le t<2pi.
]

The northern lobe is 0<t<pi; the southern lobe is pi<t<2pi. The equal-area interpretation used here is that the **combined two-lobe area** equals the remaining equatorial area. Thus each lobe encloses pi b^2, both lobes enclose 2 pi b^2, and the complement also has area 2 pi b^2.

The area equation is

[
2int_0^pi[1-sin(ksin tcos^2t)],dt=pi.
]

Its first regular root is

[
 oxed{k=2.63499709629253}.
]

The maximum lobe latitude is 58.11000154 degrees. At E, the two branch tangent vectors in local azimuth/latitude components are proportional to (2,k) and (2,-k), so the crossing is transverse. At W, both tangent vectors are proportional to (2,0), while their second-order latitude curvature has opposite sign, giving the intended tangential kiss. The curve is regular; its minimum parameter speed on the unit sphere is greater than 1.

### Length and gearing

The full material length is

[
L_A=bint_0^{2pi}sqrt{ eta'(t)^2+4cos^2 eta(t)},dt
=13.26913503960638,b.
]

For the minimum positive even multiple, the inner torus circumference contains two full Analemma circuits:

[
2pi(R-b)=2L_A,qquad
 oxed{R/b=5.22369686421446}.
]

The browser therefore derives the major radius from the tube/sphere radius. At the retained reference scale b=a=0.55:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Sphere and tube radius | 0.55 |
| Sphere great-circle / tube cross-section circumference | 3.45575191895 |
| Full physical Analemma length | 7.29802427178 |
| Torus major radius R | 2.87303327532 |
| Inner torus circumference | 14.59604854357 |
| Inner circumference / full Analemma length | 2 exactly, within numerical tolerance |

Changing the scale control changes a=b and derives R proportionally, preserving the equal circumferences and two-circuit gear ratio. The old independent major-radius slider is removed because it allowed the gear constraint to be broken.

### R/Q aperture and W_obble centering

The R/Q polar aperture adapter is a_RQ=0.78+0.20 tanh(f) radians. R is placed around +z and Q around -z, with opposite azimuths at a common meridional sweep. The aperture gain bounds the normalized crossbar-midpoint offset by sin(0.20)=0.19866933; the default harmonic pair's sampled maximum is about 0.0931 sphere radii. The azimuth/equation mapping remains an explicit representation choice, not a derived field equation.

### Rotational and epistemic limits

The browser computes the Analemma tangent, normal, and signed geodesic curvature analytically, transports its material point by numerical arc-length inversion, and keeps the existing inner selected-contact no-slip relation. The minimum even winding is now fixed at two full Analemma circuits per torus orbit; the elbow turns remain the LCM of that count and the R/Q sweep count.

Equal area is the chosen geometric balance condition. It has **not** been proven to globally minimize angular acceleration or jerk over all possible spherical figure-eight curves. A separate constrained smoothness optimization would be needed to establish that stronger claim. Equal-radius contact remains nonisolated, so the model still certifies only the nominated contact, not global no-slip across the full contact locus.

### Reproducible calculation

Run python tools/whirligig_rq/validate_equal_area_analemma.py for an independent standard-library calculation of the equal-area root, spherical length, E/W contact types, radius equality, and two-circuit gearing. This is numerical verification of the declared curve family, not proof that the family is uniquely implied by the historical prose.

{"path":"/GitHub/link_6a1a5af1b40c8191affccbb98ac60fa3/create_blob","args":{"repository_full_name":"Satobloc/HsH","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent standard-library validation of the Whirligig equal-area Analemma."""
from __future__ import annotations
import math

PI = math.pi
TAU = 2.0 * PI
APERTURE_GAIN = 0.20


def simpson(f, a: float, b: float, n: int = 8192) -> float:
    if n % 2:
        raise ValueError("Simpson interval count must be even")
    h = (b-a)/n
    total = f(a)+f(b)
    total += 4.0*sum(f(a+(2*i-1)*h) for i in range(1,n//2+1))
    total += 2.0*sum(f(a+2*i*h) for i in range(1,n//2))
    return total*h/3.0


def beta(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    return k*math.sin(t)*math.cos(t)**2


def beta_p(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s,c=math.sin(t),math.cos(t)
    return k*c*(1.0-3.0*s*s)


def beta_pp(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    s=math.sin(t)
    return k*s*(9.0*s*s-7.0)


def lobe_area(k: float) -> float:
    # d(longitude)/dt=2; north-polar lobe area = integral(1-sin(latitude)) d(longitude).
    return 2.0*simpson(lambda t: 1.0-math.sin(beta(t,k)),0.0,PI)


def speed(t: float, k: float) -> float:
    return math.hypot(beta_p(t,k),2.0*math.cos(beta(t,k)))


def analemma_length(k: float) -> float:
    return simpson(lambda t:speed(t,k),0.0,TAU)


def solve_k() -> float:
    lo,hi=2.5,3.0
    flo=lobe_area(lo)-PI
    fhi=lobe_area(hi)-PI
    if flo*fhi>=0:
        raise RuntimeError("Equal-area root is not bracketed")
    for _ in range(80):
        mid=(lo+hi)/2.0
        fm=lobe_area(mid)-PI
        if flo*fm<=0:
            hi,fhi=mid,fm
        else:
            lo,flo=mid,fm
    return (lo+hi)/2.0


def unit_curve(t: float,k: float):
    be=beta(t,k)
    return (math.cos(be)*math.cos(2*t),math.cos(be)*math.sin(2*t),math.sin(be))


def unit_d1(t: float,k: float):
    be,bp=beta(t,k),beta_p(t,k)
    cb,sb,cp,sp=math.cos(be),math.sin(be),math.cos(2*t),math.sin(2*t)
    return (-bp*sb*cp-2*cb*sp,-bp*sb*sp+2*cb*cp,bp*cb)


def unit_d2(t: float,k: float):
    be,bp,bpp=beta(t,k),beta_p(t,k),beta_pp(t,k)
    cb,sb,cp,sp=math.cos(be),math.sin(be),math.cos(2*t),math.sin(2*t)
    eb=(-sb*cp,-sb*sp,cb)
    ep=(-sp,cp,0.0)
    g=unit_curve(t,k)
    aa=bpp+4*sb*cb
    dd=-4*bp*sb
    qq=-(bp*bp+4*cb*cb)
    return tuple(aa*eb[i]+dd*ep[i]+qq*g[i] for i in range(3))


def dot(a,b):
    return sum(x*y for x,y in zip(a,b))


def cross(a,b):
    return (a[1]*b[2]-a[2]*b[1],a[2]*b[0]-a[0]*b[2],a[0]*b[1])


def norm(a):
    return math.sqrt(dot(a,a))


def main() -> None:
    k=solve_k()
    area_each=lobe_area(k)
    area_both=2*area_each
    area_remainder=4*PI-area_both
    length_unit=analemma_length(k)
    circuits=2
    ratio=1.0+circuits*length_unit/TAU
    b=0.55
    R=ratio*b
    length_physical=length_unit*b
    sphere_circ=TAU*b
    tube_circ=TAU*b
    inner_circ=TAU*(R-b)

    # E: branches at t=0,pi are transverse; W: branches at pi/2,3pi/2 share tangent.
    e1,e2=(2.0,k),(2.0,-k)
    e_det=e1[0]*e2[1]-e1[1]*e2[0]
    w1,w2=(2.0,0.0),(2.0,0.0)
    w_dot=dot(w1,w2)/(norm(w1)*norm(w2))

    # Check analytic derivatives against central differences.
    derivative_errors=[]
    t0=0.713
    for h in (1e-3,5e-4,2.5e-4):
        gm,g0,gp=unit_curve(t0-h,k),unit_curve(t0,k),unit_curve(t0+h,k)
        fd1=tuple((gp[i]-gm[i])/(2*h) for i in range(3))
        fd2=tuple((gp[i]-2*g0[i]+gm[i])/(h*h) for i in range(3))
        derivative_errors.append((h,norm(tuple(fd1[i]-unit_d1(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3))),
                                  norm(tuple(fd2[i]-unit_d2(t0,k)[i] for i in range(3)))))

    min_speed=min(speed(TAU*i/8192,k) for i in range(8192))
    max_lat=2*k/(3*math.sqrt(3))
    midpoint_bound=math.sin(APERTURE_GAIN)

    assert abs(area_each-PI)<2e-11
    assert abs(area_both-area_remainder)<2e-11
    assert abs(e_det)>1e-8
    assert abs(w_dot-1.0)<1e-14
    assert min_speed>1.0
    assert abs(TAU*(ratio-1.0)-circuits*length_unit)<2e-11
    assert abs(inner_circ-circuits*length_physical)<2e-11
    assert abs(sphere_circ-tube_circ)<1e-14

    print(f"area-balance shape k                 = {k:.13f}")
    print(f"one lobe area                       = {area_each:.13f} b^2")
    print(f"both lobes area                     = {area_both:.13f} b^2")
    print(f"equatorial remainder area           = {area_remainder:.13f} b^2")
    print(f"maximum lobe latitude               = {math.degrees(max_lat):.9f} deg")
    print(f"full Analemma length / b            = {length_unit:.13f}")
    print(f"minimum even circuit count          = {circuits}")
    print(f"required major/minor ratio R/b      = {ratio:.13f}")
    print(f"chosen tube/sphere radius b         = {b:.8f}")
    print(f"derived torus major radius R        = {R:.13f}")
    print(f"physical Analemma length            = {length_physical:.13f}")
    print(f"sphere great-circle circumference   = {sphere_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"tube cross-section circumference    = {tube_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"inner torus circumference           = {inner_circ:.13f}")
    print(f"inner circumference / Analemma L   = {inner_circ/length_physical:.13f}")
    print(f"E crossing tangent determinant      = {e_det:.13f} (nonzero = transverse)")
    print(f"W kissing tangent dot               = {w_dot:.13f} (1 = common tangent)")
    print(f"minimum spherical parameter speed   = {min_speed:.13f}")
    print(f"W_obble offset bound / b            = {midpoint_bound:.13f}")
    print("derivative finite-difference checks:")
    for h,e1err,e2err in derivative_errors:
        print(f"  h={h:.7g}: first={e1err:.3e}, second={e2err:.3e}")
    print("PASS: equal areas, E/W topology, regularity, radius equality, and 2:1 inner-circumference gearing")


if __name__=="__main__":
    main()
"}}

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. - **R** is a closed equation curve around the **north pole**, wholly in the northern hemisphere.
- **Q** is a closed equation curve around the **south pole**, wholly in the southern hemisphere.
- The Analemma is a separate closed spherical figure-eight. Its transverse self-crossing is at the **east equatorial pole** E=(1,0,0); its distinct self-tangential kiss is at the antipodal **west equatorial pole** W=(-1,0,0).

The historical source gives the self-crossing and antipodal self-tangency relationship; the E/W versus N/S placement and the equal-area condition above are the user's later explicit geometric refinements.

### Equal-area curve family and solved shape

On the unit sphere, define

[
 eta(t)=ksin tcos^2t,qquad phi(t)=2t,
]

[
G(t)= igl(cos etacosphi,;cos etasinphi,;sin eta igr),quad 0le t<2pi.
]

The northern lobe is 0<t<pi; the southern lobe is pi<t<2pi. The equal-area interpretation used here is that the **combined two-lobe area** equals the remaining equatorial area. Thus each lobe encloses pi b^2, both lobes enclose 2 pi b^2, and the complement also has area 2 pi b^2.

The area equation is

[
2int_0^pi[1-sin(ksin tcos^2t)],dt=pi.
]

Its first regular root is

[
 oxed{k=2.63499709629253}.
]

The maximum lobe latitude is 58.11000154 degrees. At E, the two branch tangent vectors in local azimuth/latitude components are proportional to (2,k) and (2,-k), so the crossing is transverse. At W, both tangent vectors are proportional to (2,0), while their second-order latitude curvature has opposite sign, giving the intended tangential kiss. The curve is regular; its minimum parameter speed on the unit sphere is greater than 1.

The full material length is

[
L_A=bint_0^{2pi}sqrt{ eta'(t)^2+4cos^2 eta(t)},dt
=13.26913503960638,b.
]

For the minimum positive even multiple, the inner torus circumference contains two full Analemma circuits:

[
2pi(R-b)=2L_A,qquad
 oxed{R/b=5.22369686421446}.
]

The browser therefore derives the major radius from the tube/sphere radius. At the retained reference scale b=a=0.55:

The R/Q polar aperture adapter is a_RQ=0.78+0.20 tanh(f) radians. R is placed around +z and Q around -z, with opposite azimuths at a common meridional sweep. The aperture gain bounds the normalized crossbar-midpoint offset by sin(0.20)=0.19866933; the default harmonic pair's sampled maximum is about 0.0931 sphere radii. The azimuth/equation mapping remains an explicit representation choice, not a derived field equation.

### Rotational and epistemic limits

The browser computes the Analemma tangent, normal, and signed geodesic curvature analytically, transports its material point by numerical arc-length inversion, and keeps the existing inner selected-contact no-slip relation. The minimum even winding is now fixed at two full Analemma circuits per torus orbit; the elbow turns remain the LCM of that count and the R/Q sweep count.

Equal area is the chosen geometric balance condition. It has **not** been proven to globally minimize angular acceleration or jerk over all possible spherical figure-eight curves. A separate constrained smoothness optimization would be needed to establish that stronger claim. Equal-radius contact remains nonisolated, so the model still certifies only the nominated contact, not global no-slip across the full contact locus.

Run python tools/whirligig_rq/validate_equal_area_analemma.py for an independent standard-library calculation of the equal-area root, spherical length, E/W contact types, radius equality, and two-circuit gearing. **Date:** 2026-10-21. **Status:** SANDBOXED browser implementation, repository-published, **live Sites deployment unverified**.

## Direct user correction and provenance

The early records' **GrAnn / Great Annulum** was a mistaken term. The user intended an **Analemma**. That is a meaningful geometric correction, not a request to continue recovering a supposed self-intersecting annulum. Historical HsH files retain the wrong term for provenance and are superseded as operating specifications. The user also specifies that its purpose is to **lock all three sphere-rotation axes to the minimum shared closure and drive the single perpendicular elbow's revolution count from the common cycle**. The sphere is to roll on the **inner radial torus surface**.

For astronomical context only, the conventional solar analemma is the figure-eight locus of apparent solar declination versus equation of time at a fixed mean time of day. See the US Naval Observatory's [Equation of Time](https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/eqtime) explanation. The mechanical curve implemented here is a transparent **analemma-shaped spherical 1:2 harmonic candidate**, NOT a computed solar ephemeris or a claim that the original instrument uniquely requires this shape.

## Implemented 3D material contact curve

Let \(t\in[0,2\pi]\) run over one material Analemma circuit and \(A>0\) control its spherical aperture:

\[
G_A(t)=\frac{(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))}{\|(-1,\ A\sin t,\ A(\sin2t+0.27\sin t))\|}.
\]

This is a closed self-intersecting curve on the **unit sphere** with unequal lobes. \(G_A(0)=G_A(\pi)=(-1,0,0)\), but the two branches have distinct tangent directions. Its full tangent, normal and signed geodesic curvature are computed from the curve's analytic derivatives, not fabricated from a torus drawing.

The older reconstruction's circular carrier has been replaced in both world and sphere-body displays. The UI labels it **Analemma**. Internal legacy variable names and research filenames may retain `grann` for implementation compatibility, but should not be mistaken for the user's corrected terminology.

## Inner-torus rolling and minimum return

Let the torus major radius be \(R\), both sphere radius and torus tube radius be \(b=a\), and \(\psi\) parameterize the torus-centerline orbit. Define unit radial \(e_r\), orbital tangent \(e_\phi\), vertical \(e_z\).

The selected point on the **inner** torus wall is \(Donomphulon=(R-b)e_r\). The separately named **outer** radial point remains \(P_{ivot}=(R+b)e_r\). Sphere center \(C=Re_r\). The selected contact offset is \(-b e_r\).

No-slip at this nominated inner contact:
\[
\dot C+\omega\times(-b e_r)=0.
\]

For the material Analemma, let \(s\) be **actual spherical arc length**, \(g=G_A(s)\), \(t=dg/ds\), \(h=g\times t\), and \(\kappa_g\) be signed geodesic curvature. The SO(3) lock is

\[
\mathcal Q(\psi)=[-e_r,\ e_\phi,\ -e_z]\,[g,t,h]^T,\qquad
\frac{ds}{d\psi}=\frac{R}{b}-1.
\]

This produces
\[
\boxed{\frac{\omega}{\dot\psi}=\frac{R}{b}e_z+
\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right)\kappa_g(s)e_r}.
\]

The required \(+z\) rolling spin now has the **same sign as orbital travel**, unlike the earlier incorrect outer-wall model. The radial spin component rotates through **x and y** as the sphere goes around the torus, so all three spatial axes participate. This is mathematically an **inner selected-contact** constraint, not global no-slip over the nonisolated \(b=a\) contact locus.

Let \(L_G(A)\) be the true spherical arclength of one material Analemma. One torus orbit moves through \(2\pi(R/b-1)\) of material arc length. The model searches for the **smallest positive even** winding count \(n\), subject to its openly stated admissible aperture \(0<A\le2\), satisfying

\[
n L_G(A)=2\pi\left(\frac{R}{b}-1\right).
\]

With \(R=1.65\), \(b=0.55\), the minimum is \(n=2\), numerical \(A\approx0.935206924\), and \(L_G\approx2\pi\). This is *minimal within this declared family and bounded aperture*, not a universal minimum across all possible analemmas.

The R/Q moving sweep plane still intersects each source curve separately. The one and only perpendicular elbow is phase-locked to \(\operatorname{lcm}(n,m)\), where \(m\) is the chosen integer R/Q sweep count per torus orbit. No extra projector and no independent elbow-turn slider.

### Numerical transport detail

The current browser integrates Analemma arclength with composite Simpson quadrature, inverts its monotone \(s(t)\) table with a bracket and a local Newton/Simpson refinement, and advances the material track by actual arc length. This avoids piecewise-linear angular-velocity kinks in the first implementation.

Executed independent tests at finite-difference steps \(0.012, 0.006, 0.003, 0.0015, 0.00075\) orbital radians gave maximum selected-contact slip discrepancies approximately \(0.03109, 0.00843, 0.00215, 0.000542, 0.000136\), respectively. These converge close to the expected \(O(h^2)\), rather than only repeating the analytic identity used in the constructor. Full orientation closure residual about \(1.1\times10^{-15}\), and length/cycle return residual about \(4.6\times10^{-13}\).

## Equation-to-curve issue and remedy

The previous source mapping squeezed both R and Q into narrow hemisphere bands:

```text
old polar aperture: 0.48 + 0.20 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
current aperture:   0.78 + 0.58 tanh(display_gain * f(lambda))
```

These are explicit geometric *representation choices*, not newly derived equation identities. Angles remain between \(0.20\) and \(1.36\) radians, keeping the chosen half-sphere assignment. The more expressive mapping allows changing source equations to produce visibly different connector and torus-wall traces.

A fourth browser panel now compares **the previous and current actual torus-wall intersection curves at the same orbital parameters**, and displays RMS and maximum world-distance change in model units and tube-radius percentage. The previous trace appears dimly behind the current trace, both in the same torus coordinate system. Nothing is auto-reselected for visual beauty.

**Expected exact duplicates:** distinct underlying equations can define the same sampled scalar representative (e.g. \(\cos\lambda\) for both an ideal spin-precession expectation and a selected circular-orbit coordinate). If selected in the same input port under identical settings, they should produce the same mapped trace. The comparison panel explicitly calls out zero difference. **The instrument still does not establish physical equivalence** of two theories.

## Output continuity, no curation

The torus trace is defined by the first forward intersection of the **single elbow ray** with the implicit torus surface. Geometrically valid wall intersections do not imply continuity of the selected-first-hit branch. The application now reports counts of adjacent-step displacements greater than \(0.20b\) and the largest step, without smoothing or deleting events. In one default 1,401-point run, 30 adjacent steps exceeded \(0.11\) model units and the largest step was about \(0.347\). These are *discontinuity candidates*; determining whether they are true root-branch transitions or very rapid continuous motion requires an additional adaptive-step/root-continuation audit.

**Unresolved:** a mathematical derivative mapping \(Q\text{ wrt }R\), complete arbitrary-field invertibility, real-browser visual acceptance, live-site deployment, and global no-slip at \(b=a\). The spherical analemma is one explicit model of the user-intended track, not a claim of recovered solar-ephemeris mechanics.

- [Website integration instructions](SITES_INTEGRATION.md)

## 2026-11-02 CURRENT: equal-area Analemma, equatorial E/W contacts, polar N/S inputs

This section supersedes the 2026-10-21 material-curve formula above and the earlier 2026-10-17 east/west R/Q placement. The canonical browser file remains [index.html](index.html).

### Confirmed geometry and terminology

- **R** is a closed equation curve around the **north pole**, wholly in the northern hemisphere.
- **Q** is a closed equation curve around the **south pole**, wholly in the southern hemisphere.
- The Analemma is a separate closed spherical figure-eight. Its transverse self-crossing is at the **east equatorial pole** E=(1,0,0); its distinct self-tangential kiss is at the antipodal **west equatorial pole** W=(-1,0,0).
- The northern lobe winds around the north pole; the southern lobe winds around the south pole.
- One Analemma circuit means the complete two-lobed closed curve. The inner torus circumference is an even multiple of that complete length.
- Sphere radius equals torus tube minor radius: b=a, so the sphere great-circle circumference equals the tube cross-section circumference.

The historical source gives the self-crossing and antipodal self-tangency relationship; the E/W versus N/S placement and the equal-area condition above are the user's later explicit geometric refinements.

### Equal-area curve family and solved shape

On the unit sphere, define

[
 eta(t)=ksin tcos^2t,qquad phi(t)=2t,
]

[
G(t)= igl(cos etacosphi,;cos etasinphi,;sin eta igr),quad 0le t<2pi.
]

The northern lobe is 0<t<pi; the southern lobe is pi<t<2pi. The equal-area interpretation used here is that the **combined two-lobe area** equals the remaining equatorial area. Thus each lobe encloses pi b^2, both lobes enclose 2 pi b^2, and the complement also has area 2 pi b^2.

The area equation is

[
2int_0^pi[1-sin(ksin tcos^2t)],dt=pi.
]

Its first regular root is

[
 oxed{k=2.63499709629253}.
]

The maximum lobe latitude is 58.11000154 degrees. At E, the two branch tangent vectors in local azimuth/latitude components are proportional to (2,k) and (2,-k), so the crossing is transverse. At W, both tangent vectors are proportional to (2,0), while their second-order latitude curvature has opposite sign, giving the intended tangential kiss. The curve is regular; its minimum parameter speed on the unit sphere is greater than 1.

### Length and gearing

The full material length is

[
L_A=bint_0^{2pi}sqrt{ eta'(t)^2+4cos^2 eta(t)},dt
=13.26913503960638,b.
]

For the minimum positive even multiple, the inner torus circumference contains two full Analemma circuits:

[
2pi(R-b)=2L_A,qquad
 oxed{R/b=5.22369686421446}.
]

The browser therefore derives the major radius from the tube/sphere radius. At the retained reference scale b=a=0.55:

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---:|
| Sphere and tube radius | 0.55 |
| Sphere great-circle / tube cross-section circumference | 3.45575191895 |
| Full physical Analemma length | 7.29802427178 |
| Torus major radius R | 2.87303327532 |
| Inner torus circumference | 14.59604854357 |
| Inner circumference / full Analemma length | 2 exactly, within numerical tolerance |

Changing the scale control changes a=b and derives R proportionally, preserving the equal circumferences and two-circuit gear ratio. The old independent major-radius slider is removed because it allowed the gear constraint to be broken.

### R/Q aperture and W_obble centering

The R/Q polar aperture adapter is a_RQ=0.78+0.20 tanh(f) radians. R is placed around +z and Q around -z, with opposite azimuths at a common meridional sweep. The aperture gain bounds the normalized crossbar-midpoint offset by sin(0.20)=0.19866933; the default harmonic pair's sampled maximum is about 0.0931 sphere radii. The azimuth/equation mapping remains an explicit representation choice, not a derived field equation.

### Rotational and epistemic limits

The browser computes the Analemma tangent, normal, and signed geodesic curvature analytically, transports its material point by numerical arc-length inversion, and keeps the existing inner selected-contact no-slip relation. The minimum even winding is now fixed at two full Analemma circuits per torus orbit; the elbow turns remain the LCM of that count and the R/Q sweep count.

Equal area is the chosen geometric balance condition. It has **not** been proven to globally minimize angular acceleration or jerk over all possible spherical figure-eight curves. A separate constrained smoothness optimization would be needed to establish that stronger claim. Equal-radius contact remains nonisolated, so the model still certifies only the nominated contact, not global no-slip across the full contact locus.

### Reproducible calculation

Run python tools/whirligig_rq/validate_equal_area_analemma.py for an independent standard-library calculation of the equal-area root, spherical length, E/W contact types, radius equality, and two-circuit gearing. This is numerical verification of the declared curve family, not proof that the family is uniquely implied by the historical prose.
